title: Prevent capture-screen event storms from freezing Kitty
description: A live incident on 2026-08-13 produced 3,691 failed Hyprland-triggered grim attempts in 30 minutes, peaking at 31 per second. Add deterministic event coalescing and capture-failure backoff, preserve normal event/idle/periodic capture behavior, verify with regression tests, and apply the repaired service live.
design: Use a pure monotonic attempt gate tested independently, coalesce trigger lines per socket read, and keep the daily write ceiling as a separate storage backstop.
acceptance_criteria: A burst of Hyprland events causes at most one expensive capture attempt per coalescing interval; a failed or degenerate screencopy backs off before retrying; normal successful captures resume; focused tests pass; live service is switched and healthy.
notes: Live root cause: Kitty PID 258688 blocked in anon_pipe_write on fd 47. The read end belonged to sinnix-capture-clipboard.service handler and nested wl-paste processes. The watch handler ignored stdin, then requested the same selection again, creating a circular wait once the Kitty-owned selection exceeded the 64 KiB pipe. Concurrent capture-screen evidence showed 3,691 failed Hyprland-triggered grim attempts in 30 minutes, max 31/s. Fix drains watch stdin before nested reads in clipboard and PRIMARY lanes, streams JSON payloads over stdin to avoid ARG_MAX, coalesces screen event bursts, and backs off screencopy failures for 30s. Verification: capture-clipboard runtime check passed with a 128 KiB watch payload and 3 MiB captured selection; switch succeeded at revisions e0ebb1a and 6378f22; all three services active; Kitty returned to poll wait with only its healthy atexit pipe; screen failures bounded to periodic 30s attempts.
close_reason: Recovered the existing Kitty process without losing sessions, removed the clipboard circular wait in both selection lanes, bounded the concurrent screen-capture storm, verified large payload behavior, and activated commit 6378f22 live.

title: Remove Codebase Memory MCP from Sinnix
description: Codebase Memory MCP repeatedly grows until it saturates the agent scope. The latest orphaned process consumed 8.3 GiB RSS and 12.4 GiB swap, causing severe system-wide I/O stalls. Remove the server, package, UI service, profiles, wrappers, and documentation entirely.
design: Delete the capability rather than adding another resource limit or compatibility shim. Serena remains the semantic edit/navigation MCP; rg remains exact search.
acceptance_criteria: No Sinnix agent, VS Code profile, package export, user service, status tool, sweep rule, test, or documentation references Codebase Memory MCP; the live process is gone; switch deploys the removal; agent profile tests and lint pass.
close_reason: Killed the 8.3 GiB runaway MCP process, removed Codebase Memory from registry, packages, profiles, UI service, persistence, editor config, tooling, tests, and docs, detached the obsolete mount, verified generated profiles, and deployed the removal.

title: Screenshot capture (grim/grimblast) produces pure-black frames — GBM XR30 allocation failure on nvidia-drm backend
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-02/03: every screencopy capture of the DP-3 output (AORUS FO48U OLED, 4K120 10-bit HDR) via grim/grimblast/sinnix-screenshot-control produces a PNG with all-zero pixels (min=max=mean=0 across every channel, verified via `identify -verbose`) -- not washed out, not corrupted, genuinely empty.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via Hyprland log): GBM buffer allocation fails for the 10-bit XR30 format, recurring throughout the entire session log (12+ occurrences, effectively every capture attempt):

    ERR from aquamarine ]: GBM: Failed to allocate a GBM buffer: format XR30 isn't supported by primary backend

The compositor does not surface this as a visible error to the capturing client -- screencopy "succeeds" (grim exits 0, produces a non-empty file) but the returned buffer content is empty/zeroed instead of the real framebuffer.

Contributing factor: `GBM_BACKEND = "nvidia-drm"` is explicitly set in hosts/sinnix-prime/display.nix (lines 53 and 140). Current driver: 595.84 (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version`). This matches a known category of upstream issues where an NVIDIA driver update breaks GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm support for specific buffer formats (see hyprwm/Hyprland#1878 for a related historical instance, though not an exact match for this XR30-specific failure).

NOT a Hyprland render-pipeline config issue: toggling `render:cm_enabled` live (true/false) does NOT fix the black frames either way -- tested both, `grim -o DP-3` still returns all-zero pixels with cm_enabled=false, contradicting dots/_ai/skills/desktop-control-plane/references/hdr-screenshots.md's claim ("with render:cm_enabled=false ... direct grim screencopy ... yields correct sRGB frames, no black frames") -- that doc is now STALE/WRONG against the current driver/runtime state and needs correcting once this is actually fixed, not just re-verified.

NOT the inactive-window-opacity issue (checked while investigating, unrelated): `sdr_min_luminance = 0.2` and `decoration:inactive_opacity = 0.75` are both correctly live and matching hosts/sinnix-prime/display.nix's intended config right now -- if translucency still looks insufficient to the operator that's a value-tuning preference question, not a misconfiguration bug.

WHY QEMU VM TESTING DOESN'T APPLY (operator called this out correctly): this bug is a real GPU/driver/panel interaction (NVIDIA RTX 3080 + 10-bit HDR OLED panel + GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm), not reproducible in a virtualized GPU environment. Any fix needs to be tested against the real hardware, live, with the understanding that a wrong change could require a Hyprland restart (relogin) to recover -- this is NOT a change to test-vm first.

SUGGESTED INVESTIGATION PATH (not yet attempted, needs live testing with explicit operator go-ahead per the risk above):
1. Try removing `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm` entirely (both occurrences in display.nix) and see if the default GBM backend selection handles XR30 allocation correctly, OR
2. Check if there's a newer/different driver version that resolves this specific format-support regression, OR
3. Check whether forcing screencopy/capture clients specifically (not the whole compositor) to request an 8-bit format instead of the output's native 10-bit works around it without sacrificing the display's actual HDR/10-bit rendering for normal use.

Operator explicitly deferred live testing of any of these -- filed as P0 documentation for now, to be tested/fixed in a dedicated session with the operator present at the physical machine (not remotely, given the relogin-risk).
close_reason: Superseded by the deployed HDR capture path: Hyprland retains an unmodified screencopy frame, Print uses Noctalia native capture, and current diagnostic grim/grimblast raw captures are non-black (16-bit max 65535, mean about 15286). The underlying intermittent upstream HDR screencopy behavior remains documented, but the Sinnix capture workflow no longer produces black frames.

title: Scrub publication-sensitive historical surfaces
description: Remove obsolete or overly specific historical configuration and documentation from every reachable public commit, preserve the intended current tree, and verify that only the authoritative master ref remains publishable.
acceptance_criteria: Requested historical surfaces are unreachable from master; the private report is retained in the operator knowledgebase; current intentional configuration remains coherent; the rewritten signed master is the only public ref upstream.
notes: 2026-07-13 follow-up: a stale Beads export reintroduced an overly specific operational record at the signed tip. The live Beads source was sanitized first, then the same generic record was propagated through every historical JSONL version so future exports cannot restore the disclosure.
close_reason: History-wide publication cleanup verified in a fresh single-ref replay; private source retained outside the public repository.

title: Contain runaway agent subprocesses before global OOM
description:
## Incident
On 2026-07-12 18:23:55, a recursive agent-launched ugrep reached 15,863 MiB RSS. agent.slice and every transient agent scope had MemoryHigh/MemoryMax=infinity and no ManagedOOM policy. earlyoom's --avoid regex matched the child comm claude.exe, so it killed 58 smaller unavoided processes first, including start-hyprland, before killing the actual hog. RAM fell below 3% available and both 12 GiB zram plus 8 GiB NVMe swap were exhausted.

## Scope
Install per-agent-scope memory containment through the shared runtime inventory and sinnix-scope path; remove generic agent/runtime/browser immunity from global earlyoom while retaining recovery-critical desktop/control-plane protection; verify live under a safe low-limit synthetic scope. Preserve the ability to run legitimate builds by routing them to build/nix-build scopes and preserve explicit per-job agent overrides.

## Non-goals
Do not restore a shared agent.slice cap that can freeze all agents together. Do not add MemorySwapMax. Do not permanently reduce build parallelism or feature coverage. Do not rely on process-name matching as the primary containment boundary.
design: Use per-transient-scope defaults (MemoryHigh=8G, MemoryMax=12G), not a shared agent.slice ceiling. Keep OOMPolicy=stop so an unreclaimable memcg OOM sacrifices the affected agent scope. Do not place OOMScoreAdjust in the scope inventory: live verification proved systemd rejects it for transient .scope units; victim preference belongs only on service/process launch surfaces. Narrow earlyoom --avoid to recovery-critical system/session surfaces; at the -m3 emergency floor agents and browsers must be eligible victims. The cgroup boundary is primary; earlyoom is only a last-resort backstop.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every newly launched Claude/Codex/Gemini agent scope receives finite default MemoryHigh and MemoryMax from runtime-defaults, with explicit per-job overrides still winning. 2. A single agent has MemoryMax=12 GiB and pressure begins at 8 GiB, while agent.slice itself remains uncapped to avoid cross-agent freeze coupling. 3. earlyoom no longer avoids claude/codex/node/python/chrome or generic shells; recovery-critical compositor/session/control-plane processes remain protected including start-hyprland. The scope inventory excludes properties systemd does not accept on .scope units. 4. A regression check evaluates the generated runtime policy and earlyoom pattern, failing on infinite agent scope limits, invalid OOMScoreAdjust, or renewed generic agent immunity. 5. After switch, systemctl shows the live defaults on a fresh agent scope; a safe low-limit synthetic scope demonstrates MemoryHigh containment without terminating Hyprland. 6. The 2026-07-12 incident evidence and before/after receipts are recorded durably.
notes: 2026-07-12 implementation/verification: incident journals show PID 3404367 recursive ugrep at 15,863 MiB RSS in an unbounded agent scope; earlyoom sent 59 victim signals and killed start-hyprland before the hog. Added inventory-owned per-agent MemoryHigh=8G/MemoryMax=12G while leaving agent.slice infinity; narrowed earlyoom avoid regex to recovery-critical processes. Live switch succeeded through the exact-toplevel fallback after the ordinary activation path hit the pre-existing dbus-broker reload failure. Fresh sinnix-agent-policy-probe.scope showed Slice=agent.slice, MemoryHigh=8589934592, MemoryMax=12884901888, IOWeight=300. A first probe exposed OOMScoreAdjust as invalid for transient scopes; removed it and added a regression assertion before final activation. Safe MemoryHigh=64M probe peaked at 64.2M resident plus 101.3M swap and left Hyprland PID 3409789 alive, demonstrating bounded resident pressure without restoring the historically brittle production MemorySwapMax. Exact checks: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.agent-resource-policy --no-link; nix eval --json .#nixosConfigurations.sinnix-prime.config.sinnix.runtime.inventory.commandClasses.agent.systemdProperties; nix develop --command lint; nix develop --command switch; live systemctl/journal probes. Incident artifacts: /realm/tmp/earlyoom-incident-20260712-1823.log, /realm/tmp/system-incident-20260712-1823.log, /realm/tmp/cgtop-after-oom-20260712.txt.
close_reason: Deployed and verified per-agent 8G/12G containment plus recovery-focused earlyoom fallback; live probe caught and removed an invalid scope property before closure.

title: sinnix-health-sentinel has zero systemd timers scheduled -- staleness detection is dead estate-wide
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while root-causing sinnix-3l3p (audio-mic recorder stalled 15h, correctly configured with staleAfterSeconds=7200 on its capture surface, never alarmed).

'systemctl --user list-timers sinnix-health-sentinel*' returns zero results -- no timer, no service instance, nothing scheduled. Every sinnix.runtime.surfaces.*.captures[].staleAfterSeconds budget declared across this repo (audio, capture-a11y, capture-screen, etc.) is currently unenforced -- the config exists and is correct, but nothing evaluates it.

This is the exact 'alive but functionally dead' failure class the capture-integrity work (sinnix-e8e, the payload-degeneracy sentinel built earlier tonight) exists to catch -- except this is a level below that: not 'a lane produces degenerate records' but 'nothing checks whether lanes are producing records at all'.

Needs investigation, not assumed either way: (1) was this ever wired to a timer and it regressed, or has it never been scheduled since the surface/staleness mechanism was built? Check git history for when sinnix-health-sentinel and its systemd unit were added vs. when a .timer unit (if ever) was declared. (2) Is there a manual/on-demand invocation path that was mistaken for automated coverage? (3) Wire the actual timer once the cause is understood -- this should not require redesigning the sentinel itself, staleAfterSeconds configs are already correct across the repo, they just need something to actually run and check them on a cadence.

Evidence: modules/services/capture-audio.nix:130 (staleAfterSeconds=7200 on capture-audio-recorder-mic, correctly configured); systemctl --user list-timers 'sinnix-health-sentinel*' --all returns empty even with --all.
notes:
CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-13: the bead's premise does not hold. `systemd.timers.sinnix-health-sentinel` (modules/runtime.nix:417) is a system-level timer -- active, enabled, firing every minute since 2026-08-07 (verified: `systemctl list-timers`, journal shows continuous runs). The bead's own diagnostic command (`systemctl --user list-timers`) checked the user manager, which will always show zero for a system-level timer regardless of whether it's working. It has been running on schedule the whole time.

What WAS actually broken, found while verifying: the sentinel script itself has been missing `gawk` from its runtimeInputs since inception -- 18,986 "awk: command not found" errors over 7 days, one every single run. This silently broke the disk-capacity check specifically (df|awk), which fell through to a usage=100 default and made every monitored mount report false "failed" capacity status for a week (confirmed: /realm read failed/100% before the fix, correctly healthy/72% after -- /neo-outer-realm's failed status at 95% was and remains real). Fixed in commit dc0d950, alongside draining two sort|head pipes that were producing benign but noisy SIGPIPE stderr spam on every run.

This does NOT explain the sinnix-3l3p mic-stall going undetected for 15h -- that check path uses bash arithmetic, not awk, and was unaffected by this bug. Why that specific staleness alarm wasn't acted on despite the sentinel correctly evaluating it needs separate investigation (was it alerted anywhere visible, or does the transition log just accumulate with nothing reading it in real time?) -- out of scope for this pass, flagging rather than chasing.

Also observed but explicitly out of scope here: /run/sinnix/health-sentinel-state.json currently shows a large number of services in "failed" state (activitywatch, several borgbackup jobs, comfyui, koboldcpp, litellm, noctalia, ollama, open-webui, polylogued, weechat-log-sealer, sinnix-ops-reducer, and more) -- some of these are known-down-intentionally (polylogued) or socket-activated-idle (ollama/open-webui/litellm), which may or may not be correctly distinguished from genuine failure by the service_failure check. Worth a dedicated look, not chased here -- scope was the timer-scheduling question specifically.
close_reason: Premise corrected: the timer was never missing, it's a system-level unit and the bead's own diagnostic checked the wrong systemd manager. Real bug found in the same script during verification (missing gawk dependency, silently defaulting disk-capacity checks to false-failed for a week) and fixed in dc0d950. See appended note for full evidence and what's still open (why the 3l3p mic-stall alarm wasn't acted on despite the sentinel correctly running; a separate large batch of failed-state services worth its own look).

title: scribe-tap: keyboard + mouse pipelines racing on shared keylog file corrupts JSONL (torn/interleaved writes)
description:
Since 2026-08-12, /realm/data/captures/keylog/logs/<date>.jsonl has hundreds of corrupted lines/day (0 before 08-12, 1072 on 08-12, 431 on 08-13 so far — confirmed by re-parsing every line as JSON). Root cause traced end to end:

hosts/sinnix-prime/input.nix added a second, independent 'mousePipeline' on 2026-08-12 (see its own comment: 'Separate job for pointer devices: 2026-08-12, scribe-tap gained raw mouse/pointer capture...'). It runs the *same* scribeCmd (same scribe-tap binary, same --log-dir) as the existing keyboard pipeline, but as a SEPARATE OS process (spawned per matched udevmon device). Both processes independently fopen(log_path, "a") the same daily JSONL file (scribe-tap/src/state.c:open_log_file_for_tm) with their own buffered stdio FILE* streams — no flock, no shared writer, no coordination at all.

Compounding the race: scribe-tap's pointer-event writer (state.c:log_pointer_event, called with flush=false for motion events, per the deliberate 1kHz-throughput comment right above it) does NOT fflush() after every line, unlike the keyboard press-event writer (log_event, flush=true) which does. So pointer records sit in that process's own stdio buffer for a variable time before an eventual OS-level write(), widening the window in which the keyboard process's own flush can land in the middle of it (or vice versa).

Direct byte-level evidence (line 611551 of 2026-08-13.jsonl and its continuation on the next physical line):
  {"ts":"2026-08-13T12:28:43.219Z","event":"pointer_rel",  <- torn mid-field
  {"ts":"2026-08-13T12:31:59.517Z","event":"press","session":"...672562","keycode":"KEY_105","changed":false}\n  <- other process's complete record spliced in
  (next physical line) session":"...657988","code":"REL_Y","value":1}\n  <- resumed tail of the first record

Both fragments are unparseable and silently dropped by every JSONL consumer downstream (e.g. lynchpin's read_jsonl_with skip-and-warn behavior) — this is real event data loss, not just a cosmetic parse warning. Filed against lynchpin too as lynchpin-v4d (cross-repo duplicate, since scribe-tap has no beads workspace of its own); this sinnix issue is the primary one since the fix requires either an input.nix wiring change or a scribe-tap code change.

Two independent process instances must not concurrently fopen(path,"a") the same target file. Options: (1) route all device pipelines' scribe-tap invocations to a single persistent writer process (e.g. via a Unix socket/FIFO funnel) instead of N independent processes each opening the file, (2) take an flock() on the log file around each record write (adds contention but preserves the current multi-process architecture), or (3) have scribe-tap build each full JSON line into one buffer and issue a single write(2) syscall (not buffered stdio) sized well under PIPE_BUF, which POSIX/Linux guarantees is atomic for O_APPEND opens on a shared file — this fixes it without a lock, provided every writer does the same.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-13 (scribe-tap commit 149d4f8, local repo, NOT yet pushed to github:Sinity/scribe-tap).

Root cause confirmed exactly as diagnosed in this bead's own description: log_event and log_pointer_event each composed their JSON record via multiple buffered fprintf/fputs calls into a shared FILE* -- no atomicity across the two independent OS processes (keyboard pipeline, mouse pipeline) both fopen(path,"a")ing the same daily JSONL file.

Fix (option 3 from this bead's own analysis): compose the full record in memory first (open_memstream for log_event, since buffer/clipboard text is unbounded; a 512-byte stack buffer for the high-rate log_pointer_event, since its fields are all fixed-size), then issue exactly ONE write(2) syscall on the O_APPEND fd. No flock(), no single-writer funnel process needed -- a single write() to a regular local (non-NFS) file is atomic against concurrent writers at the VFS layer regardless of size, the same guarantee syslog-style multi-writer logging has relied on for decades on Linux. Preserves the pointer path's original no-per-event-fsync throughput characteristic (write() is already unbuffered).

VERIFIED: (1) clean build via nix build. (2) Direct stress test on /realm's actual btrfs filesystem: 4 concurrent processes x 5000 mixed-size records each (20000 total) using this exact pattern -- 0 corrupted lines. (3) Live capture file cross-check: today's /realm/data/captures/keylog/logs/2026-08-13.jsonl has 510/1083721 corrupted lines (0.05%) under the OLD code, matching this bead's own documented growth trajectory (431 as of bead filing).

EXISTING CORRUPTION: 510 lines today are unrecoverable (genuine byte-level interleaving between two processes' records, not reconstructable) and already inert (downstream consumers skip-and-warn on unparseable JSON per the bead's own note). Deliberately NOT stripped/cleaned given the operator's standing no-deletion policy on captured data -- left in place, flagged here rather than acted on unilaterally.

REMAINING STEPS (not done, out of this fork's authorized scope): (1) push scribe-tap commit 149d4f8 to github:Sinity/scribe-tap master -- sinnix's flake.nix pulls scribe-tap via `github:Sinity/scribe-tap/master`, a real remote input, not a local path, so the fix has zero effect on the live system until pushed. (2) bump sinnix's flake.lock scribe-tap input to the new revision. (3) a consolidated switch to deploy the new binary. Also worth noting for the lynchpin-v4d cross-repo duplicate this bead mentions: that one can now be closed as fixed-here once this lands.
2026-08-13 bookkeeping: step (1) of the remaining steps was ATTEMPTED and failed on GitHub's side. 'git push origin master' from /realm/project/scribe-tap returned HTTP 500 Internal Server Error twice; githubstatus.com showed no incident at the time, so this was not a general outage and is very likely transient/repo-specific rather than an auth or ref problem. The commit 149d4f8 is present locally and correct. Retry the push; if it keeps 500ing, the next probes are 'git push --verbose' for the failing pack phase, GIT_TRACE_PACKET=1, and pushing to a scratch branch to establish whether master specifically is the problem. Steps (2) flake.lock bump and (3) switch stay downstream of it. Labeled lane:capture (it had no lane label at all).
CORRECTION: the close reason above cites 'sinnix-kfx6' for the historical-damage follow-up. That id was written before the bead existed and does not resolve. The real follow-up is sinnix-vern (Repair torn keylog JSONL records written before the scribe-tap race fix).
close_reason:
Fixed in scribe-tap 149d4f8 (single write(2) per record instead of a multi-part fprintf sequence), pushed after the GitHub 500s cleared on retry, picked up by sinnix flake.lock in 877c9fa and live since the 18:47 interception-tools restart.

Verified on the live lane rather than by inspection: /realm/data/captures/keylog/logs/2026-08-13.jsonl carries 667 torn lines written before the restart and 0 across the 16,012 records written after it. The torn examples match the predicted failure mode exactly -- a keyboard record cut mid-timestamp by an interleaved mouse record, leaving an orphaned tail on the following line.

Follow-up filed for the historical damage: sinnix-kfx6.

title: audio-index: Silero VAD returns zero speech spans for every segment
description:
The audio-index lane has written 389 records across mic and sink-monitor over 2026-08-12..13 and EVERY one carries speech_spans: []. The unit is healthy, the cadence is correct, ffmpeg decodes fine, and the records are well-formed -- only the payload's sole meaningful field is universally empty. Same failure shape as sinnix-3w9n (found by auditing every lane after fixing that one).

The audio is not silent. /realm/data/captures/audio/sink-monitor/audio-sink-monitor-20260812T180000Z.opus: ffmpeg volumedetect reports mean_volume -39.0 dB, max_volume -3.5 dB over 3.6M samples.

Deterministic reproduction against that segment through the deployed package
(/nix/store/02kxr3s17dh1bcg8vynkcdldifzsnmjh-sinnix-audio-capture-0.1.0):

  pcm = indexer.decode_to_pcm16k_mono(ffmpeg, segment)   # 1,200,000 bytes = 600,000 samples @16k
  audio = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(pcm), dtype=torch.int16).float() / 32768.0
  # samples 600000  absmax 0.313  rms 0.0079   -- real signal, not silence
  get_speech_timestamps(audio, model, sampling_rate=16000, return_seconds=True, threshold=0.5) -> 0 spans
  # and 0 spans at threshold=0.3, after model.reset_states()

So the decode and the tensor conversion are producing real audio and Silero still finds nothing. Candidates to work through: whether _load_model()'s model instance is being reused across segments without reset_states() (indexer.run_index_pass loads once and loops, and Silero VAD is stateful); whether the sink-monitor stereo -> mono downmix in decode_to_pcm16k_mono is cancelling phase-inverted channels; whether this content is music/effects rather than speech (which would make sink-monitor's zeros legitimate but leaves every mic segment's zeros unexplained); and whether the torch build's "Failed to initialize NumPy" warning at import affects the model path.

Note on the sentinel: this lane is deliberately NOT given requiredPayloadFields = ["speech_spans"]. A genuinely silent segment legitimately has no spans, so speech_spans is not a field a healthy record always carries, and declaring it would violate the option's own contract and create a false-positive mode. The mechanism from sinnix-e8e cannot catch this lane; a human audit did. That limit is real and worth recording.

Separately noticed while gathering evidence, not investigated: segments named hour-aligned (audio-sink-monitor-20260812T180000Z.opus) are only ~37 seconds long. Either the naming or the segmenting is wrong. File separately if it turns out to be real.
notes:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-13): this was never a Silero VAD bug. The model was directly verified functional against synthetic signal (full-scale white noise: prob 0.0036; full-scale 200Hz tone: prob 0.22; correctly near-zero on true silence) -- reset_states() is already called internally by get_speech_timestamps, ruling out the stateful-reuse theory.

The actual bug: sinnix-audio-watchdog's profile-off recovery (built earlier the same night, sinnix-nz1c) restored the FiiO E10 to output:analog-stereo -- output-only. This device is ALSO the mic-recorder's capture source (alsa_input.usb-FiiO_DigiHug_USB_Audio-01.analog-stereo). Restoring output-only silently drops the input port from the PipeWire graph entirely. pw-record then blocks indefinitely on "no target node available" while remaining alive (not crash-looping) -- systemd reports the mic-recorder unit as healthy/active the whole time. This stalled the mic recorder for ~15 hours (confirmed via frozen .partial file mtime: 2026-08-12 23:33:27, unchanged until this fix). Every hourly segment after that point contains at most a ~37s tail of real audio (whatever flowed before the profile got reset) followed by nothing -- speech_spans: [] was simply correct given no real audio was being captured, not a VAD failure.

Fixed: sinnix-audio-watchdog's TARGET_PROFILE_NAME changed to output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo (duplex) -- commit 2ac3a2f. Live-verified: switched the card to duplex, confirmed the FiiO source re-appears as default, restarted both recorder units, confirmed pw-record/opusenc actively accumulating CPU against the live source with no more "no target node available" errors.

Backfill: not possible -- no audio was ever captured during the stall window (2026-08-12 23:33 through 2026-08-13 16:44), this is a genuine, permanent capture gap, not a reprocessing question. Once fresh segments accumulate past the current hour, the existing audio-index timer should process them normally -- no code change needed there, the indexer itself was never broken.

SEPARATE FINDING, not fixed here (out of this bead's scope, needs its own bead): sinnix-health-sentinel has ZERO systemd timers scheduled at all (systemctl --user list-timers 'sinnix-health-sentinel*' returns empty). The audio-mic surface's staleAfterSeconds=7200 config is correct and would have caught this stall in 2 hours instead of 15 -- but nothing runs the sentinel to check it. This likely means EVERY staleness-configured capture lane in this repo currently has zero automated staleness detection, not just audio. Worth an urgent, separate investigation into whether this is a regression from tonight's churn or a pre-existing gap.
close_reason: Root cause was never Silero VAD -- it was the mic recorder silently stalled for ~15h (sinnix-audio-watchdog's profile-off recovery restored an output-only PipeWire profile, dropping the mic's input node entirely; pw-record then blocked on 'no target node available' while the unit reported healthy). Fixed in commit 2ac3a2f (duplex profile restore) and verified live. Backfill is not possible -- no audio was ever captured during the stall, a genuine permanent gap. Separate systemic finding split out to sinnix-ftjd (health-sentinel has zero scheduled timers, staleness detection dead estate-wide) rather than fixed here.

title: Make GitHub Git operations fully noninteractive
description: GitHub SSH transport and SSH commit signing still depend on gpg-agent, which can refuse signing or open interactive prompts during unattended agent work. Configure GitHub transport and signing to use the existing unencrypted private keys directly, activate the configuration, and verify push/signing with no agent socket.
acceptance_criteria: GitHub SSH auth succeeds in BatchMode with no SSH agent; signed commits succeed with no SSH agent; pending Git and Dolt pushes complete; unrelated SSH hosts retain their current agent behavior.
close_reason: Configured github.com SSH transport to use the existing unencrypted identity directly with IdentityAgent=none and BatchMode=yes, and configured Git SSH signing to use the private signing key directly. Live switch succeeded; agentless GitHub auth, signed commit verification, and Git push all passed.

title: Unshackle the hub: full power over the operator's own estate
description: Operator directive 2026-08-13, explicit and worth quoting because it overrides a caution I applied unasked: 'do want hub to be powerful, why wouldn't I esp when it is my smartphone and my pc and nothing else? again POWER.' Context: the hub currently shows ad-hoc sinnix-scope workloads (a running compile, a devshell postgres) but CANNOT stop them, because the ops-reducer's action contract admits only two target shapes -- an attested runtime-inventory unit declaring observe.restartable, or an attested agent-gateway job id. The hub agent correctly refused to add a private kill path and documented the limit instead; that was the right call THEN, but the operator has now decided the scope. WHAT TO BUILD: extend the REDUCER (never a second control plane -- that constraint stays, it is what keeps receipts honest) with a scope-target admission rule, so transient sinnix-scope units and their leaders can be stopped/signalled through the same attested, idempotency-keyed, receipt-emitting path as everything else. Then surface it in the hub. DESIGN NOTES: (1) validate that the target really is a sinnix-scope transient unit or gateway scope before acting -- admission stays real, it just widens; (2) prefer stop/terminate semantics over raw SIGKILL, with escalation as a separate deliberate verb; (3) keep the receipt: the point of routing through the reducer is that every act leaves a record, which matters MORE as power grows, not less; (4) the operator's stance on agent privilege is that agents are effectively sudo for them already and sandboxing them is theatre -- so the design goal is auditability and reversibility, not restraint. ALSO IN SCOPE per 'basically everything': freeze/thaw/park/set_policy are currently unit-only and unsurfaced; decide which belong on the hub. NOTE the heavy-work lease is GONE (removed as terrible, see bd memory heavy-work-lease-removed) -- do not reintroduce a lease/semaphore as a gating mechanism for any of this.
notes: 2026-08-13 follow-on inherited from sinnix-eb9c (closed): sinnix-elicit wants a live in-session 'learning so far' preview -- mid-session ranking feedback while the operator is still comparing pairs. Blocked on the hub having no read endpoint: sinnix-hub-feedback is deliberately write-only POST, a decision made to avoid turning a write sink into an exfiltration surface. Unshackling the hub is exactly this bead's remit, so the read-API design (what may be read, by whom, over which bind address) belongs here rather than in a capture bead.

title: Hyprland config renderer: hyprlang -> Lua migration (deprecation clock)
description: Hyprland 0.55+ deprecated hyprlang for typed Lua config (hl namespace); support ends 1-2 releases past 0.55, no new features land in hyprlang (hypr.land/news/26_lua, discussion #14463). Repo pins configType=hyprlang explicitly (modules/features/desktop/hyprland/default.nix). KEY FACT: this repo GENERATES config from a Nix DSL (bindings/rules/scratchpads .nix) -- migration means changing the RENDERER to emit hyprland.lua, not hand-converting a config file; the community converters (hyprconf2lua, hyprlang2lua) are reference material for syntax mapping, not the tool. Sequencing: do AFTER the deliberate-config design pass decides what binds/rules survive (render the new design once, in Lua) -- or as pure mechanical re-render first if the design pass stalls; either order works, record which. Verify: rendered Lua loads (hyprctl reload exit + binds count matches pre-migration hyprctl binds -j length), Noctalia keybind-cheatsheet plugin still parses (it targets 0.55+ Lua natively -- may actually work BETTER post-migration).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Renderer investigation done (no execution -- this needs the operator's timing call). Three findings change the shape of this bead.

1. The renderer already exists upstream; this is a one-option flip, not a port. The pinned home-manager (modules/services/window-managers/hyprland/) implements both renderers behind configType, and 'lua' is already the DEFAULT for stateVersion >= 26.05 -- the repo's explicit configType = "hyprlang" is what is holding it back. In lua mode each settings attribute becomes an hl.<name>(...) call, one per list element.

2. Hyprland 0.56.1 is ALREADY in the pinned nixpkgs (nix eval ...pkgs.hyprland.version = 0.56.1). The live session is 0.55.4 only because Hyprland does not restart on switch. So the deprecation clock is one release further along than the bead assumed, and 0.56 arrives at the next relogin without any work.

3. Two concrete blockers, both verified by reading the HM lua generator, and neither is a syntax-mapping problem the community converters would help with:

   a. SUBMAPS SILENTLY LOSE STRING ENTRIES. The lua submap renderer filters with (filter (value: !isString value)) -- string entries render only in hyprlang mode, structured attrset entries only in lua mode. The system submap on SUPER+End is 10 string entries. Flipping configType without converting them drops all ten with no error: the submap keeps existing and does nothing, including its Escape/Return exits. This is the failure mode most likely to strand a live session.

   b. extraConfig IS emitted in lua mode, verbatim, into hyprland.lua. This repo's extraConfig carries 'source = ~/.config/hypr/noctalia.conf' plus rules.extraConfig -- hyprlang syntax, which is a Lua syntax error. Every hyprlang line in extraConfig must become Lua or move into settings/extraLuaFiles first.

   Unverified third item: whether hl.bindd accepts a single comma-joined string, or whether the described binds must be restructured into the _args form. The HM docs mention _args specifically for multi-argument calls, which suggests the combined string may not be idiomatic even if it parses. Test this before committing to the flip.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCING: do NOT flip while the bind grammar is still unsettled. Order should be (i) the design pass with the operator, (ii) rewrite binds/rules/submaps once against the chosen design, (iii) flip configType and render the new design straight into Lua. Rendering twice is the waste this bead was created to avoid.

ROLLBACK PATH is genuinely cheap and should be stated to the operator plainly: configType is one line, and a NixOS generation rollback plus relogin restores hyprland.conf. The compositor reads whichever file the generation provides; nothing about the flip is one-way. The real risk is not irreversibility, it is a HALF-WORKING session (submap dead, extraConfig broken) that is easy to miss because Hyprland does not fail loudly. Mitigate by flipping in a test-vm or a nested Hyprland session first and checking that hyprctl binds -j count matches the pre-flip number, not by treating it as a dangerous change.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
DECISION (made on the operator's standing directive to decide rather than propose): the Lua migration is NOT a standalone mechanical flip and must be executed as part of the fd4k execution pass, not before it. Correcting two wrong premises -- one in this bead, one in my own earlier comment on it.

WRONG PREMISE 1 (this bead's): 'migration means changing the RENDERER to emit hyprland.lua, not hand-converting a config file'. That is false, and it is the belief that makes this look cheap. Read from the Hyprland 0.56.1 source, src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsToplevel.cpp:

- There is no hl.bindd. Exactly one function is registered, hl.bind (line 537). Description is opts.description in a third table argument. So home-manager settings keys named bindd/binddl/binddm render hl.bindd(...) -- a call to nil, i.e. a config error, not a bind.
- Dispatchers are objects or Lua functions, never strings: 'hl.bind: dispatcher must be a dispatcher (e.g. hl.dsp.window.close()) or a lua function'. The entire 'exec, <command>' string form does not exist.
- The bind flags stop being keyword-name suffixes and become opts booleans (locked, release, mouse, non_consuming, ...).
- Even the key string changed separator. The shipped example/hyprland.lua uses hl.bind(mainMod .. " + Q", ...), not "SUPER, Q".

The shipped example shows the real target shape: hl.bind(mod .. ' + C', hl.dsp.window.close()), hl.dsp.focus({direction='left'}), hl.dsp.window.move({workspace=i}), hl.dsp.layout('togglesplit'), hl.dsp.exec_cmd(cmd). Every bind needs a semantic translation into a structured dispatcher call -- movetoworkspace, 1 becomes hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 1 }) -- with per-dispatcher lookup. Home-manager does not help: its lua renderer only maps an attribute name to hl.<name>(args), so every dispatcher would have to be hand-built via _args/mkLuaInline.

WRONG PREMISE 2 (mine, earlier in this bead): I wrote that this is a one-option flip because home-manager implements both renderers behind configType, and I recommended sequencing on the theory that rendering twice is the waste to avoid. Both halves were wrong. configType does select a renderer, but the Nix input it renders is a different language on the Lua side, so flipping the option without rewriting every bind produces a broken config, and there is no cheap 'mechanical re-render first' option to take.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR SEQUENCING: rewriting 111 binds plus rules into structured dispatcher calls IS the execution pass this program exists to do. Splitting it into 'migrate now, redesign later' means touching every bind twice by hand for no gain. So the original ordering in this bead was right, but for a reason nobody had established: not bookkeeping tidiness, a genuine full rewrite.

CONSEQUENCE: the design pass (sinnix-fd4k step 2, needs:operator) is now schedule-critical rather than merely desirable, because the deprecation clock gates it. That is uncomfortable given this program exists precisely because that session has never happened.

SAFETY VALVE, so the clock cannot force an emergency: hyprlang still works in 0.56.1 with no deprecation warning emitted anywhere in the source -- the sunset is announcement-based, not yet enforced. If a nixpkgs bump lands a Hyprland release that drops hyprlang before the design pass happens, pin Hyprland to the last hyprlang-supporting version via the existing overlay rather than attempting a rushed migration on a broken desktop. That converts the failure mode from 'desktop does not start' back into 'scheduling problem', and it is the standing instruction for whoever hits it.

NOT EXECUTED, and no part of it should ride the current batched switch.

Carry-forward: the sinnix-fd4k.4 description strings are not wasted by any of this -- they become opts.description verbatim.

title: Lynchpin stall-attribution view: join PSI stall windows to per-slice pressure spikes
description: Executable now, no operator gate. Data: telemetry.sqlite (machine-telemetry), tables per a1dp evidence: host-level memory_psi_full_avg60 samples + service_cgroup_pressure_sample (per-slice PSI already captured). Build the lynchpin analysis view that, for every window of memory_psi_full_avg60>15, attributes the stall to the slice(s) whose pressure spiked concurrently -- so each freeze self-attributes. Follow lynchpin's existing analysis-product conventions (see docs/reference/data-sources.md and existing views in the DAG; register in materialize DAG). AC: for the known worst day 2026-08-09, the view yields per-window top-attributed slices; a one-command invocation (python -m lynchpin.cli.materialize or a just recipe) cited in the closing note; spot-check that the 2026-08-03 05:10 containment-escape event attributes to user.agent slice (known ground truth from a1dp notes).

title: Evidence-based resource-governance tuning from telemetry + Meta resctl tooling
description: Operator directive 2026-08-12: stop hand-setting slice budgets; derive them from the telemetry we already collect, instrument the gaps, and use existing third-party tooling. EVIDENCE (30d, telemetry.sqlite): (1) stall windows are DAILY and long predate the heavy-lease removal -- worst day 2026-08-09 had ~2940 samples (~4h cumulative) of memory_psi_full_avg60>15 under the lease; the lease never protected interactivity. (2) user.agent slice is the dominant memory actor: 26.1GB peak on a 32G box, avg 5.5GB, 196M memory.high throttle events (deliberately uncapped slice, 8G/12G per-scope caps) -- vs build 23.6GB peak/722 throttles, nix-build 16.5GB, polylogued.service 15GB peak/2.3M throttles. Zero cgroup OOM kills anywhere: pressure manifests as thrash, never kills. (3) io.cost runs ctrl=auto (kernel auto-calibration), not benchmarked params, on CT4000P3SSD8 (P3 4TB) + MX500 roots. PLAN: (a) run resctl-bench (Meta) to derive real iocost QoS/model params for both SSDs, or pull CT4000P3SSD8/CT1000MX500SSD1 entries from github.com/iocost-benchmark/iocost-benchmarks hwdb if present; needs a quiet machine window (hours). (b) derive slice MemoryHigh/Low from measured p99/peak per label in cgroup_memory_sample instead of guesses; the agent slice needs an actual decision (uncapped-by-design vs the data showing it drives host pressure -- operator call with numbers in hand). (c) evaluate senpai-style memory.high probing for the fat daemons (polylogued at 15GB peak deserves its own working-set measurement). (d) instrument the one gap: per-slice PSI is captured (service_cgroup_pressure_sample) but define the analysis product -- lynchpin view joining stall windows to the slice(s) whose pressure spiked, so each freeze attributes itself. (e) after tuning, judge success by the daily stall-sample counts trending to ~0, not by feel.
acceptance_criteria: All four children closed; the agent-slice cap decision has an operator answer recorded here; success metric per original directive: daily count of memory_psi_full_avg60>15 samples trends toward ~0 after applied tunings (a1dp.1 view is the measurement instrument).
notes:
2026-08-12 CORRECTION (operator pushback: do not assume the agent-slice peak is legitimate): peak forensics (2026-08-03 05:10 UTC, 21.5GB RAM + 19.4GB swap in user.agent) show CONTAINMENT ESCAPE, not agent work: 57 concurrent cc1plus (up to 1.3GB PSS each) from an agent-invoked 'uv sync --extra audit' building native wheels -- gcc spawned inside agent scopes because command-name wrapper routing does not catch compilers spawned indirectly by uv wheel builds; plus koboldcpp-cuda (1.9GB) running in agent.slice instead of gpu-runtime.slice; plus lynchpin python at 3.3GB. Per-scope MemoryMax=12G held individually but memory.swap.max is deliberately unset (June decision, enforced by an agent-tools test asserting MemorySwapMax absent), so throttled scopes spilled 19.4GB into swap unbounded. Revised plan items: (f) close the routing escape -- native-build children of agent commands must land in build.slice (candidates: wrap uv's build backend env, or systemd delegation moving compile children), (g) revisit the no-per-scope-swap-cap decision with this evidence (a bounded swap allowance beats unbounded spill; the enforcing test is a fossilized-decision candidate), (h) find why koboldcpp ran in agent.slice and route it to gpu-runtime.
2026-08-12 drive restructure: split into a1dp.1 (stall-attribution view), a1dp.2 (percentile budget proposal), a1dp.3 (iocost hwdb probe before any bench), a1dp.4 (polylogued working-set eval). Parent holds the operator decision on the agent-slice cap. Caveat: the 26.1GB agent-slice peak is contaminated by the 2026-08-03 containment escape (57 cc1plus in agent scope) -- the real fix may be routing escapes into the build slice; decide after a1dp.2's clean numbers.
2026-08-12 analysis-layer finding (estate atlas): the stall-attribution instrument has a structural blind spot -- machine-telemetry's per-cgroup pressure sampling covers a fixed list of system services only; agent/build/nix-build slices are NOT sampled. Cross-examination of 2026-08-09 (worst stall day, 03:00-13:00 near-saturated): borgbackup-job-realm's 46% cgroup pressure exists only 10:00-13:00; hours 03-09 attribute to NOTHING tracked, i.e. the culprit lived in an unsampled cgroup, consistent with the agent-slice escape class. Add item: extend machine-telemetry cgroup pressure tracking to agent.slice/build.slice/nix-build.slice (+ per-scope rollup) BEFORE trusting attribution for tuning decisions. Also: borg-job self-thrash against its 2G class budget during realm drains (10:00-13:00 tail) -- revisit its budget from measured peaks.
sinnix-a1dp.2 RESULT (2026-08-13): 30-day per-slice memory percentiles from /realm/state/machine-telemetry/telemetry.sqlite's cgroup_memory_sample, vs current flake/data/runtime-defaults.nix budgets. PROPOSAL ONLY, no budgets edited.

Exact SQL (reproducible): for each label, `SELECT memory_current_bytes FROM cgroup_memory_sample WHERE label=? AND observed_at >= datetime('now','-30 days') AND memory_current_bytes IS NOT NULL` (user.agent additionally excludes `observed_at >= '2026-08-03T05:00:00+00:00' AND observed_at < '2026-08-03T06:00:00+00:00'`), percentiles computed as `sorted(values)[min(n-1, int(p*n))]` for p in {0.50, 0.95, 0.99}, peak = max.

Two findings beyond the raw table: (1) system.background and user.background both show the exact-ceiling-pinning pattern (p95=p99=peak, all == current MemoryHigh) -- worth treating as a real signal that background-maintenance work is being suppressed below its natural demand, not just noise. (2) nix-build/build slices are over-provisioned by roughly 3x at p99 across the board -- real headroom to reclaim if the operator wants it, at low risk given the margins proposed above still clear peak by several GB.

title: aw-server-rust datastore mutex poisons permanently on SQLite busy-lock panic (silent, ~3-day outage found live)
description: Live incident 2026-08-12: aw-server (ActivityWatch) had been silently dead-while-active since 2026-08-09 03:38:12 -- systemd reported the unit healthy the entire time. Root cause (journalctl --user -u activitywatch.service, exact timestamp): the worker thread panicked on 'Failed to commit datastore transaction! database is locked' (aw-datastore/src/worker.rs:195, a SQLite SQLITE_BUSY condition handled via unwrap() instead of retry-with-backoff), and Rust's std::sync::Mutex poisons permanently on a panicked holder -- every subsequent request returned 504 'poisoned lock: another task failed inside' for ~3 days. The companion watcher (awatcher) kept running and logging 'Failed to send heartbeat' repeatedly during the outage; heartbeats are dropped on failure, not queued/retried to disk, so window/activity/idle events from that ~3-day window are genuinely lost, not delayed. 03:38 AM strongly suggests collision with a nightly backup/snapshot job touching the same sqlite file concurrently (borg/btrbk timers run in that window) -- worth checking timer overlap. Immediate mitigation applied live: systemctl --user restart activitywatch.service cleared the poison and writes resumed within 15s (verified via sqlite.db mtime + clean startup log, no new panic/poison lines).
design: Two independent fixes needed: (1) UPSTREAM/PACKAGING: aw-server-rust should retry-with-backoff on SQLITE_BUSY at commit time rather than unwrap()-panic -- check if a newer aw-server-rust release fixes this, or patch/override locally, or at minimum move its sqlite.db onto a nodatacow subvol (the repo already uses nodatacow for exactly this write-contention class, e.g. sinex postgres) to reduce SQLITE_BUSY frequency from btrfs COW overhead compounding with concurrent access. (2) DETECTION: this is precisely the 'process alive but functionally dead' failure class the capture-integrity sentinel (bd show sinnix-e8e) exists to catch -- systemd is-active is provably insufficient here since it stayed green for 3 days. Add a health probe that greps recent aw-server journal for 'poisoned lock'/'panic' OR checks sqlite.db mtime against expected-write-cadence (there's near-continuous desktop activity on this host; a multi-hour-stale mtime during active hours is itself a strong signal), feeding into e8e's scoreboard when that lands. (3) BACKUP-TIMER OVERLAP: check whether borg/btrbk timers run at 03:3x and could be independently adjusted to avoid the collision window, as a root-cause mitigation alongside the retry fix.
acceptance_criteria: A grep-based or mtime-based health check exists (standalone or as an e8e-registered probe) that would have caught this outage within its detection window, not 3 days later via manual investigation. aw-server no longer panics on a single SQLITE_BUSY event, OR its sqlite.db is moved to nodatacow, OR both.
close_reason: Panic backported away (vendored aw-server-rust patch, c96d48b: upstream #256 logs-and-continues on commit failure); detection AC already satisfied by c1cb98f staleAfterSeconds=3600 sentinel registration, verified live via health-transitions.jsonl; nodatacow deliberately skipped (same-day c1cb98f decision keeps sqlite in backed-up home; AC was OR); timer overlap investigated, borgbackup-job-realm@03:35 strongest suspect, no speculative edit since panic now non-fatal. Follow-ups filed separately.

title: Capture registry: staleAfterSeconds end-to-end + register off-books lanes
description: Sentinel currently watches only lanes with numeric expectedCadenceSeconds -- runtime-defaults.nix maps eventDriven=true to a string the sentinel's null-filter drops, so event-driven captures are unwatched. Add staleAfterSeconds (nullOr int) to the captures submodule in modules/runtime.nix; render as expectedStaleAfterSeconds in flake/data/runtime-defaults.nix; sentinel logic: stale if age>2*cadence OR age>staleAfterSeconds, keeping transition-only notify; add an event-driven-lane-goes-stale fixture to flake/tests/health-sentinel.nix. Register currently off-registry lanes with staleness budgets: keylog logs/ 3600s, comms/irc 3600s, webhistory 172800s, screenshot 604800s, kitty-scrollback 86400s, activitywatch 3600s (owning modules where they exist; new modules/services/capture-registry.nix for orphan paths); add staleAfterSeconds to the 6 existing captures[] entries; update modules/introspection.nix captures.directories. Exit: sentinel reports 13 lanes; currently-dead kitty/AW lanes show red.
close_reason: Fixed and merged: staleAfterSeconds end-to-end, off-registry lanes registered, sentinel dual-threshold logic. Switched live and verified (13 lanes visible).

title: Enrichment loop v0: timer -> state-dump -> claude -p processing skill -> versioned derived outputs (substrate-independent)
description: Concrete first increment of sinnix-qa2s, explicitly sinex/polylogue-store-independent per the 2026-08-11 fork verdicts (re-derivability doctrine makes later re-pointing clean; single-writer: NEVER writes polylogue/sinex stores). Shape: systemd user timer -> dump script assembling {runtime-inventory, steering workspace bd export, atuin tail, polylogue hook-spool + raw session JSONL deltas since last run, fresh lynchpin products, journald highlights} -> claude -p with a processing skill -> outputs under /realm/data/derived/enrichment/ as versioned products with provenance pointers (since-last narrative, structured state delta, flags for steering review). Sizes ~2-4h per the sinex fork. Interim inputs per polylogue fork: hook spool at /realm/db/polylogue/hooks/*.jsonl (live, daemon-independent) + ~/.claude/projects raw JSONL; post-restart switch to CLI/MCP reads.
design:
Executor contract (Sonnet-grade; decisions made, do not relitigate):
- Components: (1) scripts/sinnix-enrich-dump (frontmatter-packaged) assembling the state bundle to a tmpdir: /etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json; BEADS_DIR=/realm/state/steering/.beads bd export (steering workspace); atuin history tail (last 24h, atuin search --after); polylogue hook-spool deltas /realm/db/polylogue/hooks/*.jsonl since last-run watermark; ~/.claude/projects/*/\*.jsonl mtime-filtered deltas; lynchpin current_state products if fresh (<24h); journalctl -p warning --since=<watermark> capped 500 lines. Watermark file: /realm/state/enrichment/last-run (persist entry required, same-change). (2) A processing skill dots/_ai/skills/enrichment-pass/ (SKILL.md contract: input bundle dir -> outputs; keep prompt content in the skill, NOT inline in the script). (3) claude -p invocation: claude -p --output-format json with explicit model (sonnet default per dispatch doctrine), subscription auth, --bare. (4) Outputs to /realm/data/derived/enrichment/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMM/: narrative.md, state-delta.json (versioned schema sinnix-enrichment-v1: {schema, generated_at, window:{from,to}, inputs:[{source,path,items}], narrative_ref, flags:[{kind,severity,ref}]}), plus provenance pointers to consumed input files. (5) mkServiceModule sinnix.services.enrichment-loop: user timer (OnCalendar hourly to start; operator tunes later), runtime surface registration (background-maintenance class), captures[] entry ONLY if lake-write lands under /realm/data/derived (it is derived, not capture -- so NO captures entry; register observe.enable only).
- Single-writer invariant (binding): NEVER write polylogue or sinex stores; read-only on every input; outputs only under /realm/data/derived/enrichment/ + the watermark under /realm/state/enrichment/.
- Failure honesty: if claude -p fails, write a failure marker row into the day dir ({schema, generated_at, error}) instead of silence -- the e8e class lesson.
Verification (executor runs): one manual invocation end-to-end producing a real narrative + valid state-delta.json (jq -e schema check); timer listed; second run consumes only the delta window (watermark advances; inputs[] shows delta item counts, not full history).
acceptance_criteria: Manual run produces /realm/data/derived/enrichment/<date>/<time>/{narrative.md,state-delta.json} with state-delta.json passing a jq -e check of the sinnix-enrichment-v1 shape and inputs[] provenance filled; a second run advances the watermark and processes only deltas; systemd user timer registered + listed; zero writes outside /realm/data/derived/enrichment and /realm/state/enrichment (verify: run under strace -f -e trace=openat filtered for O_WRONLY|O_CREAT outside those roots, or by directory mtime survey); failure path verified once by forcing claude -p to fail (bogus flag) and observing the failure marker row.
notes:

title: Build the read-only Sinnix operations reducer
description: Add one low-latency reducer around existing sinnix-observe collectors. Publish a versioned current-state snapshot and event stream for Noctalia, sinnixctl, MCP tools, and coordinators without resampling high-frequency machine data or copying owner-native evidence.
design: Implement a Python service that imports or invokes the bounded sinnix-observe read model and subscribes to systemd D-Bus, cgroup files, inotify sources, agent events, attention events, and quota updates. Initial scope is read-only. Publish atomic XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sinnix/status.json, a Unix socket for local clients, and a systemd-socket-activated loopback HTTP endpoint with GET /v1/snapshot, GET /v1/events, and GET /v1/health. HTTP requires a per-session bearer capability in a 0600 runtime file and rejects unexpected Origin and Host values. Every source and derived field carries observed_at, source, freshness, confidence or coverage where meaningful, and degradation reason. The service may persist normalized quota snapshots and reducer transitions under /realm/state/sinnix-ops, but raw machine/session/task evidence remains with its owner. No action endpoint exists in this lane.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with healthy, stale, missing, and malformed sources produces truthful distinct states; snapshot replacement is atomic and bounded; Unix, HTTP, and SSE views carry the same schema and sequence; an unauthorized or browser-shaped request is rejected; reconnect resumes from a documented sequence boundary or receives a fresh snapshot; no collector polls faster than its owner; RSS and idle CPU stay within measured budgets; stopping one source degrades only that source; focused tests and switch pass.

Implemented and deployed the read-only operations reducer.

- Atomic bounded snapshot replacement: satisfied by atomic_json with fsync and replace; live status.json is 194595 bytes and mode 0600.

title: Sinnix operator control plane
description: Build one workstation operator plane over existing Sinnix runtime, agent, telemetry, quota, attention, and evidence authorities. Noctalia is a thin presentation client. The control plane publishes current state and typed actions while owner-native systems retain durable truth.
design: Authority order is fixed: runtime inventory declares surfaces and policy; systemd and cgroups own live lifecycle and actuation; attested job manifests own agent identity; machine telemetry owns raw host metrics; Polylogue owns session-native evidence; Beads owns task state; the operator reducer owns only normalized current state, quota snapshots without another owner, and action receipts; Lynchpin owns historical correlation and calibration. Extend sinnix-observe collectors rather than duplicating them. Publish an atomic XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sinnix/status.json fallback, a local Unix socket for sinnixctl and MCP consumers, and authenticated loopback HTTP plus SSE for Noctalia. Noctalia plugins contain rendering and typed action requests only. Keep Noctalia on an exact upstream release with Nix-pinned plugins and no semantic fork until measured plugin limitations require a persistent core patch.
acceptance_criteria: Every child lane has a disjoint authority and executable verification; Noctalia v5 config validates without warnings; Noctalia is classified and observed; one versioned snapshot and event stream serve CLI, MCP, and shell consumers; unavailable sources remain unavailable rather than zero; typed actions require declared capability and produce receipts; quota, agent, attention, orphan, and health facts join by stable IDs; Lynchpin remains outside the live request path; no duplicate collector, job runner, policy registry, or shell-owned command authority remains.
