title: Unify gateway and agent-control MCP on one official-SDK server with capability profiles
description: Replace both hand-written MCP protocol loops with one server on the exact stable official MCP Python SDK. Generate local-agent-control, remote-readonly, and remote-operator from one typed registry, with capability checks at registration and operation boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Both protocol loops and legacy HTTP handler are deleted; all profiles initialize from repo root; manifests are canonical-hashed; read-only mutation fails before effects; errors omit tracebacks and host paths; SDK negotiation has no conflicting hard-coded protocol literal.
close_reason: The official MCP SDK 2.0.0 server replaced both hand-written protocol loops and the HTTP handler. Three profiles generate canonical manifests; read-only policy, error redaction, path safety, and real stdio negotiation are covered by focused tests. The broader live launch and credential fixture remains tracked in sinnix-056.5.

title: Shared attested systemd jobs, project lifecycle, bounded artifacts, and credential profiles
description: Extract native agent handles into shared typed services. Use UUID manifests and attested transient systemd units for execution, canonical sinnix.projects metadata, private state, opaque bounded artifacts, secure path resolution, and explicit minimal credential environments.
acceptance_criteria: Native and gateway launches share manifest/status semantics; IDs never collide; deadlines/cancel kill descendants; reads bound before IO; symlink escapes fail; state is 0700/0600 and persisted; malformed legacy records are reported; old PID state is migrated or archived.
notes: Gateway and native launches now share UUID v2 manifests, atomic persistent launch reservations, transient systemd units, cgroup attestation, lifecycle reconciliation, deadlines, and descendant-safe cancellation. Reads are bounded before storage, symlink escapes fail, state modes are 0700/0600 and persisted, malformed records remain visible, legacy state migration archives old PID records, and child environments use an explicit allowlist. Live launch/cancel proof ran in agent.slice with MemoryHigh and MemoryMax enforced.
close_reason: Shared job, artifact, project, credential, migration, and lifecycle contracts are implemented and verified, including concurrent ID-collision and live descendant-cancellation proofs.

title: Gateway/job audit ledger and unified runtime/observe/Polylogue correlation
description: Register gateway, tunnel and jobs in runtime inventory; expose their live contract through sinnix-observe; emit structured journal fields and a concurrency-safe tamper-evident ledger using the same stable request/job/workspace/artifact IDs. Polylogue consumes the semantic events for historical attribution without becoming lifecycle authority.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent audit writes verify; one fixture joins journal/manifest/cgroup/observe/Polylogue by ID; worker cgroup resources are used; errors redact secrets; observe is versioned and bounded under collector failure; quota freshness distinguishes observation from inference.
notes: The SQLite WAL audit ledger verifies under concurrent writers. Runtime inventory and sinnix-observe join gateway audit, v2 manifest, structured journal fields, cgroup identity, resource policy, and the Polylogue-compatible SQLite FTS history adapter by stable job ID. The real fixture joins audit and journal records and explicitly reports the currently unavailable Polylogue archive without making it lifecycle authority. Errors redact secrets, collection is bounded and versioned, and quota data distinguishes inferred values from observed freshness.
close_reason: Audit, runtime inventory, observe, cgroup, redaction, quota provenance, and Polylogue-compatible correlation acceptance criteria pass; the external Polylogue runtime remains unavailable as an explicitly reported source condition.

title: Migrate gateway state, delete duplicate control planes, and prove final end-to-end architecture
description: Integrate all slices, migrate or archive useful legacy state, delete superseded transports/jobs/config/project/task/status registries, republish the connector, and run the complete adversarial verification matrix. Disabled duplicate code is not completion.
acceptance_criteria: Reboot/login starts a healthy tunnel; ChatGPT read-only calls match approved schema; local agent launch/cancel uses the shared server and intended cgroup; audit/observe/history correlation succeeds; failure classes diagnose correctly; target probes, root tests, Nix deployment and deletion searches pass.
notes: The pinned tunnel launches the official-SDK remote-readonly server over stdio with no local HTTP listener. Migration succeeds, the tunnel starts enabled with zero restarts, the approved 14-tool manifest gate matches 7078f104e482052bd0f2f3728a3beb1eaba3985a3895962ca553562c0e2aa3a5, and authenticated ChatGPT calls returned that exact manifest hash, the distinct capability hash, profile remote-readonly, and README content. Legacy HTTP, duplicate MCP loops, PID jobs, duplicate status command, and duplicate registries are deleted. Final security review found Git diff option injection; commit da9e087 rejects option-shaped refs, resolves commits immutably, disables external diff and text conversion, and passes a hostile-driver regression.
close_reason: Migration, deletion, deployment, tunnel health, live ChatGPT connector, shared launch/cancel, correlation, failure diagnostics, and adversarial security verification are complete.

title: Stop cursor warps during keyboard focus changes
description: Hyprland moved the mouse cursor when window focus changed through keyboard keybinds. Persist cursor.no_warps so keyboard-driven focus changes leave pointer position unchanged while ordinary pointer focus behavior remains available.
acceptance_criteria: cursor.no_warps is enabled in the declared Hyprland configuration, active in the live compositor, and survives a system switch.
close_reason: Declared Hyprland cursor.no_warps = true, deployed it with switch, reloaded Hyprland, and verified hyprctl reports cursor:no_warps set to 1. Keyboard focus changes no longer request pointer warps and the setting persists in the system configuration.

title: Keep Kitty text bright across focus opacity changes
description: Inactive Kitty windows need translucent backgrounds with readable text, while the active Kitty window should remain nearly opaque. Hyprland whole-window opacity dims text and cannot provide this split, so Kitty background opacity must follow compositor focus.
design: Enable Kitty dynamic background opacity and use a Hyprland event listener to update Kitty OS-window opacity on focus changes. Keep global inactive opacity near 1 so non-Kitty content remains legible.
acceptance_criteria: Active Kitty background is nearly opaque; inactive Kitty backgrounds use the chosen translucent level with text unaffected by compositor fading; browsers remain mostly opaque; light blur remains; behavior survives wallpaper changes and is deployed live.
close_reason: Enabled Kitty native background alpha with a Hyprland focus listener, verified fresh-window transitions at 0.96 active and 0.72 inactive, retained bright text with light blur, and deployed live.

title: Wire Grok and Antigravity into agent orchestration
description: Problem: Grok persistence exists but lacks a managed wrapper and orchestration backend, while Antigravity has a wrapper but the vendor CLI was absent and orchestration only accepts Claude, Codex, and Gemini. Scope: install and authenticate the official Grok and Antigravity CLIs, add managed wrappers and persistence, extend the attested runner, batch launcher, runtime probe, MCP control plane, and focused tests/docs for both backends. Include capability-aware handling for Antigravity print mode and preserve vendor self-updating binaries. Verification: focused shell tests, Nix agent-tools fixture, CLI version/model checks, and a non-sensitive print-mode smoke test. Follow-up: none unless vendor flags or authentication remain unavailable.
close_reason: Implemented managed Grok and Antigravity wrappers, persistence, attested batch execution, Kitty launch support, runtime probing, MCP control-plane routing, focused tests, and orchestration documentation. Verified both vendor model catalogs and completed real prompt runs through run_agent_prompt.sh. Antigravity now receives a non-blocking MCP profile without Lynchpin. The agent-tools runtime Nix check and job-handle tests pass, and the deployed wrappers are live.

title: Restore reliable HDR screenshots
description: Direct grim screencopy on the live Hyprland HDR output regressed to nearly all-black PNGs. Reinstate a capture path that produces correct sRGB screenshots and restores the exact monitorv2 configuration afterward.
acceptance_criteria: Print region and focused-output captures save and copy non-black PNGs without monitor modesets, signal blanking, or HDR metadata changes; wallpaper replacement preserves inactive-window blur composition; focused config validation, repository lint, and live switch pass.
notes:
The first repair restored screenshots by switching HDR to sRGB, but the resulting signal blink is not acceptable. Follow-up evidence: Noctalia native screencopy produced a valid 3840x2160, 6.65 MB image without changing monitor state and copied it asynchronously to the clipboard. Three forced wallpaper changes with direct HDR capture stayed healthy. Hyprland documents keep_unmodified_copy=1 for transparent screenshots and use_shader_blur_blend=true for missing blur with FP16/unmodified-copy paths.
Earlier evidence retained: direct HDR grim produced a 3840x2160 image with mean channel value 0.000006 and 47 colors; the temporary sRGB wrapper produced a normal 3.87 MB image with 90,783 colors but caused an unacceptable signal blink. Final evidence: native Noctalia focused-output capture produced identical saved and clipboard 3840x2160, 6.54 MB images with 91,757 colors. Native region capture produced identical saved and clipboard 1177x709 images. Monitor HDR fields matched exactly before and after both captures. A post-switch wallpaper replacement followed by native capture produced a healthy 6.02 MB image with 158,444 colors while all renderer pins and HDR fields persisted. Noctalia config validation passed with one inherited notification.allowed_urgencies warning; repository lint and live switch passed.
close_reason: Replaced the blinking monitor-mode workaround with Noctalia native screencopy, pinned Hyprland's retained SDR copy and shader blur path, verified output and region save/copy behavior without HDR state changes, and deployed the configuration.

title: systemd follow-up PR: destroy_bus flush guard closes 6-year-old #16471 user-manager 90s AUTHENTICATING hang
description: Session 2026-07-31 established (building on 07-19 session c0865cf6): systemd#16471 (2020, v245, still open, mislabeled not-our-bug) is destroy_bus()'s sd_bus_flush() for user managers driving an unauthenticated connection through bus_ensure_running() — single-fd ppoll block, up to BUS_AUTH_TIMEOUT=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_USEC=90s. Our merged systemd#42981 fixed only the connect-time GetId block and un-shadowed this teardown-time one; our 07-11 comment on #42981 overclaimed ('should resolve that report as well') and gets corrected via the #16471 closure comment. Fix staged: /realm/worktrees/systemd-16471 branch fix/user-bus-flush-only-when-ready commit e408b209d1 — guard flush with sd_bus_is_ready(*bus)>0 (call-site shape poettering endorsed in-thread 2021 while rejecting GKraats sd-bus boolean; 'should not issue dbus messages when the dbus service isn't fully up'). Alternatives documented and rejected: GKraats sd-bus escape hatch (maintainer-rejected), benzea socket.c !unit_stop_pending guard (complementary different layer, never landed, verified absent on main 2026-07-31), unit.c -EBUSY double-match log noise (separate concern, not bundled). C demonstrator /realm/tmp/dbx/flush-block.c: guarded=0.0s verified; unguarded ~90s run pending. Remaining: full systemd build check, PR body + #16471 comment drafts, push+PR after operator OK.
close_reason: systemd PR 43227 merged on 2026-07-31, issue 16471 closed, and the submitted guard prevents destroy_bus from flushing a user-manager bus that never reached RUNNING.

title: Refresh pre-unlock Android backup and rooting prerequisites
description: Recover the prior device-preparation session, refresh all non-destructive ADB/Xiaomi backup layers after elapsed time, verify integrity and current firmware/tool compatibility, and leave the device ready for an explicitly authorized bootloader-unlock step. Do not perform the destructive unlock or factory reset without fresh explicit operator confirmation.
design: Continue only non-destructive preparation until a fresh operator gate. Authority order is live device properties, checksummed local backup manifests, official firmware artifacts, then prior notes. Reverify backup freshness and restore readability without modifying bootloader state. Produce a gate sheet listing account eligibility, recovery readiness, firmware and boot artifact hashes, expected wipe, and exact next command. The unlock, factory reset, flashing, or partition write requires explicit authorization in the current session and must stop if any recovery-critical app or account is unresolved. Do not treat tool availability as authorization.
acceptance_criteria: A gate sheet exists (note on this bead or referenced file) listing: account eligibility status, recovery readiness per app, firmware + boot artifact hashes with checksums verified, expected wipe scope, and the exact next command for the unlock step -- with NO destructive action taken. Every backup layer reverified readable within the last session that closes this. The unlock itself is explicitly out of scope (separate fresh authorization).
notes:
2026-07-30 progress: Recovered the prior Codex preparation session and completed the non-destructive refresh. Reverified shared storage and the complete APK/split set; captured provider exports, fresh VCFs, a fresh Xiaomi local backup, Termux portable archives, a repeatable settings/package/AppOps baseline, Google transport results, and an explicitly authorized owner-only sensitive service-state layer. Source/host manifests and archive structures verify. Regenerated the firmware-matched Magisk stock-ROM candidate and verified its kernel payload; archived current official Magisk, APatch, KernelSU, Neo Backup, platform-tools, Mi Unlock, and payload extraction tools. Staged and inspected the current official Evolution X Android 16 candidate: its OTA payload parses and the published boot/vendor_boot content regions match the payload, while independently salted unsigned AVB footers explain full-file hash differences. Bootloader remains locked, Verified Boot green, and no reboot-to-fastboot, wipe, flash, unlock, or relock occurred. Remaining operator gates: verify Authenticator sync or direct transfer; verify banking recovery access; bind the Xiaomi account/device and obtain Mi Unlock eligibility; then provide the exact factory-reset authorization phrase.
2026-08-12: operator scheduled the device session for THIS WEEK. Pre-session prep (agent, before the session): assemble the gate sheet skeleton from the bead's design -- (1) locate prior device-preparation session notes (polylogue search: Xiaomi/ADB/unlock), (2) list the backup layers to reverify with their last-known checksums/manifests, (3) current firmware artifact + hash fetch links, (4) account-eligibility checklist (Mi account unlock waiting period status), (5) exact next-command sequence ending AT the authorization gate. Deliverable: session runbook note here so the physical session is <30min.
2026-08-13 -- named payoffs of unlocking, discovered while configuring the phone: MIUI/HyperOS blocks ALL adb and sideload installs (INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED; verified NOT a user-restriction -- no restrictions are set -- it is HyperOS's own Mi-account-gated check, and neither the file-URI installer route nor a Termux-initiated install with REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES granted gets past it). Consequences today: no F-Droid, no FUTO Voice Input (best local ASR keyboard), no Syncthing, no ActivityWatch mobile (the phone-telemetry hole the device program flagged). Play Store is the only install route. Unlock therefore buys the whole F-Droid ecosystem, not just root. ALSO: keep com.xiaomi.account / finddevice / cloudservice installed -- the debloat pass deliberately spared them because the unlock flow needs Mi account + Find Device. Developer options already shows 'OEM unlocking' and 'Mi Unlock status' entries.
2026-08-13 addendum: the Play-store build of Termux CANNOT install Termux:API (upstream: termux-play-store/termux-apps#29) -- termux-battery-status works from a bundled subset but termux-sensor and the rest of the 69-command API surface refuse. So the phone's whole sensor/telemetry capture plane (sinnix-uyvt.2) is gated on sideloading the F-Droid Termux, i.e. on unlock. Add that to the unlock payoff list alongside F-Droid itself, FUTO Voice Input, Syncthing, and ActivityWatch mobile.

title: machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup has silently failed daily since 2026-06-16 (sqlite3 .backup times out)
description:
Discovered 2026-07-29 while auditing polylogue-2a6d (nested-subvolume backup gap) and using machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup.service as the cited precedent pattern.

journalctl -u machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup.service shows every daily run since 2026-06-16 (Boot 9f9c92a6.. onward, ~6 weeks) failing with `start operation timed out. Terminating` at the 30min TimeoutStartSec, after writing 40-65G to disk each run. Only two real backups exist in /realm/staging/machine-telemetry/: telemetry-20260612T064528Z.sqlite.zst and telemetry-20260615T014231Z.sqlite.zst. Every day since is a stray 1024-byte `telemetry-<stamp>.sqlite.tmp-journal` file (a SQLite rollback-journal sidecar the script's cleanup trap does not remove, since it only rm's $raw_tmp/$zst_tmp, not "$raw_tmp-journal").

Root cause not yet diagnosed but likely: `sqlite3 <dbPath> ".backup '$raw_tmp'"` (modules/services/machine-telemetry.nix, script around line 396) hangs against the live, continuously-growing /realm/state/machine-telemetry/telemetry.sqlite (18G, collector writes every intervalSec=10s) -- no busy-timeout/retry handling, and the large write volume (40-65G per run) suggests repeated retried backup steps rather than a single clean .backup pass.

Separately noted in the same audit: /realm/db/machine-telemetry (btrfs subvolume ID 4085, created 2026-07-11, 0 bytes) is an orphaned, unused, empty nested subvolume -- superseded by /realm/state/machine-telemetry (the path the module actually uses, ID 1760). Not a backup gap (nothing lives there) but dead config-drift debris worth cleaning up (requires operator-supervised btrfs subvolume delete, out of scope for an automated agent).

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the configured machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup service against the live continuously written telemetry database, then inspect its journal and staging directory. The current failure is a 30-minute start timeout after tens of GiB written, followed by a 1 KiB telemetry-*.sqlite.tmp-journal sidecar and no compressed backup.
design: Keep the backup as a systemd oneshot owned by modules/services/machine-telemetry.nix. Reproduce against a copy or SQLite online-backup API before editing the live timer. First determine whether the 48-65 GiB writes come from rollback-journal churn, destination filesystem behavior, or writer starvation. Preferred implementation is a small Python backup helper using sqlite3.Connection.backup() with bounded pages, progress, busy timeout, cancellation-safe temporary files, and atomic rename, followed by zstd. Do not stop the collector for the normal daily path. Clean raw_tmp, raw_tmp-journal, raw_tmp-wal, and compressed temporary files in one trap/finally path. Keep the empty /realm/db/machine-telemetry subvolume deletion as an operator-supervised separate action. A smaller model should stop after diagnosis if the proposed helper cannot prove a consistent SQLite backup under concurrent writes.
acceptance_criteria: The old timeout is reproduced in a bounded fixture or its exact write amplification is otherwise measured; the replacement completes against an actively written fixture and passes SQLite integrity_check after decompression; temporary sidecars are removed on success, failure, and cancellation; one live timer run produces a new compressed backup and reports success; deletion of the empty legacy subvolume is either explicitly authorized and completed or recorded as a separate operator action.
notes:
Implementation checkpoint 2026-08-07: added scripts/sinnix-sqlite-backup using sqlite3.Connection.backup pages=0, bounded busy timeout, integrity_check, SIGTERM cancellation, atomic zstd output, and cleanup of raw/rollback/WAL/compressed sidecars. Added pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py. Tests: pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py, 2 passed; PYTHONPATH=pkgs/machine-telemetry pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_collector_process_memory.py, 7 passed. First live run of the page-stepped implementation was stopped by this agent after 8 minutes at 464M of a 21G source, demonstrating the old write-amplification shape without consuming the 30-minute timeout. The corrected pages=0 helper passed the active-writer fixture but has not yet had a second live run. Deployment is blocked at 2026-08-07T03:14Z by another agent's shared Sinnix heavy-work lease token 3f7926e9, owner pid 3346238; no process was killed or lease reclaimed. Staged owned script only; modules/services/machine-telemetry.nix remains unstaged. Pre-existing dirty paths are untouched.
Follow-up code checkpoint 2026-08-07: changed the production backup batch size to pages=100000 with no artificial sleep, preserving progress cancellation checks while reducing callback overhead; source and target handles now close before zstd. pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py remains 2 passed. Commit 208daea is pushed. A second live run remains pending the shared lease.
Corrected handoff reconciliation 2026-08-07: treat machine-telemetry SQLite as a producer/spool and query projection, not a boundary outside Sinex. Durability closure must include lossless Sinex admission or immutable replayable source material, coverage/watermarks, and restore/replay evidence before source rotation is accepted.
2026-08-07 live verification result: regular sparse copy of the 22 GB main file completed in approximately 6 minutes and carried the WAL sidecar while machine-telemetry.service remained active. The production route then entered full PRAGMA integrity_check, exceeded the service's 30-minute TimeoutStartSec, and was terminated by systemd before compression/publication. The exact orphaned process and telemetry-20260807T155818Z temporary sidecars were cleaned. Focused pytest remains 2 passed. sinnix-ded stays open. Next design decision is to provide a bounded large-database integrity strategy or separate verification phase; do not claim live backup success or delete the empty legacy subvolume.
Final verification 2026-08-07: changed the helper to checkpoint the WAL, copy the main database and WAL sidecar with cp --sparse=always, and apply full PRAGMA integrity_check to bounded fixtures while using a bounded schema/openability check for oversized live projections. Focused pytest -q pkgs/machine-telemetry/tests/test_backup.py: 2 passed; the active-writer fixture decompressed the output and ran full integrity_check, and failure cleanup remained sidecar-clean. Deployed via sinnix-heavy-lease --wait-seconds 300 -- nix develop --command switch. Live systemctl start --wait machine-telemetry-sqlite-backup.service succeeded: Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0, 6min49.307s wall, 24.5G read, 5.4G written. Published /realm/staging/machine-telemetry/telemetry-20260807T163618Z.sqlite.zst (2,016,757,913 bytes); zstd -t passed. Independent decompression plus sqlite3 PRAGMA page_count; PRAGMA schema_version; SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master returned 5527296, 90, and 36. No run-specific temporary sidecars remained. The empty legacy /realm/db/machine-telemetry subvolume was not deleted and remains an operator-supervised action.
close_reason: Replaced live online-backup write amplification with a bounded WAL-aware sparse copy, preserved full integrity_check proof for the active-writer fixture, deployed the helper, and verified one live timer run produced a compressed backup with independent decompression and SQLite schema checks. The empty legacy subvolume deletion remains explicitly recorded as operator-supervised.

title: repair GitHub verification for signed project history
description: Recent Sinnix commits are valid SSH signatures locally but GitHub reports no_user because the repository-local identity is Codex <codex@local>. A prior Sinex history-signing rewrite preserved GitHub <noreply@github.com> as committer while replacing GitHub signatures with the operator SSH signature, so GitHub reports unknown_key despite local cryptographic validity. Audit all first-party active repositories, repair future signing identity, and prepare a metadata-preserving history correction where it does not destroy more durable linkage than already lost.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every new local commit uses the verified Sinity <ezo.dev@gmail.com> identity and the registered SSH signing key; repository-local synthetic identity overrides cannot silently defeat GitHub verification.
2. Every rewritten commit preserves author date, committer date, tree, message bytes including PR/issue references, and parent topology; an independently generated manifest proves those invariants old-to-new.
3. The exact GitHub verification result is audited across active first-party repositories and remaining historical exceptions are enumerated honestly.
4. No published history is rewritten or force-pushed without an explicit operator confirmation naming repositories, ranges, counts, and PR-link consequences.
5. After any approved publication, GitHub API reports verified=true/valid for the rewritten default-branch commits and future smoke commits.
notes:
Audit 2026-07-16: GitHub default-branch verification counts: sinnix 311 no_user + 125 unknown_key + 142 valid (578 total); sinex 1403 unknown_key + 345 valid (1748 total). Sinnix invalids are 311 Codex <codex@local> committers, 76 Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> committers, and 49 GitHub <noreply@github.com> committers, all SSH-signed by the operator key. Sinex invalids are 1403 GitHub-committer commits signed by the operator key. The earlier Sinex rewrite already severed native mergeCommit SHAs for the 1403 affected PRs (sample #282/#2510); messages retain (#N).

Future-path repair applied locally: removed Sinnix checkout user.name/user.email overrides; effective identity is now Sinity <ezo.dev@gmail.com> with SSH signing enabled.

Prepared but NOT published: isolated candidate Sinnix tip f75e90e06c03 (base 9931044357c6, 538 replayed, 437 committer identities normalized) and Sinex tip 0395a7aacb04 (base cb2a1c72e223, 1632 replayed, 1408 normalized). Independent verification proves identical trees/message bytes/author metadata/author dates/committer dates/linear topology; all new signatures verify as ezo.dev@gmail.com. Manifests: /realm/tmp/signature-repair/{sinnix,sinex}.json. No tags or open PR branches lie in either rewritten suffix; only master and unrelated gh-pages are published. Publishing Sinex necessarily severs the still-native mergeCommit association for PRs #2511-#2515 while retaining their URLs, merged state, message references, and original commit objects.
Local Sinex work preservation: feature/docs/remove-retired-thoughtspace-refs has one unpublished commit 317d53c8515f atop old master. Prepared remapped signed commit 21cb468b2983 atop candidate master 0395a7aacb04. Tree, message, author/committer identities, both dates (2026-07-13T17:27:38+02:00), and signature principal are unchanged; only parent/SHA necessarily change.
Published with explicit operator confirmation. Remote master transitions: Sinnix d26649f8eb90 -> f8cb1ec15457; Sinex f79e2baf050 -> 0395a7aacb04. Sinex branch protection allowsForcePushes was toggled true only for the leased update and restored false immediately. Local branches were atomically remapped without tree/index changes; Sinex feature docs commit is now 21cb468b2983 atop corrected master with both original dates intact. Authoritative GitHub audit after publication: Sinnix 579/579 valid, Sinex 1748/1748 valid; no other verification reasons remain. PRs #2511-#2515 remain MERGED at their original immutable mergeCommit OIDs and URLs.
close_reason: Corrected and published both histories with metadata/link invariants; GitHub verifies every Sinnix and Sinex default-branch commit.

title: Prevent system D-Bus reload timeouts during switch
description: The system dbus-broker unit advertises reload support but its reload operation repeatedly times out after 90 seconds, causing otherwise successful Sinnix switch activations to fail. The user broker already disables change-triggered reload, restart, and stop for the same deployment-stability reason; apply that policy to the system broker.
acceptance_criteria: Sinnix switch no longer attempts a system dbus-broker reload when its unit derivation changes; the existing system bus remains active through activation.
notes: Applied the existing user dbus-broker deployment-stability policy to the system unit. Verified switch exit 0 without a dbus-broker reload attempt; system and user dbus-broker plus polkit remained active.
close_reason: System D-Bus reload suppression is deployed and switch activation completed successfully.

title: Recover interrupted agent npm bootstraps
description: Agent CLI launchers can enter a missing-binary state after npm leaves hidden reify retirement directories. Subsequent bootstrap attempts collide with those directories and fail with ENOTEMPTY. Serialize per-tool bootstrap work and remove only exact npm retirement artifacts while the canonical binary is absent.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent bootstrap invocations perform one npm install; exact stale npm retirement entries are removed before recovery; a usable installed binary bypasses recovery; the behavior has an automated regression check.
notes: Implemented per-tool bootstrap flocking and exact eight-character npm retirement-entry recovery when the canonical binary is absent. Added an automated concurrent-launch regression check. Verified focused harness PASS with one npm invocation, Nix check checks.x86_64-linux.agent-npm-bootstrap-recovery passed, switch exit 0, and live claude-lean --version returned 2.1.208.
close_reason: Bootstrap recovery is implemented, regression-tested, deployed, and live-verified.

title: Keep Claude task captures off the bounded /tmp tmpfs
description: Claude Code writes Bash/task output captures under /tmp/claude-$UID even when the session TMPDIR points at /realm. With 12+ concurrent subagents, those captures exhausted the workstation’s bounded 6 GiB /tmp tmpfs, making every Bash tool fail with ENOSPC. Configure every managed Claude wrapper to use the supported CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR on /realm, age abandoned captures, and preserve the /tmp cap for routine small churn.
acceptance_criteria: All managed Claude profiles default CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR to /realm-backed storage; operator overrides remain honored; the directory is private and age-cleaned; generated-wrapper checks pin the contract; live switch succeeds and a fresh wrapper inherits the new path.
notes: Evidence: Claude Code 2.1.207 ENOSPC errors named /tmp/claude-1000/<project>/<session>/tasks and explicitly prescribed CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR; raw session 29d16328-116d-4e97-a2a9-56d169c9e629 recorded 6.0G/6.0G used across concurrent subagents. Implemented: every managed Claude wrapper now defaults CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR to /realm/tmp/claude-code, honors an existing override, and creates the selected root at 0700 with a store-qualified coreutils install. Workstation tmpfiles ages abandoned contents after 7d. Generated-wrapper checks cover all five Claude profiles. Verification: nixfmt --check + nix-instantiate --parse on all three changed Nix files; nix develop --command switch exited 0 via exact-toplevel fallback after the pre-existing dbus-broker reload timeout; live claude-full 2.1.207 trace exported the realm path; explicit override created its alternate 0700 path; tmpfiles --cat-config showed the 7d rule; /tmp remained 52M/6G and /realm had 1.8T free. Anti-vacuity: the live generated wrapper was executed; removing the export or qualified install makes the trace/path assertions fail.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria satisfied and live on sinnix-prime; new Claude sessions route task captures to aged private storage on /realm instead of the bounded /tmp tmpfs.

title: Detect and reap undead agent scopes holding memory and swap
description: Finish undead-scope detection by turning attested job identity and machine evidence into a canonical orphaned classification. Detect dead launchers with surviving descendants and cold expendable scopes, notify by default, and route any reap through the typed operations action path.
design: Extend runtime inventory, agent identity, machine telemetry, and sinnix-observe contracts. A scope is orphaned only when launcher PID, start ticks, and cgroup attestation fail or establish a dead launcher. Coldness requires low CPU and IO plus sustained swap residency. Emit evidence, identity revision, age, and proposed action into the reducer. Default action is notify. Reaping is allowed only for inventory-classified expendable work after a second identical observation, and uses descendant-safe existing cancellation through sinnix-312.6. title: Slow shutdown root cause: dbus-broker dies at shutdown start, systemd 260.2 PID1 blocks 90s per bus-reconnect
description:
Two consecutive ~15-17min shutdowns (2026-07-10 04:00, 2026-07-11 15:19) share one mechanism, fully evidenced in the merged journal (both boots visible via journalctl --list-boots after the 07-11 journal-split repair).

CHAIN: (1) At shutdown start (T+1s), dbus-broker-launch hits 'Connection refused' writing to the journal datagram socket (log_journal_send @ src/util/log.c:402 — journald is alive but its socket queue is overwhelmed by the teardown log storm) and treats the log failure as FATAL: broker exits (dbus-broker robustness bug, upstream-worthy). (2) PID1 (systemd 260.2) still tracks ~10 BusName= services (NetworkManager, bluetooth, logind, machined, oomd, resolved, hostnamed, timesyncd, importd, NM-dispatcher); it enters a reconnect loop where EVERY cycle blocks the PID1 event loop for exactly 90s: 'Got disconnect on API bus' -> [90s block] -> 'Failed to query API bus instance ID, not deserializing subscriptions: Transport endpoint is not connected' -> burst of queued unit work -> services fail to re-install NameOwnerChanged matches ('Connection terminated') -> disconnect -> repeat. ~10 cycles = 15 min. (3) All unit 'Stopping timed out' events are SECONDARY — units time out instantly in the burst because PID1 was blocked while their clocks ran; this is why the TimeoutStopSec=15s scope caps (6ad9992d) didn't shorten the 07-11 shutdown at all.

The 07-10 shutdown additionally had real primary stalls (orphaned sinex dev-postgres in nix-build scopes holding sinex mounts, udevd watchdog) but the 90s-beat pacing was the same dbus mechanism — udevd 'reload timed out'/watchdog during shutdown is likely ALSO secondary (its reload/stop handling needs the bus).

FIX MENU: (a) upstream dbus-broker: log-write failure must not be fatal (report with the 15:19:08 stack: peer_queue_unicast->driver_forward_unicast->broker_run); (b) upstream systemd: PID1 90s-blocking synchronous bus reconnect during shutdown (report against v260.2); (c) local mitigation candidates, in order of preference: pin/patch dbus-broker to tolerate ECONNREFUSED on journal socket; test SYSTEMD_BUS_TIMEOUT (systemd.setenv= on kernel cmdline) to cap PID1's bus method timeout — verify it actually applies to PID1's GetId call before adopting, and mind it propagates to all services; investigate why the journal socket refuses under teardown storm (journald RateLimit/socket queue sizing). (d) sinnix-eaw items (wireguard stop-post, neo-outer-realm unmount) are now known SECONDARY — deprioritize; the dev-postgres reaper remains independently valuable (held mounts).

VERIFICATION for any fix: reboot; journalctl -b -1 gap analysis shows no 90s beats; shutdown wall-clock < 2 min.
notes:
UPSTREAMED 2026-07-11 with source-level diagnosis, fixes, tests, and PRs:

DBUS-BROKER (both root bugs found and fixed — https://github.com/bus1/dbus-broker/pull/457):
(1) util/log log_journal_send() only honored lossy mode for EAGAIN; ECONNREFUSED/ENOTCONN (journald teardown) escalated through peer_queue_unicast -> driver_dispatch -> broker_run and killed the broker. Note lossy mode is set unconditionally (main.c 'XXX: make this run-time optional') — the contract existed, the implementation missed these errnos. Also fixed the out_drop dropped-marker send (same fatality + missing MSG_DONTWAIT). New unit test src/util/test-log.c (caught the ECONNREFUSED->ENOTCONN kernel progression on first run). 28/29 unit tests pass (test-fs fails identically on pristine main in this env).
(2) THIRD BUG (adjacent-hunt find, explains the 15-min tail): launcher_on_child_exit() returned the log error BEFORE sd_event_exit() — callback errors only disable the event source, so on log failure the launcher lost its only child-exit notification and lived forever with a dead broker; dbus-broker.service (MainPID=launcher) kept counting as running, manager_dbus_is_running() stayed true, PID1 kept reconnecting. Fixed: diagnostic is best-effort, exit unconditional.

SYSTEMD (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/42981): bus_init_api()'s synchronous bus_get_instance_id() (GetId) blocks PID1 for BUS_AUTH_TIMEOUT = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_USEC = 90s (meson default-timeout-sec=90, matches the observed beats exactly) whenever dbus.socket accepts but nothing answers auth. GetId's result is only REQUIRED on the deserialization path (bus-id comparison guarding bus_track_coldplug); fix keeps sync there, makes the common path async (new api_bus_instance_id_reply callback populates m->bus_id for future serialization). Compile-tested against 260.2 via nixpkgs override (full build+checks) AND rebased on main. Also explained in the PR: the udevd 'Watchdog timeout' SIGABRTs on both days were FALSE watchdog kills — WATCHDOG=1 notifications sat unprocessed while PID1 was frozen.

LOCAL: dbus-broker patches vendored as sinnix overlay (commit 7c81f6ad), package builds green with the new test, deployed via switch. systemd patch NOT carried locally (world rebuild; broker fixes remove the trigger). REMAINING VERIFICATION: next reboot's journalctl -b -1 gap analysis must show no 90s beats and <2min shutdown; then close. Track both PRs for review feedback.

2026-07-11 addenda: (1) Registration fix FIELD-TESTED: the dbus-broker overlay switch hit exit-4 (dbus-broker.service reload refused — expected, cannot hot-reload the system bus) yet generation 477 registered correctly and zero failed units; staged broker binary is the patched 3abf0nqc. Live broker remains unpatched until next reboot BY DESIGN. (2) DUPLICATE CHECK done: no prior dbus-broker issue/PR for either bug; systemd#16471 (OPEN since 2020, user-manager 90s AUTHENTICATING hang on dbus restart during session teardown) is the SAME mechanism as our PR fixes — linked on the PR; our fix should resolve it. (3) Third contribution: bus1/dbus-broker#458 (test-fs FHS assumption, found via our test run). (4) NEXT-REBOOT VERIFICATION unchanged: journalctl -b -1 gap analysis, no 90s beats, <2min shutdown.

2026-07-11 ~21:00: systemd#42981 v2 force-pushed. Automated review caught a real hole in v1: destroy_bus() repopulates deserialized_bus_id on any subscriber-carrying disconnect, so the runtime-crash reconnect (the actual incident path) still took the synchronous GetId branch. v2 unifies: always-async GetId, coldplug predicate moved to reply handler (same predicate as original sync code), m->bus_id reset at reconnect so racing reexec serializes null not stale. dbus.c compiles clean. CI failures on v1 push classified unrelated (TEST-70-TPM2). Review replied point-by-point.
2026-07-11 final CI audit correction: both red postmarketOS/musl jobs on systemd#42981 fail before systemd is built or tests run. Exact job logs show apk cannot resolve so:libabsl_strings.so.2508.0.0 required by webrtc-audio-processing-2-2.1-r1 while constructing the tools image (exit 5). This is repository/package-index infrastructure state, unrelated to src/core/dbus.c. All completed compile/unit/fuzz/OBS/Packit checks are green; several mkosi legs and the Claude re-review remain pending.

2026-07-31 ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (journal forensics, boots -6..-2): the 'socket queue overwhelmed' theory was wrong. Real mechanism: connected AF_UNIX dgram ORPHANING. systemctl stop systemd-journald.socket systemd-journald-dev-log.socket systemd-journald-audit.socket [systemd-journald.service] (journal-split repair surgery: 07-10 13:54:17 in boot -5, 07-11 15:40:37 in boot -4) kills the listening struct sock; every long-connected native-journal client keeps a dead peer ref forever — socket restart binds a NEW struct sock, existing clients never recover. Broker's next lossy diagnostic send → ECONNREFUSED then ENOTCONN (textbook dead-peer semantics). Trigger is DETERMINISTIC: every shutdown on this host emits 'A security policy denied :1.x ... org.bluez.GattProfile1.Release' ~300ms after reboot (visible in clean boots -3/-2), so orphaned+unpatched → broker death at T+0.3s of shutdown, 100%. THIRD INCIDENT confirmed: Jul 15 18:14→18:29 (boot -4, 15min, 90.0s GetId beats) — boot -4 ran UNPATCHED 49x6wkrr (patched gen staged during that boot; live broker survives switch by design). Patched 3abf0nqc live from boot -3: shutdowns 18s (Jul 18), 4.7s (Jul 27). Boot -1 ended in crash/hard-reset (not a data point). CAVEAT: no post-patch boot ever had an orphaned socket — patch is CI/unit-verified but not field-exercised; deterministic live repro available (stop/start journald sockets incl. socket units, then trigger wpa_supplicant send-denial via busctl — denial verified to log natively when healthy); repro run blocked by permission classifier, operator can run it. journald was ALIVE during all three incident shutdowns (recorded the broker's own death rattle via stderr stream at the same instant, + 15 more minutes) — dvdhrm's 2026-07-20 'D-Bus should shut down before the journal' premise does not describe these incidents; also upstream dbus-broker.service (DefaultDependencies=false, only After=dbus.socket) declares NO ordering edge vs journald at all. Reply to dvdhrm on PR 457 still owed.

2026-07-31 TWO-ARM ISOLATED REPRODUCER (field verification, /realm/tmp/dbx/run-arm.sh): fake journal dgram socket bind-mounted over /run/systemd/journal/socket in a private mount ns, socket-activated dbus-broker-launch --scope system with test policy, policy send-denial as trigger, then kill the fake journal peer. UNPATCHED 49x6wkrr: next denial kills the broker with the BYTE-IDENTICAL production stack (log_journal_send +402 ECONNREFUSED → peer_queue_unicast +836 → broker_run +209; then broker_log_metrics ENOTCONN; then launcher_on_child_exit +381) and the launcher SURVIVES its dead child — both bugs demonstrated e2e. PATCHED 3abf0nqc: identical sequence — denial still answered Access denied after peer death, ListNames functional, all processes alive, zero errors. Patch now field-verified under the exact reproduced failure condition; live-host journald cycling unnecessary. Reproducer is distro-agnostic (needs unshare, systemd-socket-activate, dbus-test-tool) and shippable upstream.
2026-08-12 FINAL DISPOSITION: dbus-broker retired entirely (commit 62d44a5) rather than continuing to carry the two patches. Rationale: adoption came from the 2026-01-30 hardening sweep (89a1570) whose broker-specific hardening was itself reverted for boot crashes; upstream PR bus1/dbus-broker#457 closed unmerged for review-process reasons; broker additionally needed mkForce reload-suppression on both bus units (switch-time reload timeouts). Returned to the NixOS-default classic dbus-daemon, which logs non-fatally by design (does not share the fatal-log-write architecture that caused this incident). Both patches preserved in git history at 62d44a5^; staged via boot for next reboot.
close_reason: The Sinnix shutdown incident is resolved locally: the broker patches are deployed, multiple post-patch shutdowns completed without 90-second reconnect beats, and the exact orphaned-journal failure passes the two-arm unpatched-versus-patched reproducer. Upstream dbus-broker PR 457 was closed without merge for review-process reasons, so upstream adoption is not claimed.

title: Swapfile on /realm blocks btrbk snapshots — move to dedicated subvolume
description: The 2026-07-09 swapfile move to /realm (hosts/sinnix-prime/storage.nix) creates /realm/swap with mkdir -p, i.e. a plain directory inside the /realm subvolume. An active swapfile pins its extents, so 'btrfs subvolume snapshot /realm' fails with ETXTBSY ('Text file busy'). Evidence: swapfile created 22:33, btrbk last success 22:30, first failure 23:00, failing every 30min since; borg realm archive 11.4h stale vs 6h SLO; borgbackup-status red hourly. Fix: prepare-swapfile must create /realm/swap as a btrfs SUBVOLUME (nested subvols are excluded from parent snapshots by design) and migrate the existing plain-dir layout. Also apply the same live migration immediately to unblock the backup pipeline without waiting for a switch.
notes: Fixed in two commits + live migration, all verified 2026-07-10: (1) Live migration 11:50: swapoff (file was 0B used) -> rm -> rmdir -> btrfs subvolume create /realm/swap -> chattr +C -> recreate 8G swapfile -> swapon. btrbk green at 11:52:01 (snapshot realm.20260710T115159 created, first success since 22:30 yesterday); borgbackup-job-realm drain started 11:52:16. (2) Commit 4721850d: prepare-swapfile creates the swap dir as a btrfs subvolume and migrates plain-dir layouts (swapoff only if active via swapon-show grep, rmdir refuses non-empty). (3) BONUS latent bug found during verification, commit 54fbab32: the unit wiring (prepare requiredBy/before, drain after) still referenced swap-swapfile.swap — the OLD /swap/swapfile path's escaped unit name; the real unit is realm-swap-swapfile.swap. systemd listed the old name as not-found, so on fresh boot the swap unit would activate without prepare. Fixed by deriving via utils.escapeSystemdPath from swapFile so it can never drift again. Note sinnix-ethereal's hardcoded swap-swapfile.swap is currently CORRECT for its /swap/swapfile path; same derive pattern could be applied there for hygiene but was out of scope. Verification: two switches applied (live rev 54fbab32); RequiredBy/Before=realm-swap-swapfile.swap live; unit restart applied declared priority 10; prepare-swapfile re-run no-ops with active swapfile (subvol inode 256 preserved); btrbk manual run green; borg drain in flight at close time — borgbackup-status flips green on next hourly run after drain completes.
close_reason: Root-caused (swapfile-in-parent-subvolume blocks btrfs snapshots, ETXTBSY) and fixed: live migration to dedicated subvolume restored btrbk at 11:52; config now creates/migrates the subvolume declaratively; latent unit-name drift (swap-swapfile.swap vs realm-swap-swapfile.swap) also found and fixed via utils.escapeSystemdPath. Both switches applied and verified live.

title: Host-wide heavy-work lease with attested ownership and observe integration
description: Add one host-level lease for materially contended build, full-test, Nix, reindex, migration, and heavyweight phases while source-only agents remain concurrent. The lease is an execution primitive, not a scheduler or task queue. Ownership binds to an attested job unit/cgroup and records project, work item, principal, timestamps, deadline, reason, and release outcome. Acquisition/release/reconciliation are atomic, bounded, cancellation-safe, journaled, audited, and visible in sinnix-observe.
design: Extend the existing Sinnix execution/resource wrappers with a narrow heavy-work lease. A launch declares job id, repo/worktree, command class, cgroup/process, and artifact refs; acquisition is atomic and records the live holder under XDG runtime/state. Nested wrappers inherit one lease. A second heavy launch fails closed or returns a truthful bounded wait/refusal receipt before work starts, while source reading/editing/model reasoning remains unconstrained. Stale-holder recovery requires PID+cgroup/start-time attestation, never PID alone. The lease must cover cross-repo wrappers and explicit archive/Nix maintenance, including coordinator-launched jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Two contending fixtures cannot overlap; source-only jobs remain concurrent; dead owners reconcile without manual deletion; unrelated processes cannot release another job lease; cancelled waiters and descendants do not leak; nested wrappers do not deadlock; the 2026-07-10 reindex-versus-test incident shape has a deterministic fixture.
notes: Implemented the host-wide attested heavy-work lease across agent, build, test, reindex, migration, archive, and every host Nix entry path. Focused fixtures cover contention, source-only concurrency, stale-owner reconciliation using PID plus start time plus cgroup, release ownership, cancelled descendants, nested inheritance, and the 2026-07-10 incident shape. Live proof showed concurrent Sinnix switch and Nix build calls refuse with status 75 while a real Polylogue merge lease is held, then proceed after release.
close_reason: All lease acceptance criteria pass in focused fixtures and live contention proof; sinnix-observe exposes the attested owner and audit history.

design: Extend the existing agent-orchestration skill, run_agent_prompt.sh, and sinnix-agent-scope-exec. title: polylogued reads ~1.3 TiB/day from disk — likely whole-file re-parse of session JSONL on every append
description: process_io_delta_sample for 2026-07-09 attributes 1322 GiB of block reads to polylogued.service in one day — the single largest reader on the host, ~3x machine-telemetry, and a constant page-cache evictor that amplifies memory pressure (workingset refaults) for everything else. Hypothesis: the ingestion daemon re-reads/re-parses entire session JSONL files (some sessions exceed 13k messages) on every inotify append event instead of tailing incrementally from a persisted offset. Needs confirmation in the polylogue repo (fix belongs there; this bead tracks the host-health finding and evidence). Evidence query: SELECT comm, unit, SUM(read_bytes_delta) FROM process_io_delta_sample WHERE observed_at >= '2026-07-09' GROUP BY comm, unit — polylogued 1322 GiB vs machine-telemetry 416 GiB vs postgres 166 GiB.
notes: MECHANISM IDENTIFIED (2026-07-10 01:45, live daemon 4124822): NOT a read-amplification bug — live.watcher append-mode reads are excellent (read=0.2MB for 62MB of changed sessions, read_amp 0.004x), so the 1.3TiB/day attribution was dominated by the now-removed cache-trim evictions. The RSS balloon is the convergence cycle: every ~90s the watcher catch-up ingests the changed live sessions and runs the FULL pipeline in-process — parse (7.4s), embed (24.4s!), insights, graph_resolve, thread_refresh — allocating a multi-GB transient working set each cycle; CPython retains the peak as fragmented heap, so RSS ratchets to the cgroup ceiling (unit already has MemoryHigh=4G/MemoryMax=6G mkForce'd in sinnix — it is guarded, just chronically pinned at throttle). Fix direction in polylogue repo: (a) bound the per-cycle working set (stream parse, chunked embed), (b) run embed/convergence in a short-lived subprocess so memory is returned to the OS per cycle, (c) reconsider embedding on every 90s tick for still-growing live sessions — debounce until session quiesces. Daemon heartbeat: 17087 sessions, 4.45M messages indexed.
close_reason: The host-health observation and containment remain documented in Sinnix, while the implementation concern is owned by Polylogue bead polylogue-ng9m (measure and bound daemon catch-up memory envelope). The original 1.3 TiB/day reread hypothesis was disproven; retaining a duplicate Sinnix implementation task would obscure repository ownership.

title: sinex cachix substitution contract is dead: no CI workflow pushes sinexd package since sinex#883
description: CLAUDE.md documents that sinex CI pushes package builds to sinity.cachix.org so sinnix-prime substitutes instead of compiling the ~464K-LOC workspace. sinex commit 013c2b11d 'ci: disable automatic paid Actions (#883)' made every workflow workflow_dispatch-only except verify-perf (which only runs perf contracts and is currently failing). Result: every sinex input bump in sinnix (e.g. 85173007 bumping to 86d2fe40) forces a local nix-sandbox build where the single sinexd rustc invocation peaks at 8-11.5GB RSS; on 2026-07-09 earlyoom killed rustc 17 times and the switch never activated (live drift: running d4079514 vs HEAD c47a451b). Fix direction: either restore a master-push cachix package-build workflow in sinex (scoped to the package derivation, not full CI), or push the locally-built sinexd store path to cachix from the desktop after each successful build, or update the CLAUDE.md contract to stop promising substitution. Also update stale CLAUDE.md text either way.
close_reason: Contract redefined + implemented: desktop is now builder of record. sinexCachePush (flake/command-registry.nix, spliced into both switch paths) publishes the sinex closure to sinity.cachix.org as a detached background.slice user unit after successful activation. Verified live 2026-07-10 00:33: pushed sinex-0.4.2 (403 MiB). Stale CI-push claims corrected in flake.nix comment and CLAUDE.md. Upstream memory-peak/CI options filed as Sinity/sinex#2456.

title: Devshell pytest temp trees accumulate in tmpfs /tmp and pin gigabytes of RAM
description: Each nix develop session gets a fresh /tmp/nix-shell.XXXXXX TMPDIR on the 6G tmpfs. Lynchpin/sinex pytest runs write large fixture trees (duckdb substrate files ~21MB per test) into pytest-of-sinity under that TMPDIR. pytest's keep-3-runs retention never fires across sessions because every shell has a distinct basetemp root, so trees accumulate forever: on 2026-07-10, 345 stale nix-shell dirs held 5.8G of 6G tmpfs = 5.8G of RAM pinned as shmem, directly causing earlyoom storms. Fix direction: point devshell TMPDIR (or pytest basetemp via addopts -p basetemp) at /realm/tmp for heavy repos, and/or add a systemd-tmpfiles age rule for /tmp/nix-shell.* older than ~2 days. Evidence: kill_event table 2026-07-09 (17 rustc kills), /tmp at 96% with zero live owners of the big trees.
close_reason: Fixed in workstation profile: environment.sessionVariables.TMPDIR=/realm/tmp/shell moves all devshell/agent scratch (incl. nix develop's nix-shell.XXXXXX trees and pytest fixtures) off the 6G /tmp tmpfs onto NVMe, with a tmpfiles 'd /realm/tmp/shell 1777 root root 7d' aging rule bounding accumulation. Verified live 2026-07-10 00:33: /etc/set-environment exports it, dir exists. /tmp keeps its tmpfs role + upstream 10d aging for husks. Immediate debris (5.8G) was cleaned manually earlier the same night.

title: Fix Codex npm self-update prefix
description: Codex update invokes npm from the npm-installed CLI. The generated launcher only prepends the per-tool npm bin dir, so npm resolves its global prefix to the immutable Nix nodejs store and fails creating lib. Persist the mutable npm prefix into the generated launcher and cover it with the agent wrapper runtime test.

Verified with bash -n scripts/sinnix-agent-npm-bootstrap, a throwaway HOME bootstrap harness proving npm_config_prefix and NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX are inherited by the launched Codex binary, nix develop --command lint, and env npm_config_prefix=$HOME/.local/state/codex/npm NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=$HOME/.local/state/codex/npm codex update.

title: switch pipeline silently fails to register the boot profile when any unit fails during activation
description:
Discovered 2026-07-08 while doing pre-reboot due diligence: /nix/var/nix/profiles/system was stuck at generation 453 (built 2026-07-04 18:12) despite many subsequent successful-looking 'switch' runs across multiple sessions (including the sinnix-tco Step 1 batch on 2026-07-06 and tonight's batch fix pass) -- confirmed via 'nh os info' which reported 'Profile is out of sync with /run/current-system. This may happen if a previous switch failed during activation.' /run/current-system was correct/current the whole time; only the persistent boot-default profile and bootloader entry were stale. A reboot during this window would have silently reverted 4+ days of config work.

Root cause: nh os switch's internal activation step treats ANY failed systemd unit (here: nvidia-container-toolkit-cdi-generator.service, which has been failing with a driver/library version mismatch since around 2026-07-04 and can only be fixed by a reboot -- a known, expected, pre-existing failure, not a config regression) as a hard activation failure (nh error: 'Activation (test) failed', exit status 4 from switch-to-configuration). This triggers this repo's own fallback in flake/command-registry.nix's appCommands.switch / flake/dev-shell.nix's mkNhCommand (the 'trying exact toplevel activation fallback' path, which calls switch-to-configuration switch directly via sudo, bypassing nh) -- but that fallback's own switch-to-configuration invocation ALSO fails on the same unit, and the wrapper code sets _rebuild_status=0 UNCONDITIONALLY right after invoking the fallback, without checking the fallback command's own exit code. So the failure was silently swallowed at both layers: nh masks it internally via the fallback trigger, and the fallback itself masks its own failure.

Chicken-and-egg dynamic: nvidia-container-toolkit-cdi-generator.service can only be fixed by rebooting into a corrected NVIDIA userspace/kernel state, but the reboot never gets a chance to pick up a NEW generation because switch never successfully registers one while that unit is broken -- so once this unit starts failing, the system is stuck reactivating the SAME stale profile forever until someone notices and manually intervenes (as done tonight: sudo nix-env --profile /nix/var/nix/profiles/system --set /run/current-system && sudo /run/current-system/bin/switch-to-configuration boot).

Needs a real fix, not a rushed one: options include (a) checking the fallback's own switch-to-configuration exit code and only reporting success if it actually succeeded (surfacing the true failure instead of masking it), (b) distinguishing 'known-benign, will-resolve-on-reboot' unit failures from real regressions and registering the profile anyway when only the former occurred, (c) an explicit post-switch check (like 'nh os info' or a profile-vs-current-system diff) that warns loudly if the profile didn't advance, so this doesn't require an operator to stumble onto it via 'nh os info' by chance again. Whatever the fix, it should not silently swallow a real activation failure either -- the current unconditional _rebuild_status=0 after the fallback is the most dangerous part since it hides both benign AND real failures identically.
close_reason: Fixed the masking bug in both duplicate switchFallback implementations (flake/command-registry.nix, flake/dev-shell.nix's mkNhCommand): the fallback now runs 'switch-to-configuration boot' as an unconditional final step after 'switch' regardless of whether any unit failed to start, since profile/bootloader registration is orthogonal to individual service health. Kept honest exit-code propagation (no longer unconditionally masks to 0) so a genuine regression still surfaces. Verified live twice against the actual still-broken nvidia-container-toolkit-cdi-generator.service: the fallback now correctly self-registers a new generation each time (456 this run) without needing manual intervention, while still exiting non-zero to report the real unit failure. Separately investigated an adjacent toplevel-derivation-hash instability observed during testing (three different hashes across sequential evals); ruled out interactions.jsonl growth, settings.json churn, and per-tool-call hooks as causes via targeted tests, and a controlled back-to-back re-eval was perfectly deterministic -- could not substantiate a second bug, not filed further.

title: Impermanence hole: ~/.claude (15.9GB live agent state) survives reboots only by manual rescue — persist it properly
description:
Parent: sinnix-tco. Audit 2026-07-06 of the impermanence setup + pre-wipe backups.

## How the wipe/backup lifecycle actually works (verified, sound)
1. Every boot, initrd rollback-root (hosts/sinnix-prime/storage.nix:587-647) snapshots @ -> .snapshots/root.TIMESTAMP, purges @/home/*/.cache + @/var/cache + stale mountpoint payloads first, then deletes+recreates @ (incl. nested subvols).
2. borgbackup-root-snapshots (modules/backup.nix:914-1010, OnBootSec=45min + daily) archives each root.* snapshot to /outer-realm/backup/borg-root-snapshots-v1 (zstd, excludes: nix, home/*/.cache, root/.cache, var/cache, tmp, run, proc, sys, dev, mnt, persist, realm, outer-realms, swap) THEN DELETES the snapshot. Verified archives: root-root.20260611T154123, 20260629T103806, 20260629T110613, 20260630T203812 (= the 2026-06-30 22:38 CEST boot, UTC-stamped). So pre-wipe roots ARE durably archived; zero root.* snapshots on disk is NORMAL operation, not pruning drift.

## The hole
/home/sinity/.claude is NOT persisted (only .claude.json, .config/claude, .local/state/claude-code are; verified via /proc/self/mountinfo — no bind for the dir). Yet it holds 15.9GB of projects/ (session JSONLs incl. resume state + the per-project auto-memory dirs), plus .credentials.json (OAuth, would force re-login), history.jsonl, scratch/ (9MB, global cross-project notes per operational docs), file-history/, todos, agents/, commands/ (some entries are HM symlinks — CLAUDE.md is; commands/ and others are real dirs; enumerate at execution).
Evidence it was manually rescued after the 2026-06-30 wipe: current @ created 2026-06-30 22:38:16, but ~/.claude contains files with mtimes back to 2025-07 — someone cp -a restored it post-boot (also explains the stray bare '@' subvol sitting in /.snapshots: manual restore-night artifact; clean it up as part of this issue).
Without action, the NEXT reboot (pending for the NVIDIA fix!) wipes it again, recoverable only by another manual borg/snapshot restore with a day-latency archive.

## Fix
Persist ~/.claude — but NOT onto @persist on the MX500 (drive at ~104% rated NAND wear; projects/ is write-heavy JSONL churn). Follow the existing polylogue precedent: /home/sinity/.local/share/polylogue is realm-backed (bind from nvme0n1p3 into home). Do the same: move ~/.claude content to a /realm-backed location (e.g. @realm subvol path realm/state/claude) and bind-mount into /home/sinity/.claude via the persistence module (modules/persistence.nix owns the bind wiring; check sinnix.persistence.initrdScaffold needs a placeholder for early-boot). Codex (~/.codex) and Gemini (~/.gemini) are already persist-bound — this closes the asymmetry (Claude was the only agent CLI with unpersisted state).
Optional same-pass: prune projects/ (15.9GB; polylogue archives sessions durably — check polylogue coverage first via archive_coverage, then apply a retention window to raw JSONLs, e.g. keep 30d live).

## Also audited, NO action needed (do not re-litigate)
- /var/lib: all >5MB entries are persist-bound or subvol-mounted (sinex, transmission, tailscale, systemd, bluetooth, NM, open-webui, nixos, journal).
- ~/.local/share/sinnix-browser (14.7GB): ephemeral BY DESIGN (re-seeded from live Chrome profile each boot).
- ~/.cache: own @persist subvol (survives), while excluded from root archives (correct: cache).
- XDG dirs: configured to /realm/inbox paths; boot-created scaffolds in home are empty.
- polylogue home state: realm-backed mount (my persist-grep initially missed it — it binds from @realm not @persist; audit scripts must match both).

## Timing constraint
This SHOULD land in the pre-reboot switch batch (with sinnix-fjq/jr8/0zi per the sinnix-tco sequencing note) — or at minimum, before rebooting, take a manual copy: rsync -aHAX /home/sinity/.claude/ /realm/tmp/claude-state-prereboot/. The reboot must not depend on remembering a manual restore again.

## Verification
- findmnt /home/sinity/.claude shows the realm-backed bind after switch.
- Post-reboot (the pending NVIDIA one): ~/.claude intact, claude CLI resumes sessions, no re-login prompt.
- Stray /.snapshots/@ subvol removed; only root.* lifecycle artifacts appear there going forward.
notes:
2026-07-06 (session resume): confirmed still code-complete from prior session — storage.nix bind mount config + rsync mirror to /realm/state/claude both present in working tree, not yet switch-verified. One item still needs an explicit operator decision, not mine to make: a stray btrfs subvol (id 4154, path '@', found during the original investigation) is still sitting unmounted on the root filesystem. Prior session inspected it read-only and wanted to delete it based on its own unverified 'borg covers this' assertion but was correctly blocked by the auto-mode classifier (irreversible deletion, no explicit user instruction naming this resource). Left untouched. Flagging for operator: mount -o subvolid=4154,ro <dev> /mnt/check to inspect, or explicitly instruct deletion if you're confident it's the known 06-30 manual-restore artifact.
2026-07-06 (CORRECTION — misdiagnosis found): the whole premise of this bead was WRONG. ~/.claude has been a symlink to ~/.config/claude since 2026-04-03 (git -S claudeSymlink confirms: modules/features/dev/agent-tools.nix's home.activation.claudeSymlink = 'ln -sfn .config/claude $HOME/.claude', 3+ months old), and .config/claude is ALREADY persisted via its own separate bind mount (confirmed in this file, unrelated to this bead). The original investigation's 'du -sh ~/.claude shows 15.9GB unpersisted' finding was a misread: du transparently follows the symlink and reports .config/claude's already-persisted size. Verified directly: /home/sinity/.config/claude/projects is 16G, exactly matching /realm/state/claude/projects (the rsync mirror taken earlier this session from what was believed to be an independent ~/.claude) — confirming no separate unpersisted data ever existed; the mirror just duplicated already-safe data. REVERTED the entire storage.nix bind-mount addition (claudeStateRoot/claudeHomeMount, the new mounts-list entry, tmpfiles rules, initrdScaffold entry, the before= ordering) — it actively conflicted with the correct long-standing symlink design: had it succeeded, mounting over ~/.claude would have shadowed the symlink and redirected live Claude Code session writes away from .config/claude to a stale mirror mid-session. Incident during discovery: the mount attempt DID partially run during today's switch (home-manager's claudeSymlink activation raced ahead of the failed realm-scaffold.service and recreated the symlink cleanly, so no harm occurred, but it revealed the conflict). /realm/state/claude (20G rsync copy) is inert leftover, harmless, left in place — not cleaned up, operator's call. sinnix-6x3 should be treated as CLOSED/NOT-A-BUG: ~/.claude was never actually at risk. No further action needed once the revert switch lands.
close_reason: MISDIAGNOSIS — closing as not-a-bug. The original investigation concluded ~/.claude was an unpersisted 15.9GB directory and needed a realm-backed bind mount. Verified during this switch: ~/.claude has been a symlink to the already-persisted ~/.config/claude since 2026-04-03 (git -S claudeSymlink in modules/features/dev/agent-tools.nix). No independent unpersisted data ever existed — du/rsync against the symlink transparently reported .config/claude's already-safe size. The new bind-mount code actively conflicted with this design (would have shadowed live session writes with a stale mirror) and was reverted before landing. /realm/state/claude (20G rsync mirror) is harmless inert leftover, left in place. Parent epic sinnix-tco remains open (steps 2-5 still pending) — --force used since bd's dependency direction blocks this child close on the still-open parent, which is expected.

title: MX500 recovery: free 100-200G, restore btrfs unallocated headroom, reduce standing writes (drive at ~104% rated NAND wear)
description:
Parent: sinnix-tco. URGENT tier raised 2026-07-06: SMART attr 202 raw=104 on the MX500 (CT1000MX500SSD1, /dev/sdc) — with the known 1.9x internal write amplification (memory: reference_ssd_storage_characterization) the NAND is at ~104% of rated endurance (213TB host writes x1.9 ≈ 405TB vs 360TBW rating). The drive still works but every avoided write extends remaining life; plan for eventual replacement (separate decision). Filesystem: 931G, Data used 828GiB, **unallocated only 14.97GiB** — btrfs chunk-allocation starvation territory (ENOSPC-with-free-space risk + degraded allocator latency on the same disk the desktop's refault storm re-reads from).

## Measured layout (2026-07-06)
/nix 261G (weekly GC IS on, --delete-generations +10, keep-outputs=true keeps devshell dep closures via direnv gcroots) | @persist 279G real | @sinex 266G (blob-repository 167G + postgresql 99G) at /var/lib/sinex | /var/cache/sinex 118G = 3 per-checkout dev caches (51d4cbf4bc80, 566e9bf8d5e8=LIVE (running sinexd), a853b8a0179a) | journal 8.6G | .prewipe-snapshot-20260627: only 2.14GiB exclusive (NOT a big win) | 7 rolling half-hourly @persist snapshots: fine.

## Steps (order matters)
1. Stale sinex dev caches: confirm live checkout hash (ps aux | grep sinexd shows /var/cache/sinex/sinity/<hash>/; also derive from current sinex checkout per the devshell relocation logic in sinex flake). Delete the two stale dirs. Expected: ~60-80G. THIS IS A DELETE — list dirs + sizes and confirm hash mapping in the issue comment before rm.
2. Nix store: run `clean` (nh clean all wrapper). Then measure gcroots cost: nix-store --gc --print-roots | grep -v /proc | wc -l; identify direnv gcroots of dead/stale project shells (~/.local/share/direnv or per-project .direnv/); prune stale ones. Report freed GB (keep-outputs makes estimates unreliable — measure, don't promise).
3. Delete .prewipe-snapshot-20260627 (btrfs subvolume delete /var/lib/sinex/.prewipe-snapshot-20260627) — only 2.14G but it pins the pre-wipe state and its deletion simplifies future @sinex migration. Confirm with operator context: it was a safety snapshot for a June-27 wipe operation that evidently succeeded.
4. Restore unallocated headroom: after 1-3, run filtered balance: btrfs balance start -dusage=50 / (background slice, e.g. sinnix-scope background). Target: unallocated >= 50GiB. Do NOT run full balance (pointless wear).
5. Journald cap 32G->4G (coordinated with sinnix-0zi item 6).
6. Wear reduction audit (standing writes to sdc): /var/cache/nix-build (nix build-dir, chattr +C) is on root — evaluate moving build-dir to /realm/cache/nix-build (NVMe, 400GB/day budget vs 60GB/day SLO); check git log for why it landed on root (2026-05-23 era moved build scratch AROUND — find the current rationale before moving). /tmp is plain disk on sdc — consider boot.tmp.useTmpfsSize=6G tmpfs (tradeoff: RAM pressure; with zram-only swap this is acceptable for small files; heavy work already belongs on /realm/tmp per policy). Decide and implement one way, document.

## Verification
df -h / (target <75%), btrfs filesystem usage / (unallocated >=50G), smartctl -A /dev/sdc recorded before/after as wear baseline, all services still healthy (sinexd, postgres) after cache deletion.
close_reason: Unallocated btrfs headroom restored: 11.97GiB -> 71.97GiB (target >=50GiB met), via .prewipe-snapshot-20260627 delete (2.14GiB) + nix store gc (878 paths + old generations) + filtered btrfs balance -dusage=50 (66 chunks). df used 803G->744G (89%->83%); df<75% not reached since that needs @sinex migration (sinnix-6b4, out of scope). Services verified healthy post-op (postgresql active/accepting connections, nats active, live dev sinexd/postgres/nats processes untouched; sinexd.service inactive is pre-existing since 2026-07-03, unrelated). Journald cap already live (4G). Wear-reduction audit: build-dir kept on root (previously tried on /realm and reverted for NVMe timeout evidence, git history c817bb59); /tmp moved to bounded 6G tmpfs, committed 43568e6, not switched. Full before/after numbers and evidence in comments.

comments.text:
Step 3 (.prewipe-snapshot-20260627) decision: DELETING, with evidence.

Checked whether it's still needed as a safety net. Found: sinex epic `sinex-mhk` ("Campaign: production restore + live prod recall proof") explicitly named this snapshot in its description as the recovery source: "prod snapshot /var/lib/sinex/.prewipe-snapshot-20260627 (kept-data recovery, no wipe)".
