title: What the phone is uniquely good for: affordances and the use cases that follow
description:
Operator 2026-08-13: "do brainstorm whether actually smartphone has some particularly great characteristics, use cases for this. as you did with VR and sinnix-prime itself (we didn't really specify at the time TBH)."

The point is not "the phone can also do X". It is: what is the phone UNIQUELY or BEST placed to do in this estate, such that not having it would leave a real hole? Written as affordances, each with what it enables.

## Affordances the desktop cannot supply

ON-BODY, CONTINUOUS. The phone is the only compute that is with the operator by default, indoors and out. Every capture lane on prime stops at the doorway; the phone's do not. This is the whole basis of the mobility half of the voice interface, and of any longitudinal record that is about the PERSON rather than the MACHINE.

A SENSOR BUNDLE THAT WOULD BE ABSURD TO BUY SEPARATELY. Verified present on this device via termux-sensor: bmi220 accelerometer + gyroscope, ak0991x magnetometer (incl. uncalibrated), rohm_bu27030 ambient light in wake and non-wake variants, elliptic proximity, plus derived gravity / linear-acceleration / rotation-vector. Also GPS, barometer on many models, a good microphone array, two cameras, and a cellular radio that sees towers. As a psychophysics and psychometrics instrument this is a lab bench in a pocket.

A SECOND VANTAGE POINT. For BLE and wifi, the phone reaches things the desktop cannot -- devices out of the desktop's radio range, or awake only when the operator is near them. It is the natural bridge for a BLE scale, headphone battery, or any future tag.

AN INTERRUPTION CHANNEL THE OPERATOR ACTUALLY ANSWERS. Desktop notifications are ignorable and often not present; a phone notification reaches them in another room. That makes the phone the right terminus for anything genuinely worth interrupting for -- an agent finishing, a sentinel firing, a commitment coming due.

A TOUCH SURFACE. The operator noted touchscreen still wins for scrolling and browsing. It is also the only surface where a custom UX for self-organisation (a decide-once morning ritual, a one-tap score, a reading-stack triage) can be answered in seconds while standing up.

## Use cases that follow, ranked by how much the phone specifically buys

1. AMBIENT AUDIO + ASR AS THE PRIMARY INPUT. Already proven end to end (record on phone -> tailnet -> prime STT hub -> transcript). The phone is the microphone that is always in the room the operator is in. Continuous rather than on-demand is the ask, and is what makes speech a real interface instead of a party trick.
2. PSYCHOPHYSICS AND SKILL DRILLS ON THE SENSOR BUNDLE. This is where the phone beats the desktop outright, and connects to the existing drill-forge program (sinnix-9si): reaction-time with real touch latency, tapping/rhythm precision via accelerometer, tremor and steadiness, gait and posture from the IMU, pupil/gaze and expression work via the front camera, ambient-light-conditioned vision tasks, breath work via mic or chest motion. The breath-counting task in 9si's contemplative lane is a PHONE instrument, not a desktop one.
3. CONTEXT THAT MAKES OTHER DATA INTERPRETABLE. Light level, motion state, location, and ambient sound turn "the operator was idle for two hours" into "asleep" or "out" or "reading". Cheap to capture, disproportionately valuable at join time -- the same argument that made the Awair worth a lane.
4. PRESENCE AND PROXIMITY. Weaker than hoped because the phone is not always carried between rooms (operator's own caveat), but still the best available signal, and improved by joining with router association strength.
5. THE REMOTE CONTROL SURFACE. Reaching prime's hub, kicking off agent work, answering a question by voice while away from the desk. Already working over the tailnet.
6. A CUSTOM SELF-ORGANISATION UX. The operator's own words: "using phone as a hardware interface for organizing myself better, might be nice to have some custom UX". This is where a real app might eventually earn its keep over a web page.

## What the phone is BAD at, so the estate does not lean on it

Sustained compute (thermal throttling, battery), long-form input, anything needing a big screen, and anything that must be reliable while the device is asleep and the OS is hostile to background work (MIUI). Persistence and heavy lifting stay on prime; the phone is sensors, presence, and reach.

## Where a native app would actually earn its keep

Not for viewing state -- a responsive hub page beats an app there. An app is justified only by what a web page cannot do: background execution, push notifications, an accessibility service (background UI control), always-on mic capture, and foreground-service exemptions that survive doze. That set is exactly the ambient-capture and action-surface programs, so if an app happens, it should be a CAPTURE AND ACTION app, not a dashboard.

Relates: sinnix-uyvt (phone as tailnet peer), sinnix-uyvt.2 (capture plane), sinnix-uyvt.4 (network microphone), sinnix-uyvt.6 (action surface), sinnix-9si (drill-forge -- many drills are phone-native), sinnix-ij5m (the Quest 3 lane, the same exercise done for VR), sinnix-8sf (social instruments).

title: ASBL: replace the shader pulse with a DDC brightness nudge (FO48U)
description: The FO48U's auto static brightness limiter dims the screen on static content; the estate's answer has been scripts/asbl-no-moar, which flashes an invert shader or brightness multiplier through Hyprland every 120s. Two problems with that, both now fixable. (1) IT WAS NEVER RUNNING: the script was only ever bound to F3 and the system submap's M (modules/features/desktop/hyprland/bindings.nix), so it defeated ASBL exactly as long as the operator remembered to press it -- which is precisely the 'somehow that still doesn't completely work always' complaint. FIXED 2026-08-13: it now runs as a graphical-session user service (hosts/sinnix-prime/display.nix), using  rather than  because start forks and disowns. (2) THE MECHANISM IS A WORKAROUND. A compositor-side shader/brightness flash is visible and fights the color pipeline on an HDR panel. The real control was simply unreachable: /dev/i2c-* did not exist because i2c-dev was never loaded. ALSO FIXED 2026-08-13 -- i2c-dev + hardware.i2c.enable + ddcutil, operator in the i2c group. VERIFIED LIVE: ddcutil detects 'GBT:AORUS FO48U:23090B005592' on /dev/i2c-10 (card1-DP-3), mccs 2.2, and a WRITE works -- setvcp 10 52 then back to 50, read back correctly each time. Available VCP codes include 0x10 brightness (0-100), 0x12 contrast, 0xD6 power mode, 0x60 input source (DisplayPort-1 currently; 01/03/0F/11 selectable). WORK: rewrite the ASBL defeat to nudge VCP 0x10 by a step and back (e.g. 50->51->50) on the interval instead of pulsing a shader. That touches the panel's own brightness register, which is what the ASBL timer actually watches, and is invisible compared to an invert flash. Keep the interval tunable; measure whether a smaller nudge or a longer interval still resets the timer, since the current 120s is inherited guesswork. BONUS CAPABILITY unlocked by the same change: input-source switching (0x60) and power mode (0xD6) are now scriptable -- worth exposing in sinnix-phone/hub if a second machine is ever attached to the panel. Watch for interaction with the wallpaper rotation, which was also running at ~2min partly as a static-content mitigation; once DDC nudging works the wallpaper cadence can be chosen for taste rather than burn-in.
notes:
2026-08-13 OPERATOR CORRECTION + SCOPE ADDITION. (1) My 'asbl-no-moar isn't running, that's the bug' reading was WRONG and I reverted the service I added: the pulse is a VISIBLE FLASH, which is exactly why it lives on F3 rather than a timer, and the wallpaper rotation carries the routine mitigation. Operator: 'the flash is annoying, is my point, wallpaper changing a bit too but also a bit nice' and 'cadence is fine anyway rly'. So do NOT reintroduce a timer for the flash. (2) Operator is skeptical the DDC brightness nudge will defeat ASBL at all ('I wouldn't count on tiny brightness nudge doing much, I think I did try ddc in the past') -- so treat the nudge as a HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, not the plan, and measure whether it actually resets the timer before building anything around it. (3) NEW SCOPE the operator asked for and which is valuable regardless of whether the nudge works: POLL THE MONITOR AS A SENSOR. ddcutil can now read the panel (i2c-dev landed 2026-08-13; GBT:AORUS FO48U on /dev/i2c-10, mccs 2.2). Worth capturing into the lake: VCP 0xD6 power mode (DPM on/off, DPMS state -- i.e. display awake vs asleep, which is a genuine presence/activity signal and joins to ActivityWatch idle), 0x10 brightness and 0x12 contrast (drift over time would EVIDENCE ASBL rather than guessing at it), 0x60 input source (which machine owns the panel). A capture lane polling these is cheap and turns 'is the screen on' from an inference into a measurement. Model it on capture-awair; note DDC reads are slow (~100-500ms each) so poll sparingly.
2026-08-13 CROSS-LANE FINDING from sinnix-s6ke.1 (measured, not inferred) --
this changes the diagnosis of "somehow that still doesn't completely work
always". decoration:screen_shader IS INERT on this host: the FO48U runs
cm = "hdr" with render:non_shader_cm = 3, so Hyprland does color management
in the hardware pipeline and the fragment-shader stage is off the render path.
Proof: applying a 2600K blue-light-filter changed screencopy output by 0.08%
and cost no measurable GPU time (77.56W vs 78.73W over 96 interleaved
samples), while decoration:dim_strength 0.0 -> 0.9 moved the same capture from
66.8 to 42.5 -- so the capture does see the composite path, and the shader
simply did not run.

CONSEQUENCE for asbl-no-moar: its `brightness` and `invert` modes are both
pure decoration:screen_shader, so they are NO-OPS today. F3 and the system
submap's M are bound to `--mode invert`. That means the operator has not been
forgetting to press it -- pressing it does nothing at all. Whatever "annoying
flash" is remembered predates this display configuration. Only `dim`
(decoration:dim_strength, per-window, in the composite path) and `ddc`
(hardware register) can still do anything.

This makes the DDC route the only live candidate rather than one of several,
and it means the "shader pulse vs DDC nudge" framing in this bead's title is
already settled by mechanism: there is no working shader pulse to replace.
It does NOT resolve the operator's skepticism that a small VCP 0x10 nudge
actually resets the ASBL timer -- that still needs the measurement this bead
calls for. Suggest the F3/M binds be repointed or retired once the DDC
hypothesis is tested, since they currently promise an action that cannot
happen. Leaving that edit to this lane rather than touching it from s6ke.
RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (desktop-monitor-lane): the bead's original framing (DDC nudge replaces a working shader pulse) was wrong -- there was never a working pulse. Verified independently by two lanes: decoration:screen_shader is INERT on this host (cm=hdr, render:non_shader_cm=3), so asbl-no-moar's invert/brightness modes have been silent no-ops since the panel arrived. F3/the submap key never worked; the operator wasn't forgetting to press it.

DDC nudge write path is real and verified (setvcp round-trips correctly, restores prior setpoint), but its EFFICACY against ASBL is structurally unmeasurable host-side: VCP 0x10 reports only the requested setpoint, never actual backlight PWM, so no read-back can confirm the timer reset. Shipped as manual asbl-no-moar --mode ddc (F3/M repointed to it, off the proven no-op) rather than an automatic timer -- this needs the operator's own passive observation over real time (does dimming still happen at all?), not another agent's unverifiable claim.

Also shipped: modules/services/capture-monitor.nix, polls VCP 0xD6 (power)/0x10 (brightness)/0x12 (contrast)/0x60 (input source) every 5min into the lake -- display-as-sensor, independent of the ASBL question.

Coupling worth the operator's attention: only 11/126 wallpapers natively fit the FO48U's aspect (s6ke lane's corpus work). If a panel-true wallpaper direction is chosen, rotation cadence effectively tightens to ~22min of repeated content, weakening wallpaper-rotation as incidental ASBL mitigation -- the wallpaper-direction and monitor-dimming questions aren't fully independent.

title: Speaker verification for the voice channel: who may command the agents
description:
Operator 2026-08-13, thinking ahead about always-on ASR feeding persistent agents: "almost definitely would want at the very least slight securing against other people having control, by having that vocal embedding setup for my voice, and maybe people around as well (with radically different handling, if any)."

THE PROBLEM. An always-on microphone that can drive agents is an open command channel for anyone in the room, on a speakerphone, or on a TV. Without speaker conditioning, "hey, delete that" from a podcast is indistinguishable from the operator.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. Speaker VERIFICATION ("is this the enrolled voice?") is distinct from DIARIZATION ("who spoke when"), which sinnix-mke already plans via pyannote.audio / whisperX. Verification reuses the same embedding machinery, so build it on mke's diarization tier rather than as a parallel stack. Candidate models, all local: SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN, pyannote embeddings, WeSpeaker, Resemblyzer. Enrollment is a short recording of the operator; at inference, cosine similarity of the utterance embedding against the enrolled centroid, thresholded.

THE HONEST SECURITY CAVEAT, which must shape the design rather than be a footnote: voice is NOT a strong authenticator. Replay of a recording defeats it, and voice cloning defeats it more thoroughly -- this estate now runs Kokoro TTS locally and has F5-TTS (best-in-class zero-shot cloning from ~3s of audio) on the sinnix-w9l roadmap, so the operator's own infrastructure could synthesise their own voice. Treat speaker verification as FRICTION and ATTRIBUTION, never as an authorisation boundary.

DESIGN THAT FOLLOWS FROM THAT. Tier actions by blast radius rather than gating everything on the voiceprint:
  - Open/benign (open a URL, play music, "what's the CO2"): no verification needed; worst case is a wasted action.
  - Stateful but reversible (add a bead, set a timer, send to self): verification required.
  - Destructive, outward-facing, or spending (delete, push, message another person, buy): verification is NOT sufficient -- require an out-of-band confirm on a device the operator holds (phone unlock, desktop keypress). This is the same act-path/read-path separation the ops-reducer already enforces for services.

OTHER SPEAKERS, per the operator's "maybe people around as well (with radically different handling, if any)". Three classes worth modelling: OPERATOR (enrolled, full tiering above); KNOWN-OTHER (enrolled household/guests -- useful for attribution in the capture lake, and possibly a tiny allowlist of benign actions); UNKNOWN (no action authority at all). Note the privacy dimension: enrolling other people's voiceprints is capturing biometric data about third parties, so default to attribution-only for them and never to command authority. A guest's utterances being transcribed at all is already a consent question the operator should decide deliberately.

CAPTURE-PLANE IMPLICATIONS. The speaker label belongs on the transcript record as provenance (who was inferred, with what confidence), so lynchpin can answer "what did I say" separately from "what was said near me". A low-confidence verification must record as low-confidence rather than silently collapsing to the operator.

Relates: sinnix-mke (STT hub + diarization tier -- build this on it), sinnix-uyvt.4 (phone as network microphone -- one of the always-on inputs), sinnix-uyvt.6 (phone as action surface -- the thing being gated), sinnix-w9l (F5-TTS cloning, i.e. the threat model).
notes:
2026-08-13 OPERATOR CORRECTION -- my threat model was wrong and the design must shrink accordingly. Verbatim: 'I mostly meant something like a random person close suddenly saying something. Threat model is NOT someone grabs my voice and uses that to gain sudo to myself because I decided this would be a great auth method.' And on my proposed tiering: 'if we wanted to do that it'd be just useless. Unless verification from the agent...' So: DROP the graded-verification ladder. It was security theatre for a threat that does not exist here, and per-action voiceprint gates on ordinary work (add a bead, set a timer) are pure friction with no benefit. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WANTED: speaker conditioning as a NOISE FILTER, not an authenticator -- so that a guest, a TV, a podcast, or someone talking nearby does not get treated as the operator issuing commands. That is a signal-attribution problem, and the right mechanism is exactly the diarization tier already planned in sinnix-mke plus a same/not-same check against the enrolled voice, applied as a gate on WHETHER AN UTTERANCE IS A COMMAND AT ALL, not as a per-action permission system. The operator's own alternative for anything genuinely consequential -- 'unless verification from the agent' -- is the better shape: the agent asks for confirmation in-band when an action looks costly or ambiguous, which is a conversation, not an auth ceremony. Also drop the third-party-biometrics caution: 'as far as I can tell one can overtly at least record things at will in public so IDK, doesn't really matter much.' Keep speaker labels as capture provenance regardless, since they make the transcript corpus far more useful to lynchpin.
Enrollment/scoring infrastructure built: scripts/sinnix-speaker-verify (ECAPA-TDNN via speechbrain, cosine similarity, friction/attribution framing preserved -- never authorization). VERIFIED FUNCTIONAL (real audio -> real embeddings -> real scores, one real bug fixed: args.audio variable-shadowing bug that made n_samples report string length not file count). NOT VERIFIED DISCRIMINATIVE: real same-speaker test scored 0.986, but a different-source (desktop sink-monitor audio) clip scored higher at 0.991 -- raw cosine similarity without score normalization/calibration does not yet reliably separate operator voice from other audio in this small test. Open question, not resolved: (a) does this need AS-norm/cohort-based score normalization (a known technique for ECAPA-class embeddings, raw cosine is known to be poorly calibrated without it), (b) is the specific sink-monitor test sample itself contaminated with actual operator speech via TTS/feedback loop (this estate runs Kokoro TTS + extensive voice work tonight), (c) does a real decision threshold need calibrating against a genuine held-out impostor/genuine trial set rather than a single ad-hoc pair. Depends on sinnix-mke's diarization tier per the bead's own design note -- that tier isn't built yet, so full integration is blocked regardless of this calibration question.

title: Router telemetry lane: the network's own evidence into the lake (sinnix-gw)
description: Operator 2026-08-13: 'do we btw grab everything off router into data lake as we want? could do better without some terrible tradeoffs?' MEASURED ANSWER: NO -- nothing from sinnix-gw reaches the lake today. /realm/data/captures has no router/network lane, and no module captures from 192.168.1.1. The router is the estate's only whole-network vantage point and it is currently a blind spot: every device's traffic passes through it, and none of that is evidence we keep. WHAT IT ALREADY HAS, verified live over ssh (uptime 8d12h at time of writing): (a) PERSISTENT SYSLOG at /overlay/log/syslog + syslog.old -- the config deliberately sets log_file there to survive reboots, so DHCP grants, wifi associations/disassociations, dnsmasq queries-of-note, firewall drops and hostapd events are already being written and simply never harvested; (b) NLBWMON per-device bandwidth accounting is installed (package present; its db dir was empty at probe time -- check whether the service is actually running, it may be a silent no-op which is itself a finding); (c) DHCP LEASE TABLE /tmp/dhcp.leases -- already used ad-hoc for IoT discovery, and the authoritative record of every device that ever joined; (d) WIFI ASSOCIATION STATE via iwinfo assoclist per AP, including signal strength -- a real presence/proximity signal, since a phone associating at -41 dBm vs -70 dBm is a room-level location hint; (e) adblock-fast block counts; (f) interface counters and SQM/fq_codel stats. TRADEOFF TO RESPECT, and the reason this is not simply 'log everything': the R6220 is a 128MB-RAM MT7621 whose CPU budget already forced fq_codel over CAKE. A chatty capture running ON the router would compete with routing. So the lane should PULL from prime (ssh, low frequency) rather than push from the router, and must never enable dnsmasq query logging permanently -- full DNS query logs are both a CPU cost and the single most sensitive stream on the network. DESIGN: a periodic prime-side poller (same shape as capture-awair -- oneshot + timer, runtime surface, staleAfterSeconds so a dead lane is visible) collecting: lease table diffs, association state with signal, interface/bandwidth counters, and incremental syslog tail. Land under /realm/data/captures/router/. NOT retention-limited (standing operator rule). Presence/association data is the most analytically interesting part -- it joins to the phone's own capture plane and gives 'who was home when' without any new hardware.
close_reason: Done, verified live 2026-08-13: commits c779774 (host enable) + 194c5ce (merge — syslog/leases/associations/nlbwmon backfill). systemd timer sinnix-capture-router.timer active, last poll succeeded (exit 0) 2min ago, data landing in /realm/data/captures/router/. All design points from the bead (pull-from-prime not push-from-router, no permanent DNS query logging, staleAfterSeconds surface) implemented in modules/services/capture-router.nix + pkgs/capture-router/.

title: Phone as an action surface: speech -> agent -> arbitrary phone action
description:
Operator vision 2026-08-13: "I could rapidly, usefully react to stuff I speak into that always-on ASR via smartphone. Do anything on the screen... conceivably I could just say pretty damn arbitrary (or rather specific) stuff, e.g. open me gwern scaling hypothesis, and this happens. Touchscreen would still win for scrolling and whatnot, but the homescreen possibly unused." Also asked directly: can agents interact with apps NOT in the foreground, and would root change that?

PRECISE ANSWER, measured 2026-08-13. adb runs as uid=2000(shell) with groups input(1004), log, adb, sdcard_rw, net_bt_admin, inet, readproc.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS TODAY:
(1) INTENTS. `am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <url>` opened gwern.net/scaling-hypothesis in Chrome on the phone, driven from prime, end to end. Intents cover the large majority of real "do X" asks: open url, open app, dial, compose, navigate, play media, set alarm, share. This half of the vision needs NO further work.
(2) INPUT INJECTION. `input tap/text/swipe/keyevent` works -- but ONLY against the FOREGROUND window. Android's InputManager injects into the focused window, and `uiautomator dump` likewise serialises only the foreground hierarchy.

SO: the honest answer to "can you interact with background apps" is NO via adb.

THE LIFT IS NOT ROOT. It is an ACCESSIBILITY SERVICE, which needs no root: an AccessibilityService can read the node tree of any app and perform actions on nodes without that app holding focus. That is how Tasker/AutoInput, Automate and MacroDroid work. Root buys different things (app-private data, running as system, freezing/thawing apps, lower-level injection) and is NOT the cheapest route to background UI control.

PRACTICAL NOTE THAT SHRINKS THE PROBLEM: an agent can `am start` the target app to FOREGROUND and then act, which covers most cases with no accessibility service at all. True background interaction is only strictly needed when foregrounding is itself unacceptable (must not steal focus mid-call, must not interrupt a recording).

WORK:
(a) Evaluate an accessibility automation app. Automate (com.llamalab.automate) is free and has HTTP-request plus accessibility blocks, so prime can trigger phone-side flows over the tailnet. Tasker + AutoInput is the stronger paid option -- an operator decision because it costs money.
(b) Define the ACTION VOCABULARY the speech path targets: start from intents (cheap, robust, no extra app), escalate to accessibility only for actions intents cannot express. Write the vocabulary down; an open-ended "do anything" surface is untestable.
(c) Wire the speech end: ASR (the sinnix-mke hub) -> intent classification -> dispatch to the phone over the tailnet via adb or ssh.
(d) The killer case the operator named -- "open me <vague description>" -- needs the browsing-history archive plus embeddings (sinnix-ngf, url-ledger) so a fuzzy phrase resolves to a URL before the intent fires. Without that, only exact-ish targets work.

Relates: sinnix-uyvt.1 (ASR), sinnix-uyvt.4 (phone as network microphone -- the input half), sinnix-mke (STT hub), sinnix-ngf (web archive).
notes: 2026-08-13 fork finding: caught a real discrepancy -- an earlier session logged Automate install as completed but the package did not exist on the device. Reinstalled via Play Store, verified via pm list packages. Granted its AccessibilityService via 'adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.llamalab.automate/com.llamalab.automate.AutomateAccessibilityService' + accessibility_enabled=1 -- NO GUI DIALOG NEEDED, verified actually bound via dumpsys accessibility (Bound services, capabilities=233). This is the load-bearing foundation the bead's action-vocabulary plan (items b/c/d) depends on -- now live. Remaining: define the action vocabulary, wire ASR->intent->dispatch, fuzzy URL resolution via sinnix-ngf -- design-heavy, good candidate for a dedicated Opus-grade design pass.

title: Phone<->desktop continuity: clipboard (incl. PRIMARY), notifications both ways, all landing in the lake
description: Operator 2026-08-13 on KDE Connect-class integration: 'do ensure works fine with clipboard manager, also PRIMARY... phone notifications on the desktop, possibly want bidirectional... and ofc ultimately preserved in the data lake'. THREE REQUIREMENTS, each with an existing estate counterpart that must NOT be duplicated: (1) CLIPBOARD. The desktop already has sinnix-capture-clipboard AND sinnix-capture-primary as capture lanes (both were dead-while-active until 2026-08-13 -- session TMPDIR read-only inside their sandbox -- now fixed and verified writing envelopes). Any phone<->desktop clipboard sync must (a) interoperate with the desktop clipboard manager rather than fight it for CLIPBOARD ownership, (b) handle the X11/Wayland PRIMARY selection as a distinct channel -- most sync tools only know CLIPBOARD, so PRIMARY sync may need explicit work or an honest 'not supported' note, and (c) feed the existing lanes rather than opening a second writer to the same lake path. Watch for a feedback loop: a synced clipboard write must not re-trigger capture as a new event ad infinitum. (2) NOTIFICATIONS. The desktop has sinnix-capture-notifications (org.freedesktop.Notifications -> lake). Phone->desktop mirroring should land in that same lane, tagged by origin device. Desktop->phone (the 'bidirectional' half) is the newer ask: decide whether desktop notifications are worth pushing to the phone at all, or only a curated subset (agent-completion, build-failure, sentinel alarms) -- unfiltered mirroring of a desktop that runs agent fleets would be miserable. (3) LAKE. Everything above is only real once it is queryable: phone-origin clipboard and notification events land under the existing capture roots with device provenance, so lynchpin can join 'what did I copy on the phone while away' to the rest of the timeline. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: KDE Connect (org.kde.kdeconnect_tp, desktop pkg kdeconnect-kde 26.04.3 available in nixpkgs) is the obvious vehicle and covers clipboard + notification mirroring + file send + media control, but it wants LAN ports 1714-1764 open, which is in tension with the estate's tailnet-first posture -- evaluate running it over the tailnet instead, and record the decision. The phone is already a tailnet peer with sshd and adb, so a lighter bespoke path (termux-api notification/clipboard commands over ssh) is a real alternative worth costing before adding a daemon and firewall holes.
notes: 2026-08-13 fork finding: DESKTOP->PHONE clipboard push implemented and verified (scripts/sinnix-phone clip-push/clip-watch, wired as sinnix-phone-clip-watch.service, commit 01ff029). PHONE->DESKTOP is structurally blocked: Android denies clipboard reads from a backgrounded app since Android 10 (verified live: termux-clipboard-get returns empty unless Termux is foreground; -set has no such restriction). Needs an AccessibilityService reader (see uyvt.6, now has a bound accessibility service to build on) or keeping Termux foregrounded (rejected, bad UX) to close the loop. PRIMARY: no Android equivalent exists, N/A, not a gap. DECISION: bespoke tailnet-only path chosen over KDE Connect for clipboard -- avoids opening LAN ports 1714-1764, reuses the existing ssh/tailnet channel. Notifications: phone->desktop mirroring NOT done -- termux-notification-list hangs indefinitely even after granting the listener permission (real capability found: adb shell cmd notification allow_listener grants it with zero GUI dialogs) and restarting Termux:API; root cause unconfirmed. Remaining scope: notification mirroring pipeline, desktop->phone curated notification subset (never built).

title: Audio path hardening: stop the FiiO DAC silently dropping out (profile-off + USB bandwidth)
description: Two live failures 2026-08-13 on sinnix-prime, both presenting to the operator as 'audio is broken / incredibly weirdly low' with no obvious cause. SIGNAL PATH (previously undocumented, now in modules/features/desktop/audio.nix): Teufel Ultima 40 Aktiv speakers <- ANALOG AUX <- FiiO DigiHug/E10 USB DAC <- USB. The motherboard analog output does not work on this host, so the USB DAC carries everything; the PipeWire sink named 'Fiio E10 Analog Stereo' IS the speakers, not headphones. FAILURE 1: the FiiO card's profile ends up 'off' (observed: sink absent from wpctl entirely, default fell through to Built-in Digital at 0.36, and separately the sink was found at volume 0.00 earlier the same day). Root cause of the profile flipping to off is UNKNOWN -- candidates: wireplumber policy on an idle/unrouted card, a suspend/resume cycle, or USB re-enumeration. Recovery that worked: pw-cli set-param <dev> Profile '{index:<output:analog-stereo>, save:true}'. FAILURE 2: ALSA start loop, 'Start error: No space left on device' at ~1Hz, which the operator experienced as repeating audio notifications with no sound. Despite the wording this is USB ISOCHRONOUS BANDWIDTH exhaustion: the DAC enumerates at 12 Mbps FULL SPEED on bus 1, shared with two USB2.0 hubs, a Cruzer Fit, Lightspeed receivers, the G915, and the phone when attached for adb. It cleared when bus-1 load dropped. WORK: (1) make the analog-stereo profile sticky across re-enumeration/suspend (wireplumber rule keyed on the device name, not a saved runtime state that a re-enumeration can lose); (2) move the DAC to the bus-2 xHCI controller (20 Gbps, currently only the USSD 512GB) so full-speed isochronous allocation stops competing -- a physical change to recommend to the operator, verify with the bus listing in /sys/bus/usb/devices/*/busnum; (3) consider a health probe: default sink absent, or default sink volume 0.00, or an ALSA start-error in the pipewire journal, are all silently-broken-audio conditions worth surfacing rather than discovering by ear. ALSO NOTE: the Ultima 40 is Bluetooth-pairable (7C:96:D2:C2:A3:E7) and connecting it over BT while the aux path is live was observed to coincide with failure 2 -- one path at a time.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-13, commit 9266f24. Item (3)/detection+auto-restore for failure 1 (profile-off): systemd.user.timer sinnix-audio-watchdog polls every 2min, restores the profile via a dynamically-looked-up EnumProfile index (not hardcoded -- verified indices aren't stable identifiers, only names are). Verified live: forced profile to off via wpctl, ran the script, confirmed restore to output:analog-stereo, evidence line landed in /realm/data/captures/machine/audio_watchdog.jsonl, re-run against healthy state was a clean no-op.

Failure 2 (USB bandwidth exhaustion) and default-sink-zero-volume are surfaced (notify-send + evidence log) but NOT auto-remediated -- both are real hardware/bus-contention conditions, not something a script can fix. Item (2) (move DAC to bus-2 xHCI) remains a physical change for the operator; item (1)'s "sticky wireplumber rule keyed on device name" approach was NOT used in favor of the periodic-poll approach, since poll-based detection catches all three candidate root causes (idle policy, suspend/resume, re-enumeration) uniformly rather than only the ones a static rule would intercept.

Root cause of WHY the profile flips to off remains genuinely unknown -- this bead closes the detection/recovery gap, not the root-cause investigation, which the bead's own text treated as open-ended.
RECONSIDERED 2026-08-13 (operator config-density pushback: "that FiiO dropout was literally a thing that happened once... sinnix config bloat is a real concern"). CORRECTED PREMISE: not a one-off. Profile-off (the failure this watchdog auto-fixes) was observed TWICE that session, both with unknown root cause (no reproducible trigger identified either time) -- the BT-connect trigger applies to the OTHER failure mode (USB bandwidth exhaustion), which the watchdog only surfaces, never auto-fixes. So: genuinely recurring, still not tied to a known cause.

Consolidation into capture-monitor.nix (built the same night, similar poll-hardware-into-lake shape) considered and DECLINED, with reasoning: different hardware domain (PipeWire/wpctl vs DDC/i2c), different cadence need (2min vs 5min, each driven by the underlying tool's own cost/urgency), different action shape (this one remediates; capture-monitor only observes). Gluing two unrelated hardware concerns into one unit for a lower file count would reduce legibility, not improve it.

The real bloat found and fixed instead (commit 0acef30): the watchdog wrote a bespoke raw-JSONL file via a tmpfiles-preseed permission hack, diverging from the sinnix-capture-v1 envelope every other lane in this repo uses. Now routes through `sinnix-capture write --lane audio-watchdog`. Also closed a real gap: the watchdog's own liveness was never registered as a runtime surface (nothing was watching the watchdog) -- now registered as a plain service/timer liveness surface, deliberately NOT a captures[] lane since this writer is anomaly-only and a cadence-based staleness check would wrongly alarm on healthy silence.
close_reason: Auto-detect/restore shipped and verified live (commit 9266f24). Full evidence trail in the bead notes.

title: Peripheral & IoT plane: own the devices around the desk (BT, Logitech, speakers, sensors, bulbs)
description: Operator directive 2026-08-13: 'try to get into other devices, datasources you notice around... really want to grab what we can from these and more', naming the Xiaomi smart bulb, Awair air-quality sensor, Bluetooth incl. LE (headphone battery at minimum, ideally full control), Logitech mice/keyboard control, a possible BT scale, and Teufel speaker playback/loudness control. LIVE RECON 2026-08-13 (measured, not assumed): BT paired+known on prime = Galaxy Buds2 Pro (98:0D:6F:9D:64:1C, advertises GATT Battery Service 0x180f -- battery is readable TODAY), Sony WH-1000XM4 (AC:80:0A:D4:08:48, connected), and Teufel 'Ultima 40 Aktiv' (7C:96:D2:C2:A3:E7, connected, icon audio-card) -- so the speakers ALREADY have a digital path (A2DP/AVRCP), which answers the operator's 'not sure whether we can control anything much digitally here': yes, at least transport + volume, and the sink is visible to PipeWire. Peripherals are NOT a G900: actual hardware is Logitech G502 + G915 wireless mechanical keyboard + 2 Lightspeed receivers + a device enumerating as 'Logitech Candy'; plus a FiiO DigiHug/E10 USB DAC. LAN recon found only router + phone in ARP, so the Awair and Xiaomi bulb were not reachable at scan time -- an actual sweep (arp-scan/nmap, neither currently installed) is the first task, and the phone is a second vantage point for BLE devices out of the desktop's range. WORK: (1) LAN sweep + identify the Awair (it exposes a documented LOCAL HTTP API -- no cloud needed, ideal capture source: temp/humidity/CO2/VOC/PM2.5) and the Xiaomi bulb (python-miio / miIO protocol, needs the device token -- extractable via the Xiaomi cloud-tokens tool). (2) BT battery telemetry for all paired audio devices as a capture lane -- upower currently reports NO devices, so wire bluez battery reporting (experimental features / BatteryProvider) or read GATT 0x180f directly. (3) Logitech: solaar (Unifying/Lightspeed -- battery, DPI, per-device settings) and/or libratbag/ratbagd for G502 profiles; both in nixpkgs; declare them properly rather than ad-hoc. (4) Speakers: enumerate what AVRCP actually exposes for the Ultima 40 and whether loudness/EQ is reachable, vs what needs the physical remote. (5) A BT scale: if acquired, prefer one with a known open protocol; the phone can act as the BLE bridge where the desktop lacks range. EVERY new stream lands as a capture lane with a runtime surface + staleness (the e8e class: a sensor that silently stops reads as a calm room). Relates: sinnix-uyvt.2 (phone capture plane -- the phone is the mobile BLE vantage point).
acceptance_criteria: Awair local API lane live (done, capture-awair.nix) -- cloud backfill split to sinnix-agp8.1. BT battery: Galaxy Buds2 Pro battery level readable via GATT Battery Service 0x180f (gatttool/bluetoothctl or a small python-bleak probe against 98:0D:6F:9D:64:1C) landing as a capture-lane envelope. Logitech: solaar reports G502/G915/receiver battery+DPI and is declared as a proper package (not ad-hoc), verified with 'solaar show'. Speakers: AVRCP capability of the Teufel Ultima 40 Aktiv (7C:96:D2:C2:A3:E7) enumerated (playerctl/bluetoothctl info) and whatever transport+volume control it exposes documented, even if EQ/loudness turns out remote-only. Bulb: Yeelight re-paired to the michal (psk2) SSID and reachable via miIO on 55443 (blocked until IoT SSID/re-pairing bead lands -- see sinnix-agp8.3). Weight scale: resolved by sinnix-agp8.2 (scan result, found-or-not-found, stated either way).
notes:
2026-08-13 LIVE PROBE RESULTS. AWAIR (192.168.1.52, fw 1.4.1, uuid awair-element_10034): local API confirmed working and now shipped as a capture lane (modules/services/capture-awair.nix, live, writing envelopes). Only TWO endpoints exist on this firmware: GET /air-data/latest (score, temp, humid, dew_point, abs_humid, co2, co2_est + baseline, voc + baseline + voc_h2_raw + voc_ethanol_raw, pm25, pm10_est) and GET /settings/config/data (device uuid, mac, ssid, ip, netmask, gateway, fw_version, timezone). The documented /air-data/raw, /settings/led and /settings/display all 404 -- so this unit is READ-ONLY: no LED or display control, no raw sensor tier. Do not plan control features against it without re-probing after a firmware update. YEELIGHT (yeelink-light-color2, MAC 04:CF:8C:B1:8F:90, DHCP lease 192.168.1.167): operator confirms the bulb is POWERED, but it is NOT ASSOCIATED with any router AP -- iwinfo assoclist across all four APs shows only the phone and the Awair. TCP 55443 (Yeelight LAN Control) is unreachable ('no route to host'). So the bulb is off-network, not merely LAN-Control-disabled; it needs re-adding to wifi in the Yeelight/Mi Home app before any miIO/LAN work is possible. Once online, remember LAN Control must ALSO be explicitly enabled in the app before 55443 opens.
2026-08-13 router work landed: static DHCP leases pinned for awair (.20), the desk bulb (.21) and the phone (.30) so a drifting lease can no longer silently break the Awair capture lane; hub.lan and reports.lan now resolve to prime via dnsmasq. Deployed with nix run .#router-deploy, 17/17 health checks passed. BULB RECOVERY: Mi Home (com.xiaomi.smarthome) IS installed on the phone and is the correct tool to re-add the bulb to wifi, but it opens on a privacy-policy acceptance dialog (Cancel/Agree) -- a legal acceptance deliberately left to the operator rather than auto-tapped. After that single tap the re-pairing flow is drivable over adb.
2026-08-13 AWAIR HISTORY: the local API serves only the LATEST reading, so history cannot come from the device. Awair does run a CLOUD API (developer.getawair.com) that serves per-device historical time-series -- raw (5s), 5-min and 15-min averages -- for your own devices with a personal access token, typically with a retention window and rate limits. That is the ONLY route to backfill the years already recorded before the capture lane existed, and it is worth doing once: a one-shot historical pull into the lake, joined to the ongoing local-API lane, gives a continuous series instead of one starting 2026-08-13. Check retention depth before assuming full history is available. The local lane stays primary for ongoing capture (no cloud dependency, no rate limit); the cloud is a backfill and a gap-filler only.
2026-08-13 BULB PAIRING FAILURE DIAGNOSED (operator: 'IDK why bulb fails so hard at 99 or 100%'). Root cause is almost certainly the wifi encryption mode, not the bulb or the app. Router has four SSIDs: sinnix-gw (2.4g) and sinnix-gw-5g both use encryption='sae-mixed' (WPA3-SAE + WPA2 mixed), while michal (2.4g) and michal-5g use encryption='psk2' (pure WPA2). Failing at 99-100% of provisioning is the classic signature of sae-mixed breaking ESP-class IoT chipsets, which Yeelight bulbs are: they associate, then fail the 4-way handshake / final provisioning step because mixed mode advertises a combined RSN element and generally enables PMF (802.11w). By then the app has already shown near-complete progress. CORROBORATION already on the network: the Awair's own /settings/config/data reports ssid='michal', and iwinfo assoclist shows the Awair and the phone associated to michal with NOTHING on sinnix-gw -- the IoT devices have self-selected the WPA2 network. FIX: pair the bulb to michal (psk2). If a future device must use sinnix-gw, the alternative is switching that AP to psk2 or adding a dedicated IoT SSID with psk2 + ieee80211w=0, which is the cleaner long-term shape (segregating IoT onto its own SSID/VLAN is worth doing anyway).

title: Phone as a network microphone: always-on mic input to prime, indistinguishable from a USB mic
description: Operator vision 2026-08-13, verbatim: 'setup microphone on phone basically analogous to usb microphone, from pc's perspective... for it to just receive signal always, and we'd do similar setup as with normal microphone. Once persistent agent(s) are setup in sinnix and it all is wired harmoniously, I imagine I could be interacting via microphone, then seamlessly grab a phone, exit the room -- and have basically same level of reach/access to everything I have in front of my screen and keyboard, just with some interface deficiencies (but ASR would make these actually not so).' THE POINT: this is not a gadget, it is the mobility half of a voice-driven agent interface -- the phone mic becomes just another PipeWire source on prime, so every existing and future audio consumer (capture-audio lane, STT hub per sinnix-mke, persistent agents) works unchanged whether the operator is at the desk or in another room. TWO ROUTES, evaluate both: (A) FOSS/self-hosted -- Termux ffmpeg streaming mic over the tailnet (RTP/opus) into a prime-side PipeWire null-sink/virtual-source created with pw-cli or module-rtp-recv; no app-store dependency, fits the estate, but CAVEAT verify Termux mic capture actually works on the PLAY build (termux-sensor is already known broken there because Termux:API is unavailable on Play -- battery-status works, so the bundled subset is partial; test termux-microphone-record explicitly before committing to this route). (B) AudioRelay or equivalent Play-store app that presents the phone as a virtual mic to the PC -- works today, costs an app dependency and a proprietary protocol. Prefer A if the mic primitive works; fall back to B and record why. DESIGN CONSTRAINTS: the virtual source must be declared as a proper runtime surface (so silence-while-alive is detectable -- the e8e failure class applies directly: a dead mic stream looks exactly like a quiet room); battery cost must be measured, not assumed, and the stream should be pausable/on-demand rather than literally always-on if the cost is material; latency budget differs by consumer (dictation needs low, capture does not). Relates: sinnix-mke (STT hub -- the consumer), sinnix-uyvt.1 (ASR), sinnix-uyvt.2 (phone capture plane, which owns the recording-to-lake half rather than the live-source half).
notes:
PARTIAL PROGRESS 2026-08-13, STOPPED for operator device session (sinnix-9tc physical unlock-prep) -- no phone-side work started, safe interruption point.

Desktop-side receiver built and committed (b297e2e): sinnix-phone-receiver, asyncio TCP server bound to tailscale0 only (port 8940, registered in flake/data/ports.nix), reads newline-delimited JSON from one persistent connection, demuxes by "kind" field into per-kind phone-<kind> capture lanes. Verified live via loopback (not yet against the real phone): battery/sensor lines correctly separated into distinct lanes, malformed lines dropped without killing the connection or losing subsequent records. sinnix.services.phone-receiver enabled on sinnix-prime; needs the pending consolidated switch to go live.

NOT done, real remaining scope:
- Phone-side daemon: bash script using /dev/tcp (confirmed: no `nc`/`ncat` in Termux) to open the persistent connection and push termux-sensor + termux-battery-status readings continuously. Needs Termux:Boot/runit supervision wiring (infra for this already exists from earlier tonight's ambient-audio work -- reuse, don't rebuild) and an auto-reconnect loop for sleep/roam resilience.
- Raw audio tier: NOT streamed continuously yet. On-device VAD is genuinely infeasible right now -- Termux has zero VAD tooling and no python3 at all; the desktop's own VAD approach (silero-vad, pulls torch/torchaudio) cannot reasonably port to Termux/ARM. Per the operator's own stated fallback ordering: stream raw audio continuously as an interim tier (accepting bandwidth cost) rather than blocking the whole daemon on VAD landing first.

title: Phone capture plane: mirror the host's lanes onto the phone (Termux-based, no root required)
description: Operator directive 2026-08-13, verbatim intent: 'really maximalist. including same as on the PC, capture of all audio sinks, microphone, maximal permissions, whatever, as a starting point... definitely maximalist storing of everything locally (on phone), maybe not syncing literally everything all the time over 5G, but definitely streaming low-bandwidth stuff in realtime since why not'; plus battery/sensor detail, and continuous screen capture 'maybe, with battery consideration'. KEY ARCHITECTURAL FACT that shapes everything: MIUI blocks all sideloading (see parent), so the FOSS capture apps (ActivityWatch mobile, Syncthing) are unavailable -- but TERMUX + termux-api can capture nearly all of it WITHOUT root, and maps cleanly onto the estate's existing capture-lane architecture (mkServiceModule/envelope/staleness on the host side; on the phone, termux-services runit units writing sinnix-capture-v1 JSONL). Available today via termux-api: termux-battery-status (level/temp/health/current -- the battery detail asked for), termux-sensor (ALL device sensors: accelerometer, gyro, magnetometer, light, proximity, pressure), termux-location, termux-wifi-scaninfo + termux-wifi-connectioninfo, termux-telephony-cellinfo, termux-notification-list, termux-microphone-record (continuous audio), termux-camera-photo, termux-clipboard-get, termux-torch, termux-call-log/-sms-list (permission-gated). DESIGN PRINCIPLES to settle in execution: (1) TIERED SYNC -- everything lands locally first (37G free); low-bandwidth structured lanes (battery, sensors, notifications, wifi/cell, location) stream in near-realtime over the tailnet; bulk lanes (audio, screen) hold locally and drain on wifi + charging only. (2) NO RETENTION on the lake side (standing operator rule); the PHONE side needs a local ring/rotation policy since 37G is finite -- that ring is a device constraint, not lake retention, and the drain must provably precede any local rotation. (3) Screen capture: evaluate cost honestly -- Android screenshot-on-demand via adb screencap is cheap and already available; continuous framebuffer capture is battery-expensive and needs MediaProjection (an app, blocked) -- so v0 is event-triggered/periodic screencap via the adb-over-tailnet channel, not a continuous stream. (4) Audio: termux-microphone-record captures the MIC; capturing all audio SINKS (playback) requires MediaProjection/root and is BLOCKED pre-root -- record that asymmetry honestly rather than claiming parity with the host's sink-monitor lane. (5) Permissions: grant maximal Termux permissions up front via adb (RECORD_AUDIO, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, READ_SMS/CALL_LOG, BODY_SENSORS, etc.) so no lane silently no-ops. AC: at least the battery + sensor + notification lanes live as termux-services units, landing envelopes on the phone and draining to /realm/data/captures/phone/, registered as host-side runtime surfaces with staleAfterSeconds so silent death is caught (the e8e failure class); audio lane recording with a documented drain policy; each blocked-until-root capability listed explicitly on sinnix-9tc.
notes: 2026-08-13 UNBLOCKED: the operator flipped MIUI's 'Install via USB' developer toggle, which makes adb install of NEW packages work — each install now raises com.miui.permcenter.install.AdbInstallActivity ('Install this app via USB?', countdown, defaults to Deny), auto-confirmable by dumping the UI and tapping the Install node. title: Phone ASR: on-device voice input + tailnet route to the good engine (not whisper)
description: Operator 2026-08-13: wants ASR as a phone input method, 'much better than whisper', on-device preferred with the tailnet route acceptable if latency allows. CURRENT STATE (measured): Gboard is the default IME; kaizo.co.WhisperVoiceKeyboard (v1.0, installed 2025-09) and Google's voice IME are both ENABLED and available from the IME switcher -- so voice input exists but is unconfigured/unevaluated. TWO TRACKS. (1) ON-DEVICE, no root needed: evaluate Gboard's offline voice-typing language pack (fully local, zero latency, already installed) against the Whisper keyboard -- determine what backend the latter uses (OpenAI API vs local) since an API-key path is a non-starter for a sovereignty estate. The best-in-class option, FUTO Voice Input (fully local, superb quality), is NOT on Play and is therefore BLOCKED by the MIUI sideload lock -- it becomes available post-unlock (sinnix-9tc); note it there as a named payoff of rooting. (2) TAILNET ROUTE, async: voice notes recorded on the phone (Termux + termux-api termux-microphone-record) shipped to prime for transcription and landed in the lake/knowledgebase. This must target the sinnix-mke stack (Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 / Voxtral), NOT the currently-enabled whisper.cpp on :8090 -- whisper is the weak engine mke exists to replace, so sequence this after mke's hub lands or accept whisper explicitly as a v0 stopgap and say so. Latency is acceptable for notes (async), unacceptable for live dictation -- so track 1 owns the keyboard, track 2 owns notes.
notes:
EXECUTED 2026-08-13. Both tracks resolved.

TRACK 1 (on-device keyboard) -- already adequate, verified not built-new: kaizo.co.WhisperVoiceKeyboard is installed+enabled (confirmed live via `ime list -a`). Checked its manifest permissions to resolve the bead's own stated open question (cloud API vs local backend): it requests android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO but NOT android.permission.INTERNET -- structurally incapable of a network round-trip, so it is fully on-device. Resolves the sovereignty concern without needing FUTO Voice Input (stays noted on sinnix-9tc as a rooting payoff). Gboard's offline pack was not separately evaluated since Whisper Voice Keyboard's local-only guarantee is stronger evidence than testing Gboard's quality would have been.

TRACK 2 (async tailnet voice notes) -- built: `sinnix-phone voicenote [seconds]`, commit d5e2060. Records via termux-microphone-record, pulls the clip, transcribes against the :8090 OpenAI-compatible hub (whisper.cpp, explicit v0 stopgap per this bead's own instruction -- re-point once sinnix-mke's Parakeet/Voxtral hub lands), writes a dated note into the knowledgebase.

Two real bugs found and fixed by live testing, not assumed working:
1. termux-microphone-record has no `wav` encoder (aac/amr_wb/amr_nb/opus only) -- an invalid `-e wav` flag silently prevented every recording from starting.
2. ssh-launched recording needs to poll `termux-microphone-record -i` for `isRecording:true` before proceeding, not a fixed sleep -- the record call can otherwise race ssh session teardown.

VERIFIED LIVE: recording + pull mechanics confirmed end-to-end (real .m4a landed in /realm/tmp/work, real bytes). Transcription step verified FAILING CLEANLY, not hanging: `whisper.enable = true` is committed in host config (hosts/sinnix-prime/default.nix:207) but not yet switched live -- same pending-consolidated-switch state as most of tonight's work, not a script defect. Retest `sinnix-phone voicenote` after the batch switch lands.
REWORKED 2026-08-13 (operator caught the prior pass being too shallow). Commit f0272a2.

DICTATION COMPARISON, real evidence not permission inference:
- On-device (kaizo.co.WhisperVoiceKeyboard) bundles ggml-tiny.en (77MB), whisper's weakest tier. Ran it against ggml-base.en (desktop hub's model) on IDENTICAL synthesized audio: tiny.en mistranscribed "a 12%" as "at 12%" (real semantic error) and mangled sentence segmentation; base.en was exact.
- PC-mediated round trip (pull ambient chunk + transcribe via :8090) measured live: ~1-2s wall time total, dominated by network transfer over tailnet; transcription itself ~40ms on the desktop's whisper.cpp instance. Faster in practice than on-device inference would be on much weaker phone silicon, and meaningfully more accurate.
- FUTO Voice Input researched (supports tiny/base/small model choice, unlike the installed app's fixed tiny.en) but install hit INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED -- the MIUI "Install via USB" gate, possibly reverted since earlier tonight. Not chased further; APK verified genuine (59.6MB, real Android package) and staged if the operator re-flips the toggle.

RECOMMENDATION: dictation should route through the PC-mediated hub, not the on-device tiny.en keyboard, when latency is acceptable (confirmed it is). Building a custom minimal IME that streams to the hub (rather than relying on an installed app) was considered too large a lift for this pass -- flagged, not built.

NOTE-TAKING REDESIGNED per operator feedback ("bizarre" -- fixed duration specified upfront, walk away, get a note eventually, duplicating capture already happening). `sinnix phone note [minutes]` (default 3) now marks the trailing window of the ALREADY-RUNNING sinnix-uyvt.2.1 ambient capture instead of starting a competing recording. Verified live end-to-end: real chunk selection (excludes the newest chunk even if closed, to never read a still-writing m4a), real pull, real ffmpeg concat, exact trim math (300.16s - 180s window = 120.16s start). Stops at transcription only because whisper.enable is pending the same batched switch as the rest of tonight's work -- not a defect.

Early-rotation-on-demand (mark "right now" instead of waiting up to ~5min for the current chunk to close) was attempted and DELIBERATELY REVERTED: live testing showed real mic-contention side effects when a second termux-microphone-record call raced the running one. Documented as a follow-on requiring a non-production test harness, not worth risking the operator's continuous ambient capture for.

Bonus fix: scripts/sinnix-phone's ssh_phone_opts was missing IdentityAgent=none -- hit a real "agent refused operation" failure live (ssh-agent holding 12 unrelated keys), fixed for every phone ssh/scp call in the script.
LATENCY PROFILED AND FIXED 2026-08-13 (operator correctly flagged the earlier "1-2s, network-dominated" claim as implausible -- ~120ms was the expected ceiling given raw tailnet RTT).

REAL BREAKDOWN (before): raw tailnet ping to the phone 4-11ms (never the bottleneck). Each cold SSH handshake 380-586ms. The `note` command's list+pull sequence made 2+ sequential fresh connections with zero multiplexing -- that repeated handshake cost, not network transit, was ~80-90% of the reported round-trip.

FIX: ControlMaster=auto + ControlPersist=120 added to ssh_phone_opts (scripts/sinnix-phone), commit b3c610e. Verified live: first call 404ms (cold, establishes master), subsequent calls ~195-210ms (confirmed reusing the live socket via `ssh -O check`, not silently re-handshaking). ~2x improvement on repeat calls within one command invocation.

HONEST FLOOR: remaining ~200ms/call is SSH client process startup + Termux forking a remote shell per command, not network or auth -- further reduction would need a persistent phone-side daemon instead of per-call ssh spawns, out of scope for this pass, worth a follow-on if dictation latency still matters after this lands.

BONUS FIX: the multiplexing change surfaced a latent bug -- ssh_phone_opts used `-p PORT` (ssh's flag), which scp would have silently misparsed (scp's `-p` is a no-arg "preserve attributes" flag, not port) had the array ever been shared with scp verbatim. Switched to the portable `-o Port=` form; added scp_phone() helper; note's chunk-pull loop now uses it instead of a stale hand-duplicated flag set.

title: Phone as a first-class tailnet peer: control surfaces, tuning, and what root would unlock
description: Landed 2026-08-13 (session work, mostly done -- this bead records state + residuals). The Redmi Note 11 (2201117TY, HyperOS V816, Android 13, UNROOTED) is now a tailnet peer at 100.124.215.25 with two control surfaces: Termux sshd :8022 (bidirectional -- prime->phone and phone->prime both key-authed) and adbd :5555 over TCP, both reachable anywhere the tailnet reaches. Desktop side: ssh host alias 'phone', scrcpy in the workbench, and scripts/sinnix-phone (status/shell/mirror/screenshot/pull/adb-connect/adb-restore). Lake landing at /realm/data/captures/phone/{camera,download,health,voice}, pull-only rsync, never deletes on the phone. Tuning applied: EU safe-volume cap DISABLED (audio_safe_volume_state 3->1) and bluetooth absolute-volume disabled -- together these were the 'incredibly low headphone volume'; animation scales 0.5; low_power off; adaptive battery off; battery-optimization exemptions + RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND for Termux/Tailscale/SleepAsAndroid. Debloat: 21 MIUI packages removed via pm uninstall -k --user 0 (reversible with pm install-existing) -- MSA ad engine, analytics, GetApps, App Vault, Glance lockscreen ads, cleaner, yellowpage, discover, mi browser, mi player/video, ugd, mtb, miservice, barrage, fm, payment, audiomonitor, bugreport, glgm, wps. DELIBERATELY KEPT: com.xiaomi.account, finddevice, cloudservice -- bootloader unlock requires them (see sinnix-9tc). KNOWN CONSTRAINT: MIUI blocks ALL adb/sideload installs (INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED) -- no user restriction is set, it is HyperOS's own Mi-account-gated 'Install via USB' check; Play Store is the only working install route today, which excludes F-Droid, FUTO Voice Input, Syncthing, ActivityWatch mobile. That constraint dissolves on unlock/root.
notes:
2026-08-13 RELIABILITY FIX (the one that mattered): the phone's Tailscale kept dropping (~5-10 min) despite doze whitelisting, standby-bucket pinning, and miui_optimization=0. The actual fix is Android's always-on VPN: settings put secure always_on_vpn_app com.tailscale.ipn (lockdown deliberately 0 -- lockdown would kill all traffic whenever the tunnel is down, which is the wrong trade for a phone). After that the phone holds a DIRECT path (192.168.1.51) rather than a DERP relay. VERIFIED END TO END: from the phone, http://100.114.9.64:8880/ , /reports/ and /ai/ all return 200 -- the sinnix hub is reachable from the phone browser over the tailnet. ALSO: F-Droid was installed by the operator, which unblocks the F-Droid ecosystem for on-device installs (adb/sideload from the desktop is STILL blocked -- unchanged). ActivityWatch (net.activitywatch.android) is now installed and running with GET_USAGE_STATS granted, doze-whitelisted and standby-bucket pinned -- the phone telemetry hole the device program flagged is closing. NOTE the Play-build Termux still cannot get Termux:API; swapping to the F-Droid Termux would unlock the 69-command sensor surface but requires uninstall+reinstall (different signing key) which would destroy the working sshd/key setup -- back up ~/.ssh and the config first if that swap is taken.
2026-08-13 SIDELOAD DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED (supersedes the earlier 'Mi-account-gated Install via USB' theory). The real blocker for the INSTALLER UI path was Android's package verifier: after 'settings put global package_verifier_enable 0' + 'verifier_verify_adb_installs 0', the MIUI installer stopped hanging on 'Installing...'. TWO DISTINCT RESTRICTIONS, now separated: (a) adb install of an app that ALREADY EXISTS on the device succeeds (verified: reinstalling Tailscale returned Success); (b) adb install of a genuinely NEW package still returns INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED regardless of the verifier -- that is the MIUI gate proper. MIUI also interposes a securitycenter 'Danger / Install dangerous apps' dialog (com.miui.permcenter.privacymanager.SpecialPermissionInterceptActivity) before the system installer, which must be OK'd; automated tap loops that poll-and-tap will cancel the install, so drive it once and then WAIT. RESIDUAL: the Play-build Termux was uninstalled (its ~/.ssh was backed up to scratch first) and the F-Droid build has NOT successfully installed -- F-Droid reaches 'Installing...' and stalls. CONSEQUENCE RIGHT NOW: the phone has NO Termux, so sshd is gone; adb over USB and (when the VPN is up) adb over the tailnet still work, as does Tailscale itself. Next attempt: either finish the F-Droid install by hand, or flip the MIUI 'Install via USB' developer toggle which would make adb install of new packages work directly.

title: Hyprland 0.56 adoption: no_auto_hdr windowrule vs global fp16 workaround, stableid, glow, tags
description: Live system on 0.55.4; 0.56.x is out (no breaking changes per release notes). Adoption targets: (1) TEST whether windowrule no_auto_hdr can replace the global render.use_fp16=false + keep_unmodified_copy=1 HDR-dimming workaround for the AORUS FO48U -- a targeted rule beats a global render-quality tradeoff (UNVERIFIED against this panel: that test IS this bead's core); (2) evaluate stableid: window selector + windowrule tags (tags unconfirmed in primary changelog -- verify first) as replacements for the regex-heavy matching in rules.nix scratchpads; (3) note glow-gradient support as the plausible native mechanism for any future notification-glow idea (park, no build). Gate: nixpkgs Hyprland bump to 0.56 (check current pin first; if already possible via overlay, weigh against cache cost). HDR-active testing mandatory for item 1, not just SDR.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Gate is already satisfied -- the bead's blocker no longer exists. The pinned nixpkgs builds Hyprland 0.56.1 (nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.sinnix-prime.pkgs.hyprland.version). The live session reports 0.55.4 only because Hyprland does not restart during a switch, so 0.56.1 goes live at the next relogin with no version work, no overlay, and no extra cache cost.

That makes item (1) -- testing whether windowrule no_auto_hdr can replace the global render.use_fp16 = false plus keep_unmodified_copy = 1 workaround -- executable as soon as the operator next logs in. It stays operator-present work: the bead itself requires HDR to be ACTIVE during the test, which no agent can honestly verify from a headless probe, and the failure mode (whole output visually dim) is a judgement the operator makes by looking at the panel.

Suggested test order once relogged into 0.56.1: confirm hyprctl version reports 0.56.x, then drop the two render options at runtime via hyprctl keyword with HDR content on screen and watch for the dimming to return. If it does, that reproduces the problem the workaround exists for and no_auto_hdr can be tried against it. If it does not reproduce, the global workaround may simply be obsolete in 0.56 and the honest outcome is deleting it rather than replacing it with a rule.

title: bindd sweep: every bind carries a description (cheatsheet substrate)
description: The Noctalia keybind-cheatsheet plugin (installed, bound SUPER+/) renders from hyprctl binds -j; description strings come from the bindd family. The repo's bindings.nix already uses bindd for many binds ('SUPER, End, Open Sinnix system controls, ...') but bare bind entries render undescribed. Sweep: convert every user-facing bind to bindd with a description written for the CHEATSHEET reader (verb-first, workflow-relevant, no implementation jargon); submaps + scratchpads + system controls included. This is the mechanical half of the operator's legibility concept and the annotation layer any future AI-maintained help builds on. Verify: hyprctl binds -j shows zero user-facing entries with empty description; SUPER+/ renders them; count noted before/after. Feeds sinnix-v034 (cheatsheet design session material).
close_reason: Done, source-verified: 112 bind entries in bindings.nix, all in the described families (bindd 105 / binddl 4 / binddm 3); zero undescribed bind/bindl/bindm declarations remain anywhere in modules/ or dots/. Commit 9cc9f14 records live validation -- all 99 rendered lines fed through 'hyprctl keyword' against Hyprland 0.55.4, all reported has_description, bind count unchanged at 109. Cheatsheet substrate (sinnix-v034 + the Noctalia SUPER+/ plugin) now has real strings to render; they appear live after the pending consolidated switch.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Sweep implemented in 1842c40 (bindings.nix + hyprland/default.nix; commit message belongs to a concurrent lane that swept the staged files -- content is correct and on master).

All user-facing binds now use the described family. bind -> bindd, bindl -> binddl, bindm -> binddm; the flag letters combine, verified live against Hyprland 0.55.4: hyprctl keyword binddl/binddm returned ok with has_description true.

Counts: baseline hyprctl binds -j = 109 total, 92 undescribed, 17 described (the 7 pre-existing bindd + 10 submap entries). Rendered config now evaluates to 92 bindd + 4 binddl + 3 binddm + 10 submap = 109, so no bind was lost or added. All 99 top-level rendered lines were fed through hyprctl keyword against the live compositor: 99/99 accepted, described count went 17 -> 116. Live state restored with hyprctl reload.

Descriptions are written for the cheatsheet reader (verb first, no commas -- hyprlang splits the bind line on them, so a comma in a description silently eats the dispatcher). That constraint is now documented in the bindings.nix header.

Remaining: SUPER+/ render check after the next switch (needs:switch).

Noted for the design pass, not fixed here: SUPER+B and SUPER SHIFT+B are byte-identical binds, so the cheatsheet will show the same entry twice. Left alone deliberately -- removing a working bind is a design-pass call, not a sweep call.

title: Hyprland deliberate-config program: the whole-config redo that never came

I don't even know most keybinds -- never bothered to learn because I expected to redo the whole config sometime and the time never came.' This bead IS that time, as a program. comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:

title: Off-site backup restoration: borg to sinnix-ethereal (kills the 100%-local accepted risk)

title: sinnix-observe managed-units view omits active capture-kind user services
description: Found 2026-08-12 during the agent-teams pilot audit: both blinded research arms independently concluded sinnix-capture-clipboard/-primary were absent from live state because sinnix-observe's managed-units section does not list them, while systemctl --user shows both active. polylogued (also capture-runtime class) IS listed, so the omission is selective — likely the unit-row source filters by surface kind or observe flags in a way that drops some kind=capture surfaces that have real backing .service units. Consequence: any consumer treating observe output as the live-state authority (agents, the pilot corpus, future dashboards) sees phantom outages. Fix: make the managed-units view include every surface whose unit field names a real unit, regardless of kind; add a check that every active sinnix-* user service with a registered surface appears in observe output.
close_reason: Root-caused more precisely than the bead's own hypothesis: not a filtering bug in sinnix-observe's Python view, but a Nix-declaration mislabel. capture-clipboard.nix and capture-primary.nix set kind = "capture" despite having real, live, observe.enable=true .service units -- diverging from the convention every OTHER capture-* module already follows correctly and documents in comments (capture-a11y.nix, capture-notifications.nix, capture-screen.nix all explicitly note 'kind=capture is reserved for orphan surfaces with no real backing unit'). This mislabel excluded them not just from sinnix-observe's managed_units() (runtime_inventory.py:47, which skips kind in {capture,slice}) but also from the Nix-level kind==service render lists in modules/runtime.nix:411,452 -- a wider blast radius than the bead described, since anything consuming those lists (not just sinnix-observe) would have the same phantom-outage view. Fixed by removing the kind override on both (defaults to service). Verified: nix eval .config.sinnix.runtime.surfaces.{capture-clipboard,capture-primary}.kind now returns 'service' on both; full toplevel eval confirmed the change itself introduces no new eval error (a separate, unrelated, uncommitted in-progress edit to serena.nix from another concurrent agent is currently breaking eval -- not touched, not mine, noted separately). description: Cheap probe FIRST: fetch github.com/iocost-benchmark/iocost-benchmarks hwdb and search for CT4000P3SSD8 (Crucial P3 4TB) and CT1000MX500SSD1 (MX500 1TB) model entries. AC: note records either the found params + proposed stanza, or the bench plan with the operator-gate stated.
notes: 2026-08-12 hwdb probe DONE (the free half). Result: NEITHER model present in iocost-benchmark/iocost-benchmarks database/2.2 (34 entries, checked exhaustively; 2.1 has no Crucial either). CT4000P3SSD8: absent. CT1000MX500SSD1: absent (DB is almost entirely NVMe; only SATA entries are Samsung 860/870). Nearest miss: CT1000P3PSSD8 = P3 *Plus* 1TB -- different controller generation (Gen4 vs the P3's Gen3) and 1/4 the capacity; NOT adoptable as params for the 4TB P3, at most a sanity anchor. Consequence: real params require a local resctl-bench run -- and benching the MX500 (live root disk) realistically needs the dedicated resctl-demo boot image (repo README), while the P3 needs an hours-long quiet window saturating /realm. RECOMMENDATION: defer the bench entirely until a1dp.1's stall-attribution view shows whether IO pressure is even implicated in the observed stalls (memory PSI dominated the evidence so far); if stalls attribute to memory, ctrl=auto stays and this bead closes as not-worth-the-window. title: Acknowledged-outage surface: stop agents re-alarming on known-down services
description: Operator pain (2026-08-12, stated twice): agents repeatedly discover and alarm about sinex being down (intentional, under active repair) and polylogue known-states. No machine-readable acknowledged-state carrier exists, so every fresh session re-derives the outage as an emergency. Design sketch: per-surface acknowledgement in the runtime registry (sinnix.runtime.surfaces.<name>.acknowledged = { down; reason; since; ref }) rendered into /etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json; consumers: (a) sinnix-health-sentinel treats acked surfaces as expected-down (no red, no notify; listed in a distinct acknowledged section so they cannot be forgotten), (b) sinnix-observe prints the ack prominently, (c) sessionstart-sinex-recall hook includes it so agents see acknowledged-down at session start instead of alarming. Acks carry a reference and date so stale acks are auditable; an ack without a live ref is itself a sentinel warning. Build only the consumed path; no extra taxonomy.
acceptance_criteria: sinnix.runtime.surfaces.<name>.acknowledged = {down, reason, since, ref} exists as a schema option rendered into /etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json; sinnix-health-sentinel treats acked surfaces as expected-down (no failure transition, listed in a distinct acknowledged section of its output); sessionstart-sinex-recall.sh prints acknowledged-down surfaces at session start; an ack whose ref bead is CLOSED trips a sentinel warning (stale-ack audit); live proof: ack the current sinex-down state with ref to its repair bead, run the sentinel, confirm no red + visible ack line; then a fresh claude session's start hook shows it. Do NOT build any consumer beyond these three.

title: scribe-tap: window-context attribution always falls back to 'unknown' (root vs user Hyprland session)
description: Live investigation 2026-08-12 (triggered by asking whether keylog events carry window attribution -- they're meant to). scribe-tap logs a 'window' field per event via update_context() in src/state.c, shelling out to 'hyprctl [--instance SIG] activewindow -j'. In practice EVERY event in every checked day (2026-08-10 full-file scan) shows window="unknown" -- the fallback path (reset_context_on_failure, state.c:584) fires on every poll, meaning the hyprctl subprocess call is failing every time, not that the feature is disabled (context_enabled is true; a disabled context writes "global", not "unknown" -- confirmed distinct code paths at state.c:609-614). Root cause: scribe-tap's three worker processes run as ROOT (required for raw /dev/input access via intercept-tools + uinput -- confirmed via ps -o user=), and root's process environment has no HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE (confirmed via /proc/<pid>/environ -- empty for all HYPRLAND_* vars). The --hypr-user sinity CLI flag exists specifically to bridge this privilege gap (locate the signature via the target user's session) but its lookup is not succeeding in this deployment -- state->hypr_signature is evidently empty/unset at the point update_context() builds its argv, so hyprctl runs with no --instance and can't find the user's Hyprland instance from a root-owned process with no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/session context.
design: Two fix directions, either sufficient alone: (1) FIX THE LOOKUP: find and repair whatever --hypr-user resolution mechanism scribe-tap intends (likely scanning /run/user/<uid>/hypr/*/... for the target user's instance signature file, or reading it from a process in that user's session) -- check src/main.c/state.c for how --hypr-user is currently parsed and used, it may be a stub/incomplete implementation. (2) PASS IT EXPLICITLY: since the sinnix Nix module that launches scribe-tap (find the exec-once/systemd wiring -- not a systemd --user unit per this investigation, likely a Hyprland exec-once line) already knows the live session's HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE at composure-config-generation time is NOT reliable (it's dynamic per-session), but the LAUNCHING context (whatever spawns scribe-tap, itself presumably running IN the user's Hyprland session before any privilege drop to root) DOES have the real env var available -- capture it there and pass via --hypr-signature/an explicit flag rather than relying on scribe-tap's own runtime user-session lookup. Either fix restores per-window keystroke attribution, which has real analytical value (confirmed today: it's exactly the kind of evidence that would help reconstruct activity timelines when other capture lanes have gaps).
acceptance_criteria: A fresh day's keylog file shows non-'unknown' window values for at least the large majority of events during normal desktop use (some 'unknown' is expected during compositor restarts/transitions).
close_reason: Superseded by the scribe-tap redesign (scribe-tap 5c92de3, 2026-08-12): compositor window-tracking was REMOVED from scribe-tap entirely -- window attribution is now a downstream timestamp-join against ActivityWatch window events (lynchpin), not scribe-tap's job. This bead's AC (non-unknown window values in keylog files) is unsatisfiable by design against current source; the root-cause investigation it records (root workers lack HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE; --hypr-user lookup used a file path Hyprland never wrote) is preserved here and in the redesign commit messages.
