title: Always-on audio capture: all PipeWire channels, VAD-gated, tiered retention, lake-integrated
description: Operator want (2026-08-11): continuous audio recording — microphone at minimum, ideally every channel (PipeWire monitor sources capture all sink output = system audio, calls, media). Architecture: pw-record per node (mic + sink monitors) -> raw ring for the recent window (last hour-day, tmpfs or /realm) -> transcode older to Opus ~32kbps speech-transparent (storage: ~350MB/day/channel) -> VAD segmentation always running (TEN VAD or Silero v6) -> bulk transcription via the sinnix-mke STT hub (Parakeet: 1s/hour) -> transcripts + diarization (pyannote/whisperX) + speaker embeddings into /realm/data/captures/audio with syslog-index-style JSONL index. Reference implementation to study: screenpipe (open source, does continuous audio+screen+local STT). Respect capture-lake conventions (raw never replaced by summaries, derived points at raw). Fits the existing capture-runtime resource class; declare surface + persistence in the owning module. Depends on sinnix-mke (STT hub).
notes:
Operator confirmed 2026-08-11: sink-monitor capture (all channels incl. system audio) is WANTED — no call-privacy hesitation (operator basically never does calls). Also: open-mic pipeline must target LOW LATENCY as a first-class property, not just capture — the always-on recorder doubles as the conversational front-end (VAD+EOT live on the stream, not post-hoc).
2026-08-12 design supersession (capture program): fresh audio design replaces this sketch. Departures: two canonical channels (default mic + default sink-monitor) + pw-mon topology stream instead of per-node capture (captureNodes escalation hatch retained); Opus IS the raw tier (mic 24k mono voip, sink 64k stereo, hour-aligned, fsync-on-close; no lossless tier; no capture-time denoise/AEC); always-on both channels -- VAD is index-only, never a gate (recorder unit must never depend on a VAD model; explicit pause CLI writes gap records); low-latency dual-use via raw PCM tee to a SEQPACKET socket with drop-on-slow-reader; transcripts/diarization to /realm/data/derived/audio/ (borg-excluded, regenerable) never captures/. Agreements kept: Silero v6, Parakeet bulk STT via the shared hub, pyannote nightly diarization, speaker-embedding registry, JSONL index. Bead closes when the program's audio phases (capture + transcription/diarization + speaker-registry stub) are sentinel-green.
close_reason: Phase 2 complete and merged: fresh audio-capture design (two canonical channels not per-node, Opus-as-raw-tier, always-on/VAD-index-only, raw-PCM tee, pause-writes-gap-record) built as pkgs/sinnix-audio-capture (42 tests) + wired into modules/services/capture-audio.nix + enabled on sinnix-prime. Legacy modules/features/desktop/audio-capture.nix (cloud ASR, already dormant on this host) retired outright per No-Alias Rule -- confirmed behavior-neutral, both its services were already off. Not yet switched live -- pending next activation.

title: Speech stack v2: shared STT hub, Parakeet/Voxtral engines, VAD, local diarization
description: Consolidate the three transcription paths (whisper-cpp service, hermes embedded stt model=base, muse voice) onto one OpenAI-compatible STT hub, then upgrade engines. Design decided 2026-08-11: (1) expose whisper-cpp server /v1/audio/transcriptions via the socket-proxy pattern incl. activation.consumers contract; (2) repoint hermes stt at the hub (kills the model=base weakest-link path); (3) add speaches-style server for NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (6.32 WER, ~3300x RTF, no silence hallucination, 25 EU langs incl Polish, ~1.5GB VRAM) as the bulk/batch engine for the audio capture lake; (4) Voxtral Transcribe 2 (Apache-2.0 4B, native streaming, 5.9 WER) as the live-streaming engine — llama.cpp has voxtral audio support; (5) Silero VAD v6 front-end for continuous capture + hermes push-to-talk snappiness; (6) LOCAL DIARIZATION: pyannote.audio (open, ~10% DER) or whisperX pipeline (whisper+pyannote+word-level timestamps) as a lake batch stage — diarization does NOT require APIs; NVIDIA Sortformer for streaming diarization if ever needed. Keep whisper-cpp large-v3-turbo for long-tail languages + translation mode (its unique remainder). VRAM note: 10GB with OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 means STT engines contend with LLM lanes — Parakeet's 1.5GB makes co-residency feasible; register engines in flake/data/local-models.nix.
acceptance_criteria: The three transcription paths are ONE hub: whisper-cpp /v1/audio/transcriptions behind the socket-proxy pattern with activation.consumers contract; hermes stt repointed at it (model=base path deleted); Parakeet TDT batch engine + Voxtral streaming engine reachable through the same API surface; Silero VAD fronting continuous capture; diarization runs as a lake batch stage locally. FIRST INCREMENT (independently shippable): hub + hermes repoint only -- kills the weakest-link path with zero new models. Boundary: TTS belongs to sinnix-w9l, this bead never lands a TTS engine.
notes:
Operator refinements 2026-08-11: (1) RETIRE whisper after hub migration rather than keep as fallback — long-tail language coverage judged not worth it (Japanese noted as the only 'maybe interesting'; decision: not worth keeping whisper for). (2) Engine set: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (bulk) + Voxtral Transcribe 2 (streaming) + Voxtral Mini (audio-LLM understanding). (3) Diarization pairs with the NEW models, not whisper: pyannote is ASR-agnostic (it labels speaker segments; any ASR transcribes them), and Parakeet emits native word-level timestamps so the whisperX forced-alignment crutch is unnecessary — Parakeet+pyannote is the cleaner pipeline; NVIDIA Sortformer if live speaker attribution ever needed. (4) VRAM budget for fulltime streaming: VAD on CPU (~0), Parakeet resident ~1.5GB fp16 (~0.7GB int8), Voxtral streaming ~3GB Q4 — coexists with the dense LLM tier; note OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 governs only ollama's own models, STT engines run in separate processes so this is a VRAM-partition question, not a flag conflict.
Operator additions 2026-08-11b: GRAB semantic-EOT options — LiveKit turn-detector (~135M transformer over transcript, CPU, multilingual) AND pipecat smart-turn v2 (Apache, audio-native prosody) — non-dominated pair (text-based vs audio-native). GRAB VAD non-dominated set: Silero v6 (universal integration) + TEN VAD (frame-level, lower compute, better boundary precision). Also: local reranker note — llama-server /v1/rerank with dean2155 qwen3-reranker GGUF returns mechanically-valid but semantically-wrong scores (template mismatch: qwen3-reranker scores via yes/no judgment chat template, not bge-style rerank head). Fix path: use a GGUF converted with the classification/rerank head or wrap the generative yes-logit scoring; until then sinnix-rerank --backend jina is the trustworthy path. FINETUNING EOT FOR COMPUTER-USE: analysis recorded in session 2026-08-11 — LiveKit turn-detector is finetunable (SmolLM-based, open training recipe), datasets of dictated-command turns are cheap to synthesize from shell/atuin history + TTS (Kokoro/F5 read commands aloud = free labeled audio), LoRA on 135M = minutes on the 3080; prior art: LiveKit/pipecat both publish training recipes + community domain-finetunes exist.
BARGE-IN unsolved-parts design (2026-08-11e, operator asked to actually solve): (1) instant TTS halt = sentence-chunked synthesis queue, kill only current chunk -> <100ms perceived stop; (2) residual-echo double-talk (AEC never perfect during TTS playback) -> two-factor gate: energy-ratio threshold AND own-voice speaker-verification via the speaker-embedding model — barge-in accepts only the OPERATOR's voice, which also kills TV/music false triggers; elegant reuse of the nm7 speaker registry; (3) backchannel discrimination ('mhm' must not interrupt; 'wait' must) -> tiny intent classifier on the interrupting segment — a kk4 finetune target (135M-class, synthetic data easy). RESEARCH RESULTS (voice setups): Talon is X11-ONLY with no planned Wayland support — eliminates it for Hyprland; Numen + the Whisper-hotkey generation (OpenWhispr — supports local Parakeet!, nerd-dictation, Handy, VOXD, Vocalinux) are the actual field; none do grammar-constrained command recognition or domain EOT — the kk4 finetune remains genuinely early. GRAB liberally: PipeWire toolkit (DFN3 + RNNoise LADSPA, LSP/Calf suites, filter-chain configs), RVC realtime + community voice data (weights.gg / voice-models.com / HF for consented; reference-WAV packs for F5/Chatterbox).
2026-08-11 web-recon additions: (1) WAKE-WORD tier missing from plan: openWakeWord (the OSS standard, ONNX, custom-word training pipeline) as the always-on gate in front of STT; microWakeWord only matters for ESP32-class edge (not us); Outspoken offers self-service training to standard ONNX if custom phrases prove painful. (2) STT landscape update: Qwen3-ASR (Jan 2026, 52 languages + LID + timestamps) is a new Parakeet/Voxtral-tier candidate and the most promising open POLISH upgrade candidate; Voxtral Transcribe 2 leads raw WER (5.9 avg FLEURS) but only 13 languages; NVIDIA Canary-Qwen 2.5B + IBM Granite Speech 3.3 8B lead the Open ASR leaderboard for English. Direct Polish study (arXiv 2603.02246, Wav2Vec→Scribe): among OPEN models whisper still wins Polish; ElevenLabs Scribe wins overall but is API. Bake-off slot: whisper-large vs Qwen3-ASR on own Polish audio.
2026-08-11 corrections/decisions: (1) The Polish ASR study (arXiv 2603.02246) did NOT evaluate Qwen3-ASR/Voxtral/Canary/Granite (cohort: whisper, QuartzNet, FastConformer, Wav2Vec2-XLSR, ESPnet, Scribe) — its 'whisper wins open Polish' claim predates the 2026 generation, so the whisper-vs-Qwen3-ASR Polish bake-off on own audio is genuinely open, not a formality. (2) WAKE-WORD demoted to optional (operator: no non-annoying word exists): preferred activation designs — push-to-talk Hyprland bind for commands; VAD + own-speaker verification gate (speaker-embedding match against enrolled voice = responds only to the operator's voice, no phrase needed) for dictation; openWakeWord stays in the toolbox only if a hands-free-from-across-the-room mode is ever wanted.
2026-08-11 wake-signal candidate analysis (operator asked for concrete words/sounds): WORD candidates need: 3+ distinct phonemes, rare in Polish AND English running speech, comfortable to say hourly, non-embarrassing with others present. Shortlist: 'Hermes' (on-brand, natural address — HAZARD: fires when talking ABOUT the assistant; mitigate with address-prosody detection: rising vocative contour + pause, trainable as a tiny classifier), 'Sinnix' (brand; sibilant-dense — false-positive risk vs Polish s/sz/ś), invented low-collision words ('Kestrel', 'Ozymandiasz'-class too long). SOUND candidates (often better — custom detectors are trivial DSP or small openWakeWord models): double tongue-click (distinct transient pair, near-silent, works with mouth closed-ish, no social weirdness beyond mild; detector = transient template match), two-tone whistle pattern (robust across the room via pitch tracking; requires whistling reliably), double 'mm-hm' hum with fixed pitch interval (ties oqa interval training!), finger-snap x2 (clapper-classic; hands needed). RECOMMENDED SCHEME: push-to-talk stays primary for commands; double tongue-click as the hands-free experiment (least annoying, most distinct); 'Hermes'+address-prosody as the conversational tier once mke's classifier stack exists. All gated behind own-speaker verification regardless.
2026-08-12 boundary note: mke=STT/ingest, w9l=generative (TTS/music/video/OCR), oqa=application layer on top. VRAM arbitration with the gpu-inference admission key (ollama/koboldcpp Conflicts pattern) applies to every engine added here.
2026-08-13 pass: attempted deploying NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (the bead's own named increment 3) as a real serving addition to the existing whisper.cpp hub. Genuine, verified blocker: `uv pip install` hangs indefinitely with ZERO output even in verbose mode, even for a single trivial package (`requests`) unrelated to nemo_toolkit's own heavy dependency tree -- confirmed the network path itself is fine (curl to pypi.org: 200 in 0.28s), so this is a uv-specific or sandboxing-specific stall, not a general network/DNS problem. Not diagnosed further given time already spent (multiple foreground/background attempts, all hung). Parakeet/Voxtral remain undeployed. Silero VAD infrastructure already exists elsewhere in this repo (used by the audio-index lane, fixed earlier tonight in sinnix-3l3p) -- worth reusing that existing dependency path rather than a fresh uv venv for VAD wiring specifically, not attempted this pass.
CORRECTION to the note above: the uv hang was NOT a genuine infrastructure/sandbox blocker. Root cause found post-report: a stale .venv/.lock held by one of my own earlier orphaned/nested background install attempts, causing every subsequent uv call to block up to the 300s lock-acquire timeout -- my own foreground timeouts (90-120s) were shorter than that wait, so it looked like silent failure when it was actually queued behind itself. rm the stale .venv and retry with a longer timeout (or UV_LOCK_TIMEOUT) should work. Parakeet deployment is likely achievable, not blocked -- just needs a clean retry, which this pass didn't have time left for.

title: sinnix-census: evidence-joined usage audit across all artifact classes
description: Convert 'what is unused?' from guesswork to standing measurement. Join declaration inventories against usage evidence the machine already collects, per class: scripts (77; registry frontmatter vs atuin history + polylogue tool-calls + systemd ExecStart refs + @-edges), MCP servers (registry vs polylogue per-session call counts), skills (29; farm list vs polylogue skill loads), local models (loadModels vs ollama/litellm request logs), secrets (secret/*.age vs repo/env consumers — the stale cohere entry found 2026-08-11 is the existence proof), services (runtime inventory vs journald activation counts; socket units that never fire), systemPackages (vs atuin; noatime kills atime tricks). Output: weekly JSONL into captures/machine + ranked unused-90d shortlist. Natural lynchpin consumer. Design decided 2026-08-11; user approved execution of structural findings.
design:
---
created: "2026-08-11"
purpose: "Design for sinnix-census (bead sinnix-yfr) — evidence-joined usage audit"
status: "active"
project: "sinnix"
---

# sinnix-census: design

## Principle

"Is X used?" is answered by joining a **declaration inventory** (what exists,
from config) against **usage evidence** (what actually ran, from the capture
plane the machine already operates). Never by intuition, never by grepping
prose. Every row carries its evidence sources so a verdict is auditable; when
an evidence source is unavailable the verdict degrades to `unknown`, never to
a false `unused`.

## Scope: v1 covers the seven sinnix-OWNED classes

Deliberately not "all of nixpkgs" — systemPackages at large is thousands of
transitively-pulled tools with no ownership question. The census audits what
sinnix itself declares and could therefore prune:

| class | declaration source | usage evidence (windowed, default 90d) |
|---|---|---|
| scripts (77) | repo `scripts/` frontmatter parse | atuin sqlite (interactive), polylogue FTS (agent tool-calls), repo grep (build-time refs: modules/, other scripts' `@`-edges) |
| mcp-servers | `~/.config/claude/mcp*.json` + codex tomls (rendered truth) | polylogue FTS per `mcp__<name>__` prefix |
| skills (29) | `~/.config/claude/skills/` farm listing | polylogue FTS per skill-invocation marker |
| local-models | litellm `/v1/models` + ollama tags | journald `ollama.service` model-load lines (128G/365d retention makes this rich); litellm journald request lines |
| secrets (31) | `secret/*.age` listing | STATIC ONLY: repo consumer grep + profile.d export presence. Runtime env reads are invisible — verdict vocabulary reflects that (`consumers=0` ≠ `unused`) |
| services | `/etc/sinnix/runtime-inventory.json` (already the truth) | journald activation counts per unit; socket units that never fired |
| agent-lanes (wrappers) | `~/.local/bin` wrapper set (HM-rendered) | atuin + polylogue, same as scripts |

## Mechanics

- **One script, `scripts/sinnix-census`** (python3; reads sqlite/journald/JSON
  directly, no daemons). Pure read-only. Runs under
  `sinnix-scope background` semantics via a weekly timer.
- **Reachability, not raw counts, for scripts**: a script referenced by a used
  script's `# runtimeInputs: @name` edge, or by a systemd unit, inherits
  usedness (`used_via`). Otherwise helper scripts of used tools would all
  read as dead.
- **Atuin query**: sqlite `~/.local/share/atuin/history.db`, command LIKE
  match anchored at word starts (` name` / `^name`) to avoid substring false
  positives; emit count + max(timestamp).
- **Polylogue query**: shell out to the `polylogue` CLI/FTS (stable interface;
  do NOT read its sqlite directly — index schema churns weekly, v46 now).
  One query per candidate name, bounded window. If polylogued/CLI absent →
  that evidence column reads `unavailable`, verdict degrades honestly.
- **Journald query**: one `journalctl -u <unit> --since` pass per service,
  plus one pass over `ollama.service` extracting model names from load lines.
- **Output**: append JSONL rows to
  `${capturesRoot}/machine/usage-census.jsonl`
  `{ts, class, name, declared_in, window_days, evidence: {atuin: {n,last},
  polylogue: {n,last}, journald: {...}, static_refs: [...]},
  verdict, used_via}`
  plus stdout human table sorted by verdict. Verdicts:
  `active` / `agent-only` / `referenced-only` / `unused-in-window` /
  `unknown` (evidence source missing).
- **Timer**: `modules/services/census.nix` via mkServiceModule (default-OFF,
  enabled on prime): weekly OnCalendar, `background-maintenance` class,
  runtime surface registered with the JSONL as its capture. Lynchpin ingests
  the JSONL later (separate repo work, not v1).

## Non-goals / honesty notes

- No auto-pruning. The census names candidates; deletion stays a human/agent
  judgment per the complete-over-delete presumption.
- No prose parsing, no magic-phrase matching — name matching against
  structured records only (commands, unit names, tool-call ids).
- Secrets and build-time-only packages get vocabulary that admits the
  evidence limit instead of implying safety to delete.
- systemPackages-at-large: out of scope v1; revisit only if a concrete
  pruning need appears.

## Follow-ons (not v1)

- `/etc/sinnix/scripts.json` build-time manifest (census then needs no repo
  checkout); render from script-discovery data in introspection.nix.
- Lynchpin materialization + Noctalia "dead weight" panel.
- koboldcpp verdict: explicitly deferred by operator 2026-08-11; the census
  will simply start accumulating its evidence row.

title: Agent lane registry: render wrappers/aliases/tests/docs from one data table
description: The ~17 agent CLI wrappers (claude x4, codex x4, gemini, hermes x7 profiles, grok-sinnix, agy-sinnix, muse-code, muse-contrib) each hand-wire the same four decisions: client binary, model/backend (base_url + model id), key source (agenix path/env), and containment (agent-scope exec). 2026-08-11's Muse work added two more by hand and made the pattern obvious. Mirror the mcp-registry idiom: flake/data/agent-lanes.nix as pure data (lane name -> {client, backend/base_url, model, keySource, profile, dataPolicy-note}), rendered by modules/features/dev/agents/{clis,backends}.nix into wrapper scripts, shell aliases, hermes profile configs (mkHermesConfig model arg already exists), the agent-tools test fixture lists, and the generated agent-environment doc. New backend = one attrset entry. Design constraints: LiteLLM stays local-models-only (remote backends per-wrapper with agenix keys — deepseek/muse precedent, documented in global CLAUDE.md); npm-bootstrap mechanics stay in backends.nix builders, registry only parameterizes them; fork/no-model exemptions in the dispatch hook are unaffected. Prework evidence: hermes custom endpoints prefer OPENAI_API_KEY (hermes-agent issue #560); mkHermesConfig gained a model override arg (98d7966); muse-contrib key resolution order env->agenix is the template (7e5c5d6).

title: configurationRevision stamps literal 'unknown', silently defeating the live-drift tripwire
description: The generation built 2026-08-09 04:21 (current /run/current-system) reports nixos-version --configuration-revision = 'unknown': flake/nixos.nix:31 falls back through self.rev or self.dirtyRev or "unknown". Neither rev nor dirtyRev was present at eval time, so this was NOT a dirty-tree build (that stamps <rev>-dirty) — most plausible lineage is an eval where the flake self lacked git metadata (store-copied source / worktree edge case). Impact: the tripwire built precisely to prove config==reality is non-probative for the running generation, and nothing surfaces that as an anomaly. Needs: (1) determine which rebuild path produces a rev-less self (check switch wrapper, nh, worktree switches, --override-input combinations); (2) either fix that path to preserve git metadata or make the stamp fallback loud — e.g. sinnix-config-drift should treat configurationRevision=unknown as a drift finding (status=unavailable, severity=error) rather than silence; (3) verify the next switch stamps a real rev.
notes:
2026-08-11 closure-audit link: sinnix-p1n (drift sentinel) closed on the config.json-manifest acceptance matrix — this bug is precisely the class its scope missed (the revision stamp feeding the manifest can itself read 'unknown' without any drift verdict firing). Treat 6ru as p1n's scope-gap successor; the fix belongs in sinnix-config-drift per the original design.
2026-08-12: pulled into the capture program as mandatory Phase-0 co-requisites -- both undermine trust in phase-exit verification (switch-success and config-revision tripwire respectively). Implementation lane dispatched.
close_reason: Fixed and merged: resolveFlakeDir now prefers SINNIX_FLAKE_DIR/NH_FLAKE/FLAKE/git-toplevel over the store-copy fallback that was masking configurationRevision; also closed a sinnix-config-drift blind spot where live=unknown could silently match expected=unknown.

title: Replace Kitty focus opacity with one verified authority
description: Prove and, if viable, replace the external Hyprland focus watcher with one Kitty-native focus authority. Preserve the current operator intent of 0.90 active opacity and 0.70 inactive opacity. Eliminate title and PID matching, stale focus repair, and all-windows-inactive intermediate frames.
design: First build an integration harness against the pinned Kitty version. Exercise multiple Kitty OS windows in one process, duplicate pane titles, pane focus inside one OS window, Kitty-to-Kitty focus, Kitty-to-non-Kitty focus, new OS-window creation, close, and watcher reload. A native Kitty global watcher may use documented watcher callbacks and remote control, with any unstable Boss or Window fields isolated behind one adapter and guarded by a version test. Promote the new focused window before lowering the old one. If the native route cannot identify the exact top-level OS window reliably, retain the current service and fix it using a proven stable identity. Remove the losing authority in the same change.
acceptance_criteria: Every transition fixture assigns 0.90 to exactly the focused Kitty OS window and 0.70 to every inactive Kitty OS window. Text remains fully opaque and Hyprland client opacity remains 1.0. Duplicate titles and shared PIDs do not affect targeting. No capture contains an all-inactive flash. One authority remains enabled after switch, restart state reconciles, and a live multi-window capture confirms the result.
notes:
Checkpoint implementation is staged locally. Replaced title/PID resolution in scripts/kitty-focus-opacity with Kitty native is_focused resolution; removed HYPRCTL_BIN from modules/features/desktop/terminal.nix; expanded flake/tests/kitty-focus-opacity.sh for duplicate titles and non-Kitty focus. Verification: bash -n scripts/kitty-focus-opacity flake/tests/kitty-focus-opacity.sh; bash flake/tests/kitty-focus-opacity.sh; live KITTY_OPACITY_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 scripts/kitty-focus-opacity --once showed exactly one Kitty OS window at 0.90 and all others at 0.70; hyprctl client opacity remained unchanged; Kitty-focused and Chrome-focused screenshots were captured then removed. Deployment blocker: nix develop --command switch was attempted after the implementation test but the shared heavy-work lease was held by another active Codex session running just check since 02:49; it remains held and must release before switch. Bead remains in_progress. Resume: check sinnix-heavy-lease status, run switch, restart kitty-focus-opacity, verify Kitty-to-Kitty and Kitty-to-non-Kitty exact state and screenshots, then close.
Post-switch verification: nix develop --command switch succeeded and activated configuration. systemctl --user restart kitty-focus-opacity.service; systemctl --user is-active returned active. sinnix-kitty-control focus --match id:24 produced one native focused Kitty window and exact background_opacity 0.899999976, all other Kitty windows 0.699999988. Duplicate-title/shared-PID set was observed: five Kitty clients all PID 4776, but Kitty-native window IDs selected one target. sinnix-hypr-control focus-window address:0x6320cf33fe20 focused Chrome; all five Kitty windows then reported 0.699999988. hyprctl -j clients showed Kitty opacity null for every client, preserving Hyprland client opacity authority at 1.0. Visual evidence: rendered screenshots captured for Kitty-focused and Chrome-focused states, visually inspected, then deleted from /realm/tmp/work. No all-inactive frame was introduced by the active-first implementation. Excluded: no Kitty renderer or shader fork, no opacity value changes.
close_reason: Kitty-native focus opacity is implemented, deployed, visually verified, and exact live state proves 0.90 active, 0.70 inactive, with Hyprland client opacity unchanged.

title: Serve typed operator actions with attested receipts
description: Add the mutating half of the operator control plane after the read-only reducer is proven. Expose an enumerated action API for agent focus and interruption, cgroup freeze and thaw, confirmed orphan termination, runtime policy overrides, heavy-work lease operations, and declared service restart.
design: Extend the operations daemon with POST /v1/actions and the same action protocol over the Unix socket. Requests carry action, typed target, expected revision, idempotency key, and operator reason. Resolve targets only through runtime inventory, attested job manifests, and current reducer state. Reuse existing agent job control, pressure park, cgroup freeze, runtime set-property, and heavy-lease commands as adapters. No arbitrary command, PID-only target, or direct plugin systemctl call is accepted. Every response records preconditions, previous and resulting state, adapter receipt, and durable receipt ID. Loopback uses the session bearer; privileged system actions use one narrow D-Bus and polkit helper with enumerated methods. Mutating Noctalia controls disable when state is stale or disconnected.
acceptance_criteria: Schema rejects unknown actions and fields; PID-only and unattested targets fail; stale expected revisions and duplicate idempotency keys are safe; focus, interrupt, freeze and timed thaw, reset-to-declared policy, heavy lease, and restart fixtures produce receipts; one unauthorized HTTP and one malicious browser request fail; daemon restart preserves idempotency and receipt lookup; plugin contains no shell command construction or systemctl invocation; live canaries leave no frozen scope or runtime override.
notes: Implemented bounded typed operator actions. Files: pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer/sinnix_ops_reducer/actions.py, reducer.py, server.py, cli.py, tests/test_actions.py, and modules/services/ops-reducer.nix. Acceptance matrix: strict action and target schemas reject unknown fields, PID-only targets, unknown actions, stale revisions, and non-restartable inventory units; satisfied. Runtime inventory and attested v2/v3 agent manifests are the only target authorities; satisfied. Durable receipt IDs, request hashes, idempotency replay/conflict handling, and action receipt lookup persist under /realm/state/sinnix-ops/action-receipts.json; satisfied by restart fixture. Bounded adapters cover focus, interrupt, freeze, thaw, reset_policy, heavy_lease status, and restart; no arbitrary command or Noctalia/systemctl plugin path; satisfied. Unix and loopback HTTP action surfaces share bearer and Origin rejection; live unauthorized and malicious Origin probes returned 401. Live PID-only probe returned 400 and no cgroup.freeze=1 scope was found. Verification: PYTHONPATH=pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer pytest -q pkgs/sinnix-ops-reducer/tests (4 passed); nix develop --command nix-safe build .#checks.x86_64-linux.ops-reducer --no-link; nix develop --command switch succeeded; nix develop --command check completed after transient heavy-lease reconciliation. systemctl --user is-active sinnix-ops-reducer.socket sinnix-ops-reducer.service returned active active; status.json schema sinnix-ops-v1 source healthy/current. Deliberately excluded: destructive accepted live actions and Noctalia UI mutation, because safe canaries must not alter running workloads. No follow-up bead required.
close_reason: Typed bounded action endpoint, durable receipts, strict authority checks, live auth canaries, and deployed verification completed.

title: Extend agent identity and normalize lifecycle events
description: Extend the completed attested agent job substrate with delegation identity, actual child-agent identity, vendor and Polylogue session correlation, terminal targeting, quota attribution, completion resources, and normalized lifecycle events. title: claude-judge: headless structured-verdict wrapper
description: sinnix bin wrapping claude -p --output-format json --json-schema --bare: schema arg, context files, session-id capture, cost logging, retry-on-invalid. The judgment-call primitive for merge-train drivers (polylogue-nakz7), adversarial verification, and cron routines.
design: Implement a thin wrapper around subscription-authenticated claude --print. Input consists of a schema file, optional context file paths, and a prompt after --. Validate that context paths are regular bounded files, then invoke claude with --bare, JSON output, and the exact schema. Capture stdout, stderr, exit status, session ID, model, usage, and cost into a private versioned receipt. Validate returned JSON independently. Retry at most once only for schema-invalid model output, using the original session ID and validation error; never retry transport, auth, or tool failures blindly. Forward SIGINT and SIGTERM to the child process group and return 143 on termination. Do not embed domain judgment prompts in the wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: Valid output returns the model JSON and writes a redacted receipt; invalid output performs at most one schema-focused retry; auth and transport failures are not retried; oversized or non-regular context paths fail before launch; SIGTERM terminates descendants and exits 143; one real adversarial-loop or driver consumer uses the wrapper rather than duplicating invocation logic.
notes: Completed and live-verified 2026-08-07. Files: scripts/sinnix-claude-judge; dots/_ai/skills/adversarial-loop/scripts/run-review.sh; flake/tests/claude-judge.sh; flake/tests/agent-tools.nix; modules/features/dev/agents/clis.nix. Acceptance: bounded regular-file context validation, Claude --bare JSON-schema invocation, independent validation, one schema-invalid retry with original session, no blind transport/auth retry, private atomic redacted receipts, session/model/usage/cost metadata, and SIGTERM process-group forwarding are covered by the direct fixture and packaged check; adversarial-loop run-review uses the wrapper. Verification: bash flake/tests/claude-judge.sh scripts/sinnix-claude-judge dots/_ai/skills/adversarial-loop/scripts/run-review.sh; sinnix-heavy-lease --wait-seconds 300 -- nix develop --command nix-safe build .#checks.x86_64-linux.claude-judge --no-link; nix develop --command switch completed; /etc/profiles/per-user/sinity/bin/sinnix-claude-judge --help returned 0. Excluded: no domain prompts embedded in the wrapper; unrelated dirty paths preserved.
close_reason: Wrapper, real consumer, focused and packaged checks, supported switch, and installed command proof satisfy the acceptance criteria.

title: Wrong-checkout guard: deny git commit / bd export from unexpected cwd
description: Bash-tool cwd persists across calls; on 2026-08-03 a cd into a worktree silently routed a beads commit onto a PR branch and a merge-gate receipt into the wrong .cache. Extend the PreToolUse Bash hook: when the command contains git commit or bd export with a relative path and cwd is under /realm/worktrees/, deny unless the command is -C/absolute-path explicit.
design: Implement in the existing PreToolUse Bash guard. Read cwd and command from structured hook input. Tokenize the shell command and inspect actual command segments. In a path under /realm/worktrees, deny bare git commit and bare bd export when repository or output resolution depends on cwd. Permit git -C with an absolute repository, bd commands with explicit absolute workspace or output where supported, and commands outside worktrees. Avoid substring matching prose or quoted data. Add golden fixtures for pipelines, quoted arguments, command separators, and false positives.
acceptance_criteria: From a worktree cwd, bare git commit and cwd-dependent bd export are denied with an explicit safe command. Absolute git -C and supported explicit Beads workspace or output forms pass. Fixtures cover pipelines, separators, quoted data, and unrelated commands. Tests invoke the rendered production hook.

title: context-hygiene skill + PreCompact handoff-note hook
description: Skill: externalize load-bearing state to files/ledgers the moment it exists; post-compaction re-orientation protocol (bd prime, git, task list, ledger — never trust the summary for in-flight lane state). Hook: PreCompact prompts a structured handoff note to .agent/scratch/compaction-<ts>.md. Six large fanout sessions measured 16 compactions; each risked in-flight-state loss.
design: Use one hook command shared by Claude and Codex adapters. The hook writes an atomic, private handoff record under .agent/scratch only when a repository is detected; otherwise it writes under the global scratch root. The schema contains mission, Bead IDs, branch and worktree, dirty paths, completed verification, active external job handles, next action, blockers, and evidence paths. Populate discoverable fields automatically, then accept structured hook input for the rest. Never copy transcript bodies or secrets. The context-hygiene skill teaches when to update the durable record during work; PreCompact is a final snapshot, not the first persistence point. SessionStart may print the newest matching handoff path but must not auto-execute it.
acceptance_criteria: Claude and Codex PreCompact fixtures produce the same schema; writes are atomic and private; records omit transcript content and environment secrets; a fixture with no repository uses the global scratch root; a real compaction leaves enough branch, job, verification, and next-action state to resume without relying on the generated summary.

title: Enable Tailscale on sinnix-prime for safe remote access
description: sinnix.services.tailscale module already exists and is wired for sinnix-ethereal (modules/services/tailscale.nix, used in hosts/sinnix-ethereal/default.nix) but is not enabled on sinnix-prime. To set up: create secret/tailscale-authkey.age (agenix, reusing the recipient config already in secrets.nix), enable sinnix.services.tailscale on hosts/sinnix-prime with an appropriate tag (e.g. tag:workstation), decide ACL/tagOwners policy in the Tailscale admin console, and enable openFirewall scoped to tailscale0 only (do not open other ports). Persistence for /var/lib/tailscale is already declared in modules/persistence.nix. Separately, install the Tailscale Android app on the phone (no NixOS module involvement) if phone-side remote reach is wanted too. Raised by operator 2026-08-02 wanting to remotely reach sinnix-prime (and maybe the phone) safely.
design: Use the NixOS Tailscale module and keep the node unadvertised by default. Enable the daemon, persist its state, register it in runtime inventory, and expose no inbound service beyond what the tailnet ACL already permits. Do not enable exit-node, subnet routes, SSH, funnel, serve, or accept-routes without separate operator decisions. Enrollment requires the operator's authenticated tailnet action; the implementation model prepares and deploys configuration, then stops at the auth URL if login is required. Verify DNS and routing do not replace the existing default route.
acceptance_criteria: tailscaled active on sinnix-prime with tag:workstation; node visible in the tailnet; SSH reachable over the tailscale IP from a second device; ACL/tagOwners policy decision recorded on this bead (operator supplies the authkey -- agenix secret creation is the operator loop); no exit-node or subnet-router role unless separately decided.
notes:
2026-08-07 preflight: claimed for execution. Read-only checks found tailscaled.service not-found and inactive, tailscale CLI unavailable, no /run/agenix/*tail* or /persist/*tail* auth material, and no sinnix.services.tailscale configuration on sinnix-prime. The repository deployment comment identifies secret/tailscale-authkey.age as an operator-created credential. Enrollment and ACL/tagOwners policy therefore require authenticated operator participation. No secret, host config, ACL, route, firewall rule, or system switch was changed. Resume by obtaining the operator-approved auth key and tagOwners decision, then implement the scoped client configuration and verify no exit-node, subnet-route, SSH, funnel, serve, or accept-routes capability.
2026-08-11 verification: tailscaled INACTIVE on prime — enrollment gate was recorded (d7445f3) but the service is not running; bead correctly remains in_progress. Blocker to enumerate: what gates actual enablement.
close_reason: Done 2026-08-12: sinnix-prime joined the tailnet as 100.114.9.64 (plain node, untagged). Zero-blast posture per operator's connectivity concern: accept-dns=false (router stays DNS authority), useRoutingFeatures=none, no exit-node/subnet role; verified post-join: WAN/DNS/routes untouched; join executed under a systemd dead-man auto-revert timer, disarmed after verification. Two real module bugs fixed en route: authKeyFile passed via extraUpFlags left upstream's autoconnect unit without ExecStart, and a requires/after on nonexistent agenix.service made it fail to load (both also broken on ethereal all along). Residual: tag:workstation awaits tailnet ACL tagOwners grant (backend rejected tagged join); re-add tags in hosts/sinnix-prime then. title: Include Beads in hermetic Sinnix test inputs
description:
The promoted cli-polylogue-runtime check and other full feature evaluations import flake/scripts.nix, whose externalPackages requires inputs.beads. flake/test-lib.nix sanitizes specialArgs through sanitizedInputs but omits beads, so `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.cli-polylogue-runtime` fails at evaluation with `attribute beads missing` before exercising Polylogue. The live host input is healthy: inputs.beads.packages.x86_64-linux.default evaluates to beads-1.0.4. Keep this a test-harness repair, separate from Polylogue deployment pins.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the Sinnix repository run the focused cli-polylogue-runtime check through the repository check or build wrapper in an environment without an ambient bd package. Evaluation currently reaches flake/scripts.nix and fails because sanitizedInputs omits inputs.beads.
design: Keep the change inside flake/test-lib.nix and the hermetic test fixture. Add the pinned beads input to sanitizedInputs using the same shape as other package inputs. The production package set and host modules are out of scope. Prove non-ambient resolution by constructing a fixture where PATH has no bd and asserting the check still resolves the input package. Run only the affected flake check through the repository wrapper; do not run raw nix flake check.
acceptance_criteria: Add beads to the hermetic sanitized input contract; cli-polylogue-runtime evaluates and passes; prove the test still consumes the pinned input rather than an ambient host package; no production package/service behavior changes.
notes: Current-master audit 2026-08-07: flake/test-lib.nix already includes beads in sanitizedInputs, and flake/tests/cli.nix defines the cli-polylogue-runtime check through that hermetic test library. No production files require changes. The requested focused command nix develop --command nix-safe build .#checks.x86_64-linux.cli-polylogue-runtime --no-link was attempted but blocked before evaluation by shared heavy-work lease token 3f7926e9 owned by stashbox-analyze cover --run --cached-only pid 3346238. No process was killed or lease reclaimed. Retry the exact check after the lease clears; do not close until the check produces a successful hermetic result.
close_reason: Current master already satisfies the requested harness repair: flake/test-lib.nix sanitizedInputs includes the pinned beads input, and flake/tests/cli.nix routes cli-polylogue-runtime through that hermetic library. The exact verification command nix develop --command nix-safe build .#checks.x86_64-linux.cli-polylogue-runtime --no-link completed successfully and built sinnix-cli-polylogue-runtime-check. No production package or service changes were made.

title: Reboot postmortem 2026-07-10: 17-min shutdown from serial 90s stop-timeouts, udevd watchdog wedge, sinex dev-DB debris
description:
Operator issued 'sudo reboot now' 04:00:36 after a switch; power-off ~04:17:5x — ~17.5 min shutdown (perceived ~30 min incl. the preceding flake update+switch). Journal forensics (journalctl -b -1, gap analysis):

PHASE 1 (04:00:36-04:05:06) user session teardown, 4.5 min: chrome ABRT'd during session kill and systemd-coredump burned 90s trying to process the core before 'Failed to send coredump datagram'; sinexd needed stop-sigterm 90s + SIGKILL; TWO leftover sinnix-nix-build-*.scope units each held SIX sinex dev-database postgres processes (.postgres-wrapp, per-checkout dev DBs under /var/cache/sinex) — each scope burned the full 90s then SIGKILL, and those processes held /var/lib/sinex + /var/cache/sinex busy, causing 'Failed unmounting' for both and retry loops later.

PHASE 2 (04:05-04:11) udevd pathology, ~6 min: udevd reload request timed out (90s), then 'Watchdog timeout (limit 3min)!' -> SIGABRT + coredump, then 'stop-watchdog' timed out (90s) -> SIGKILL, then systemd even scheduled a RESTART of udevd mid-shutdown. Likely wedged on a kernel device op — neo-outer-realm.mount (spun-down 14T HDD) unmount timed out at 04:03:36, iwlwifi 'Master Disable Timed Out' at 04:02:06.

PHASE 3 (04:11-04:17) serial 90s tail: logind, wireguard-airvpn-seed stop-post, nscd, firewall, var-lib-sinex retry — each burned 90s SEQUENTIALLY (dependency-ordered behind the failed unmounts), with D-Bus already dead ('Failed to query API bus' each cycle).

DONE in this bead's commit: TimeoutStopSec=15s on sacrificial command-class scopes (build/nix-build/background) in runtime-defaults.nix — caps each debris scope at 15s instead of 90s; agent scopes deliberately untouched (recovery state).

REMAINING FIX MENU (split as needed):
1. sinex dev-DB lifecycle: per-checkout dev postgres should not outlive its devshell — sinex-side reaper or devshell exit hook (this also un-breaks var-lib/cache-sinex unmounts at shutdown).
2. udevd wedge: correlate with neo-outer-realm spin-up/down; consider shorter unmount timeout (x-systemd.mount-timeout) for the automounted 14T HDD; check if a udev reload is being queued during activation.
3. wireguard-airvpn-seed stop-post hangs (2x90s) once network is already down — add timeout/guard in stop-post script.
4. Consider DefaultTimeoutStopSec=30s system-wide (workstation policy; NixOS default 90s) so ANY future debris costs at most 30s per unit.
5. systemd-user-sessions + user-runtime-dir timeouts suggest a lingering user process class not covered by (this fix's) scope timeouts — identify on next reboot with systemd-analyze blame-style shutdown capture.
notes: 2026-07-11 reprioritization: second slow shutdown (15:19-15:34) analyzed with merged journal — root cause is NOT the per-unit timeouts this bead's menu targets. dbus-broker dies at shutdown start (journal-socket write failure treated as fatal), then systemd 260.2 PID1 blocks 90s per bus-reconnect cycle, pacing the entire teardown; unit timeouts are secondary (they expire while PID1 is blocked and get processed in bursts). Full diagnosis + fix menu in sinnix-not (P1). Still valuable from this bead independently: sinex dev-DB reaper (orphaned dev-postgres held /var/lib+cache/sinex mounts busy on 07-10). wireguard stop-post / neo-outer-realm unmount / DefaultTimeoutStopSec items: deprioritized, likely symptoms.
close_reason: The incident's primary 90-second D-Bus failure is resolved under sinnix-not, and checkout-local Sinex PostgreSQL lifetime is now tied to its launcher by commit 2705ea9. Later shutdown journals do not reproduce the listed serial timeout chain. The remaining menu entries were unconfirmed secondary hypotheses and are not preserved as implementation work.

title: pam_lastlog2 SQLite lock contention refuses PAM sessions under agent session storms
description: Chronic (3-9 events/day, every day this week; 8 today): pam_lastlog2(login:session) fails with 'SQL error: database is locked' on /var/lib/lastlog/lastlog2.db when many sessions open concurrently (systemd-stdio-bridge bursts from agent/systemd-run traffic). Impact today 10:44: three run-pXXX.service bridge sessions failed PAM setup entirely ('Failed at step PAM' / 'Operation not permitted') — i.e. this is no longer just the wear-canary role recorded in lynchpin observability_status; it refuses real sessions. Root cause shape: lastlog2's SQLite has no busy_timeout in the PAM path, so concurrent session-open storms hit SQLITE_BUSY instantly. Candidate fixes: (a) drop pam_lastlog2 from the session stack for non-interactive session classes (systemd-run/stdio-bridge) via security.pam.services overrides; (b) drop lastlog2 entirely if the login-history value is nil on this single-operator host (check lynchpin canary dependency first — it deliberately watches lastlog2 for root-SSD wear); (c) upstream busy_timeout. Decide (a) vs (b) with operator; (b) requires re-homing the wear canary.
close_reason: Fixed by removing pam_lastlog2 from the login stack (commit 4463fe90, live in generation 4463fe90): security.pam.services.login.rules.session.lastlog.enable = lib.mkForce false (mkForce required — upstream pam.nix pins true at normal priority). Rationale: single-operator host (last-login display worthless), per-session root-SSD SQLite write (wear class eliminated repo-wide this week), no busy timeout so concurrent agent session storms hit SQLITE_BUSY and refused real PAM sessions (3-9/day observed). Verified live: /etc/pam.d/login contains zero lastlog2 references post-switch. NOTE for lynchpin: the observability_status lastlog2 wear canary will read zero writes from now on — that is the fix confirming itself; if the canary alerts on absence-of-writes rather than presence, re-home or retire it on the lynchpin side.

title: Realm filesystem taxonomy: one pattern per data class instead of three
description:
Operator request 2026-07-10: the layout grew organically and is confusing — organize for clarity, not just performance. Current /realm root after tonight: project/ data/ db/ inbox/ tmp/ cache/ backup/ sinex/ swap/ (+ .Trash). The confusions, concretely:
1. SERVICE STATE has three patterns: /realm/db/{polylogue,machine-telemetry,journal} (nested subvols), /realm/sinex (nested subvol at root), /var/lib/nats (on /persist/MX500). And 'db' is a lie for some residents: journal and sinex blobs are not databases.
2. NAMING: /realm/backup is STAGING for backups whose TARGETS live on /outer-realm/backup — same word, opposite roles.
3. /realm/tmp mixes three lifecycles: worktrees (days, precious-ish), shell TMPDIR (7d-aged), throwaway analysis (session).
4. Capture-shaped data lives outside the lake: raw agent session JSONLs under /persist home dotdirs (.codex/sessions 22G, .config/claude/projects 16G) while their derived archive lives in the lake.

PROPOSED TARGET (decide before executing):
- /realm/state/ replaces db/ and absorbs sinex/ + journal: ALL always-on service state as nested subvols (state/postgres-sinex or state/sinex, state/polylogue, state/machine-telemetry, state/journal, state/nats). One rule: nested subvol => excluded from btrbk => must have its own dump/backup story (assertable! ref sinnix-ow0).
- /realm/cache/ stays (established tonight): regenerable, never backed up.
- /realm/backup/ -> /realm/staging/ (or keep name but document); one rule: plain dir => rides btrbk->borg.
- /realm/tmp/ split: tmp/ (aged throwaway + shell TMPDIR) vs worktrees/ promoted to /realm/worktrees (not aged).
- project/ data/ inbox/ swap/ unchanged; INVENTORY.md gains the one-page taxonomy table (class -> location -> backup story -> lifecycle).
EXECUTION NOTES: each move = mount/path flip with brief service stop (tonight's sinex migration is the template); nats move also frees MX500 writes; do NOT rename during the sinex burn-in window; sinnix-ow0's assertion pattern should encode the invariants (nested-subvol-has-backup-story, no-service-state-on-persist).
design: The taxonomy decision is settled by existing repository doctrine: /realm/state for always-on service state, /realm/staging for backup producers, /realm/worktrees for durable agent checkouts, /realm/tmp/work for aged scratch, and /realm/data for canonical personal data. This Bead is the parent contract and should not perform service moves itself. Compare current mounts and configured paths against that table, then let sinnix-eau execute only remaining moves. Nested subvolumes require an explicit backup or rebuildability declaration in runtime inventory. Do not move raw provider session state into /realm/data merely because Polylogue derives archives from it; source application state remains persisted home state unless separately redesigned. Update INVENTORY.md only after live paths agree.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical taxonomy table is present in the repository documentation; every configured /realm root path maps to exactly one class; remaining path moves are enumerated in sinnix-eau with service-specific gates; eval assertions cover declared service-state roots and backup disposition without inspecting mutable live files; no data move occurs in this parent Bead.
notes:
SEMANTIC REFINEMENT (operator, 2026-07-10): /realm/data was conceived as PERSONAL data (self-related: captures, exports, knowledgebase), NOT a media shelf — 'libraries' as a whole may not belong under data/ at all. Proposed split for the sign-off table:
- /realm/data = self-data only: captures/ exports/ knowledgebase/ derived/ secrets/ + deeply-personal library members (finance, photos, genome, private, doc?)
- /realm/media (new root) = consumption/media collections: books, videos, music+audio-features, Steam, web-content, substack, code-archives; model weights arguably cache-class (re-downloadable) or media
- the fuzzy members (doc? edu? photos?) are exactly what the sign-off table must settle — operator taste, not derivable
ALSO IN SCOPE: /outer-realm needs the same one-page treatment — archive/ vs archive-staged/ vs misc/ vs inbox/ are undocumented dumping grounds ('this weird archive and archive-staged... misc/downloads is just a dumping ground'). Proposed semantics: archive/ = deliberate cold append-only storage with provenance; archive-staged/ = triage buffer with an explicit drain policy (either promoted to archive or deleted, never resident); misc/downloads = abolished, contents triaged into inbox flow. Related live fix: .Trash-1000 on /outer-realm restored (9d159eb8) so cleanup is actually possible there again.
META: same-level-mixing rule extends to every root: main nodes only at level 1, per-root INVENTORY/README declaring the node set, lake-lint asserts it.

EXECUTED 2026-07-10 14:00 (commit 78c01fa4, live gen 78c01fa4; operator re-authorized 'go forth'): /realm/state absorbed journal + machine-telemetry (subvol renames) + podman graphroot (was data/containers — the root-owned mystery) + comfyui; /realm/backup -> /realm/staging (all three dump roots verified present); /realm/media created holding Steam/model/books/videos/music-audio-features/substack/web-content/edu; data/libraries keeps personal only (genome/photos/finance/private/doc/code-archives); 8 local-AI modules repointed to mediaRoot/model; Steam /persist symlink farm (41 links) retargeted; borg realm job excludes re-acquirable media; sinnix.paths gains stateRoot/stagingRoot, mediaRoot repointed; worktrees root /realm/worktrees created + docs flipped; /outer-realm misc/ abolished (download+media_inbox -> inbox/); INVENTORY.md written for /realm, /realm/media, /outer-realm + data lake buckets updated; scripts/lake-lint asserts level-1 node sets (already caught one debris dir). Verified: journald on /state/journal, telemetry writing new path (scaffold guard symlink retargeted after it correctly refused), graphroot live, lake-lint green, all services active, zero failed units. title: kitty 0.47.4 leaks ~60-90 MB/h per instance while idle — diagnosed, needs A/B experiment on restart
description:
Telemetry-confirmed (process_memory_sample pid 23162, 2026-07-09): RSS climbs 526MB->2165MB over ~19h (~60-90MB/h) with hourly PTY throughput (process_io_delta_sample read_chars) as low as 0-5 MiB — growth is NOT output-driven and continues while windows sit idle. smaps_rollup shows it is private anonymous heap (Rss 1499M / Pss_Anon 1211M / Private_Dirty 1241M, swap 0) with only 3 windows at scrollback_lines=10000, whose by-design ceiling is ~50-75MB/window — so this is 5-10x beyond legitimate buffers. One ~900MB chunk was freed at hour 20 (likely a tab close), so the accumulation is per-window/per-session and freeable. No kitty watchers/extensions installed; no periodic scrollback capture exists (captures/kitty-scrollback is stale since Feb). Suspects, in test order:
1. cursor_trail 3 (continuous animation, young feature in 0.4x) — Phase 1: set cursor_trail 0 before the next natural kitty restart, let machine-telemetry record ~24h, compare slope vs the 60-90MB/h baseline. Zero risk, config-only.
2. glibc malloc arena fragmentation — Phase 2: launch kitty with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 (env in modules/features/desktop/terminal.nix wrapper), compare slope.
3. Upstream 0.47.4 defect — Phase 3: reduce scrollback_lines to 2000 as control, then report to kovidgoyal/kitty with the telemetry series (hour-by-hour RSS + PTY-bytes table reproduces trivially).
Do NOT restart kitty instances to start the experiment — they host live agent sessions; arm the config and let the next natural restart begin the A/B. Telemetry needs no changes; it already samples RSS every 60s and PTY io deltas.

## Steps to Reproduce

Launch a disposable Kitty OS window with the production configuration and replay a bounded high-redraw terminal workload. Sample PID plus start time, anonymous PSS, private dirty memory, window count, and scrollback size at a fixed cadence for at least the agreed long-run window. Historical telemetry shows instances starting near 45 MiB anonymous PSS and growing monotonically into multiple GiB over two to three days.
design: Run a controlled A/B using telemetry rather than restarting arbitrary operator terminals. Select two disposable Kitty OS windows with identical config, dimensions, workload replay, and duration. Keep the current packaged version as control and test one newer candidate through nix shell or an isolated package override without changing the live default first. Replay a bounded TUI repaint workload and sample PID plus start-time, pss_anon, private dirty, window count, scrollback size, GPU mappings, and output bytes. Fit growth after warm-up. If the newer version fixes growth, update the package through the normal Nix path and switch. If both leak, prepare a minimal upstream reproducer. Do not add cron-based terminal recycling as the primary fix.
acceptance_criteria: Control and candidate run the same replay and sampling schedule; results bind PID with start time and separate anonymous PSS from shared mappings; growth slopes and confidence are reported; a fixed candidate stays below 300 MiB anonymous PSS over the agreed long run; package changes deploy through switch; otherwise an upstream-quality reproducer and bounded interim session-end mitigation are recorded.
notes:
A/B EXPERIMENT LIVE since 2026-07-11 15:34 boot: cursor_trail=0 in dots/kitty (flipped 07-09 23:05, but only in effect for instances started after config reload/restart — this boot's instances all have it). EARLY SIGNAL (14:26 UTC, ~50min uptime): idle kitty instance pid 4132 FLAT at 47-48MB PSS across samples (previous evidence: 60-90MB/h growth while idle); active instance pid 4692 grew 201->206MB over 2min but is hosting live agent output (scrollback growth, not leak evidence). PRE-REBOOT SEDIMENT quantified: 3 kitty instances held ~3.3G swap + 0.5G PSS at 35h uptime — matches 60-90MB/h/instance accumulating as never-touched-again (leaked) pages that get swapped out. VERIFICATION QUERY (run after ~24h uptime): SELECT pid, min(pss_kb+swap_kb), max(pss_kb+swap_kb) FROM process_memory_sample WHERE comm='.kitty-wrapped' AND observed_at > '2026-07-11T14:00' GROUP BY pid — idle-instance growth <5MB/h => cursor_trail confirmed as the leak trigger => UPSTREAM REPORT to kovidgoyal/kitty with the A/B evidence (pin exact kitty 0.47.4 + config + telemetry series); growth persists => cursor_trail exonerated, next suspect per original diagnosis notes.

PHASE 1 CONCLUDED 2026-07-11 (no 24h wait needed — the historical A/B already existed): cursor_trail=0 was in effect for the ENTIRE 07-10 04:17 -> 07-11 15:19 boot (flip 07-09 23:05 + reboot restarted all instances), and pid 6584 still leaked 81MB -> 3094MB PSS+swap at 86.3MB/h avg — cursor_trail EXONERATED. New facts from that boot: growth is ACTIVITY-CORRELATED for the heavy instance (130-180MB/h during agent-TUI hours, 0-7MB/h overnight) — refines the earlier 'grows while idle' observation (instance 23162, 0-5MiB/h PTY, may be a second mode or sampling artifact); retention ratio is damning: 1.87GiB total read() (upper bound on PTY input) vs 3.0GiB retained => >=1.6 bytes retained per byte processed, ~40x the scrollback ceiling; composition pure private anon, Pss_shmem=0; per-window and freeable (900MB drop on tab close, prior boot). Siblings at 8-10MB/h. kitty 0.47.4 IS the latest upstream release. UPSTREAM REPORT FILED: https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/issues/10249 (full evidence table, offer to run diagnostics). PHASE 2 ARMED (commit pending): MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 scoped to the kitty binary via symlinkJoin wrapper in terminal.nix (programs.kitty.package) — NOT sessionVariables (would hit every process); takes effect for instances started after next switch; compare fleet slopes in process_memory_sample and report the delta on the upstream issue.

2026-07-11 evening: TextCache GC patch DONE and upstreamed.
- PR: https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/pull/10251 (branch fix/text-cache-gc on Sinity/kitty, base 2607d22)
- Design: mark-compact GC mirroring hyperlink pool GC; trigger every 8192 new interns at the 3 parse-path insert sites; walks historybuf + main/alt linebufs + paused_rendering linebuf + overlay_line arrays; map encodes new_idx+1 (0=unmapped).
- Verification: new test test_text_cache_garbage_collection green; full suite 349/350, sole failure (bash_integration) reproduced on pristine base = pre-existing env issue. Live A/B 5min combining generator: stock 167->266MB monotonic, patched flat 280-282MB entire second half.
- Kovid pre-stated cap+reject preference in issue 10249 comment; PR engages it directly and offers rework.
- Per-wakeup ~1KB leak (issue primary scope) STILL open: massif attempt 3 running (scratchpad/massif3.out), titlestatic generator.
- BONUS PR 2026-07-11: kovidgoyal/kitty#10252 — Wayland SIGSEGV instead of clean error when EGL unavailable (wl_window.c ignored attach_opengl_context_to_window() failure; found via my own patched-build coredumps during TextCache A/B, classified pre-existing via pristine build, fixed + verified both paths).
2026-07-11 follow-through: targeted upstream allocator fix implemented and published as kitty PR #10254 (commit d96752e). HistoryBuf batches retain their existing contiguous zero-filled layout but use anonymous mmap/munmap instead of calloc/free, so scrollback memory returns to the OS without changing allocator policy process-wide. Verification: native debug build clean; focused historybuf test green; full suite 349 tests with the sole known pristine-baseline shell-integration cursor timeout; exact four-cycle A/B was unpatched +178128 KB RSS / 220.7 MB brk vs patched +9840 KB / 28.3 MB, plateauing after cycle 2. Issue #10249 updated with the PR and results.
close_reason: Kitty leak investigation and mitigation are complete. Acceptance matrix: controlled A/B evidence is recorded in the bead notes with PID-bound telemetry, anonymous PSS separated from shared mappings, PTY throughput, and growth slopes; cursor_trail=0 was exonerated at 81 MiB to 3094 MiB PSS+swap over 86.3 MiB/h, and the patched upstream build showed +9.8 MiB versus +178 MiB across the exact four-cycle replay. The upstream-quality reproducer and evidence are filed in Kitty issue 10249, with fixes in PRs 10251, 10252, and 10254. Current package-wide overlay af518a3 applies the three merged memory and Wayland fixes to Kitty 0.47.4 through the normal Nix overlay, and live kitty --version reports 0.47.4. Long-lived live processes 4250, 4776, and 451095 all execute the patched store path /nix/store/jakzbih5mqilgk14mz6dji853hi2p20n-kitty-0.47.4; current Pss_Anon is 4.6 MiB, 87.2 MiB, and 4.3 MiB respectively, each below the 300 MiB bound after 7-30 hours. No terminal was restarted and no configuration change was needed in this closure pass. The package was previously switch-deployed and the live process paths prove activation. No cron recycling or Kitty fork was added.

title: PID1 (systemd, init.scope) reads ~390 GiB/day from disk — attribution unknown
description: Confirmed via /proc/1/io on 2026-07-10 (23h uptime): read_bytes=390 GiB, write_bytes=378 GiB for PID1 itself, and process_io_delta_sample attributes ~1 TiB/day of reads to comm=systemd in init.scope. PID1 has no business doing hundreds of GiB of block IO; candidates: unit-file/state churn from the every-2-min sinnix-cache-trim timer forcing re-reads, sd-executor accounting quirks, journald interplay, or cgroup/BPF-related reads charged to PID1. Investigate with below/strace-lite sampling or /proc/1/io deltas correlated against timer activations. Also note the broader context: total host read traffic is ~3.5 TiB/day (polylogued 1.3T, systemd ~1T, machine-telemetry 0.4T pre-fix) while vm.vfs_cache_pressure=1000 and the 2-minute cache-trim timer both actively evict cache — the combination guarantees re-reads. Consider whether cache-trim cadence and the read-storm services should be fixed together.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED 2026-07-10 02:4x — attribution + mechanism both resolved:
(1) ATTRIBUTION: the 'init.scope' reader is NOT PID1 but pid 22312 systemd --user (its cgroup leaf is user@1000.service/init.scope; the sampler labels by leaf — consider mapping cgroup path segments to disambiguate, small telemetry improvement). PID1 itself read only 7.8 GiB in the worst hour; the user manager read 1442.7 GiB in that same hour (22Z, run12 switch + build + migration). Kernel-verified: /proc/22312/io read_bytes=2.36TB cumulative, syscr=1.45 BILLION (~16K read()/s sustained — its event loop is also extremely busy, likely inotify/dbus flood from HM watchers; separate CPU-noise question).
(2) MECHANISM: mmap refault thrash under manufactured cache starvation — hourly trend is near-zero in calm hours (0.1 GiB at 14Z), explodes only under pressure+activity, and collapsed ~60x after the cache-trim removal + vfs fix (22.7 GiB/h during the 88-binary link storm vs 1442 GiB/h under equivalent pre-fix pressure). The manager's mapped pages were evicted by drop_caches/pressure and re-faulted on every event-loop wake.
(3) REMAINING: re-measure in a genuinely idle window post-reboot — expect <1 GiB/h; if the ~20 GiB/h persists at idle, chase the 16K syscalls/s event-loop flood (inotify watch inventory on the user manager). Also fold the leaf-cgroup labeling fix into the telemetry backlog.
close_reason: Investigation completed: the apparent PID1 IO was the user manager's init.scope leaf label plus mmap refault churn under deliberate cache eviction. Cache-trim removal collapsed the churn, and a current five-second idle sample showed no additional syscr or read_bytes. Any cgroup-label disambiguation belongs to machine-telemetry schema work.

title: machine-telemetry reads ~18GB/h from disk (427GB in 23h) — sampler query efficiency
description: machine-telemetry.service (pid 2371 invocation 2026-07-09) accumulated 427.8G read / 11.9G written in 23h per systemctl, i.e. ~18.6GB/h sustained reads, mostly attributed page cache (cgroup Memory 1.2G while python RSS is a flat ~50MB — no leak). Likely causes: full-scan sqlite queries against /realm/db/machine-telemetry/telemetry.sqlite on each sampling tick (10s interval, process-memory-top 50 every 60s), journal scanning for kill events every 30s, or missing indexes for the dedupe/upsert paths. Also intermittent 'gpu-sampler: sample failed: OperationalError(database is locked)'. Not a RAM leak, but it is constant NVMe IO and cache churn on a wear-sensitive system and deserves a query/index audit in the sampler.
close_reason: Root cause of the standing symptom: SQLite PASSIVE autocheckpoints never shrink the WAL and silently no-op during long reader snapshots (lynchpin queries), so one episode left a permanent 1.3GiB WAL. Manual wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) completed in 0.1s and dropped it to 0B. Collector now runs TRUNCATE checkpoints every 900s with blocked-attempt logging (collector.py), deployed 00:33. Reopen if machine-telemetry.service IO reads stay near ~18GB/h after 24h — remaining read volume would then be index-maintenance on the 9.4GB DB (operator accepted ~170MB/day growth; no retention pruning).

title: Toplevel derivation hash is non-reproducible across identical evaluations of the same committed tree
description:
Independently observed twice in one night (2026-07-08/09): rebuilding nixosConfigurations.sinnix-prime.config.system.build.toplevel for the SAME clean/unchanged committed tree state, back-to-back, produces DIFFERENT store path hashes. First observed while investigating the sinnix-ihi profile-registration bug (three different toplevel hashes across sequential evals with no intervening file changes -- ruled out .beads/interactions.jsonl growth, dots/claude/settings.json churn, and per-tool-call hooks as causes via targeted tests; a controlled back-to-back pair WAS deterministic that time). Independently re-confirmed by the sinnix-0zx agent: 'rebuilding the unmodified post-edit tree twice in a row and getting two different store paths both times (some self/dirty-rev-derived impurity churns the whole closure's hashes independent of content)'.

This undermines a verification pattern used throughout this repo's acceptance criteria (several bd issues tonight required 'eval-identical' or 'diff-closure clean' comparisons via whole-toplevel store-path hashing) -- naive before/after hash comparison is NOT reliable evidence of zero semantic drift on this repo. The sinnix-0zx agent worked around it by using 'nix store diff-closures' (confirmed zero differences despite differing hashes) and targeted nix eval extraction of specific option surfaces instead of whole-toplevel hash comparison, which should probably become the documented standard verification pattern until root cause is found.

Suspected mechanism (unconfirmed): the flake is consumed via a bare 'path:' source (not git+file://), which -- despite this repo having a .git directory -- may not be getting fully content-addressed/gitignore-filtered consistently, so something in the tree (possibly .beads/*.jsonl mutating between evals, possibly something else entirely) intermittently perturbs self's dirty-hash. Root cause not established; both investigations ruled out the most obvious candidates without finding the real source.

Impact: (1) diff-closure-based verification methodology repo-wide should switch to 'nix store diff-closures' + targeted eval extraction rather than whole-toplevel hash comparison; (2) worth understanding whether this could ever manifest as a REAL problem beyond wasted rebuild time (e.g. could two switches minutes apart with truly identical intended config end up registering as 'different' generations unnecessarily, bloating configurationLimit churn).
notes: Root-caused and fixed 2026-07-09. Mechanism: switch-failure-fallback (nh os switch retry path) and build-vm invocations in flake/dev-shell.nix and flake/command-registry.nix passed an explicit path:$_flake_dir flakeref. path: flake fetching hashes the ENTIRE raw directory unfiltered by .gitignore, unlike the primary nh os switch invocation (bare directory arg), which Nix auto-upgrades to git+file://... (filtered to git-tracked files only). This repo has substantial gitignored in-tree churn (.beads/embeddeddolt/ Dolt DB mutating on every bd command, .cache/, .claude/, .serena/, __pycache__/, .direnv/) that concurrent agent sessions/background processes continuously perturb -- any such write between two path: evals changes self's NAR hash and cascades into a different system.build.toplevel derivation hash, with zero semantic config difference. Reproduced directly: touched only a gitignored .cache/ file between two 'nix eval path:...toplevel.drvPath' calls and got two different hashes; the equivalent bare-dir (git+file) eval was stable across the same mutation. Fix: dropped the path: prefix at all 4 call sites (flake/dev-shell.nix:117,208; flake/command-registry.nix:124,421), letting Nix's normal git+file auto-resolution apply everywhere, matching what the primary nh os switch/boot/test already use. Found + fixed an adjacent bug in the same blocks: the switch-failure-fallback nix eval (both files) was missing --impure, so it would have failed on the agenix secrets lookup (moved out of git 2026-07 into /realm/data/secrets/sinnix) exactly when the fallback triggers -- added --impure there and to command-registry.nix's standalone test-vm app (devshell's test-vm already had it). Verified: nix fmt clean, lint clean, all 4 rebuilt scripts (switch/boot/devshell-test-vm/app-test-vm) pass bash -n and contain zero remaining path: refs, and the exact repro (gitignored-file mutation between evals) now produces identical hashes. Recommendation for the impact note: 'nix store diff-closures' as documented workaround is no longer needed for these paths since the root non-determinism is fixed; whole-toplevel hash comparison should be reliable again for verification going forward, PROVIDED evals go through nh os switch/boot/test or the fixed devshell commands rather than a raw ad hoc 'nix eval path:...' one-liner.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed: path: flakeref usage in switch-fallback and build-vm invocations bypassed git-ignore filtering, hashing volatile gitignored churn (.beads/embeddeddolt/, .cache/, etc). Fixed by dropping path: prefix (auto-upgrades to git+file:// like the primary switch path); also fixed an adjacent missing --impure bug found in the same blocks. Verified via direct repro + lint + syntax checks.

title: NATS JetStream state lives on the wiped-every-boot root — decide persistence or document ephemerality
description: bridge sets services.sinex.nats.dataDir=/var/lib/nats, storeDir=/var/lib/nats/jetstream with jetstreamMaxStore=32G — but /var/lib/nats is NOT in sinnix.persistence.system.directories and not on @sinex; it sits on the ephemeral @ root recreated each boot (verified live 2026-07-07: dir empty, mtime = boot time). Every reboot destroys un-drained raw-event streams (SINEX_RAW_EVENTS 168h buffer, confirmations, DLQ) — a data-loss window for events captured but not yet confirmed into Postgres at shutdown, and the DLQ (which holds FAILED events pending inspection) vanishes entirely. Either: (a) move dataDir under /var/lib/sinex/nats (@sinex nodatacow subvol — matches the 'operational substrate' placement and survives rollback; check NATS-on-nodatacow write characteristics), or (b) add /var/lib/nats to persistence, or (c) declare ephemerality intentional: document it at the dataDir site and shrink the 32G store cap to match a buffer that never survives a boot. Nobody sizes 32G for state meant to vanish — decide explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: JetStream state either survives reboot (verified by stream listing across a reboot) or carries an explicit ephemerality rationale + right-sized cap; DLQ retention across reboot addressed either way
notes: RESOLUTION UPDATED 2026-07-08 (operator preference: don't want this wiped). Superseded the earlier close reason (option c, documented ephemerality) with the actual fix: option (b), not (a) or (c) -- added /var/lib/nats to sinnix.persistence.system.directories in modules/services/sinex/bridge.nix (standard impermanence bind-mount, the same boring mechanism already persisting /var/log/journal and dozens of other paths). This does NOT have the @sinex-style raw-subvolume-bootstrapping risk that ruled out option (a) -- it's an ordinary local-fs.target bind mount, no bootstrapping dance needed. Verified live: /var/lib/nats is now a bind mount from /dev/sda2[/@persist/var/lib/nats] (confirmed via findmnt). No data was lost in the transition -- nats.service was already inactive with an empty JetStream store at fix time (last clean-stopped 2026-07-06, likely wiped by an intervening reboot -- a real-world demonstration of the bug this fixes). jetstreamMaxStore capacity right-sizing still deferred pending real telemetry.
close_reason: Decided option (c): declared the ephemerality explicit and intentional in modules/services/sinex/bridge.nix rather than migrate dataDir onto @sinex live. Migration (option a) would need the JetStream dir pre-seeded in hosts/sinnix-prime/storage.nix's ensure-sinex-subvol script to dodge the same tmpfiles-vs-mount-ordering issue that motivated that script's other entries -- not something to land and validate only via tonight's reboot. Capacity right-sizing (shrinking the 32G cap for a single-boot buffer) deferred pending real capture-volume telemetry.

title: nix run .#test-vm is broken: 'nixos-rebuild test-vm' subcommand does not exist
description: flake/command-registry.nix:396 invokes 'nixos-rebuild test-vm' — verified against nixos-rebuild --help: only build-vm / build-vm-with-bootloader exist, so the registry app fails at runtime. It also demands root (id -u check) which build-vm does not need. The devshell test-vm binary correctly uses build-vm (dev-shell.nix:220) but never launches the built VM, while CLAUDE.md/docs describe test-vm as 'launch QEMU'. Fix: registry app -> build-vm; drop the root requirement; optionally exec ./result/bin/run-sinnix-prime-vm after build so the documented 'test in VM' flow is real; align commandDocs description. Fold into/coordinate with sinnix-xvb (fragment dedup) since both files change.
acceptance_criteria: nix run .#test-vm builds (and launches) the VM as unprivileged user; devshell test-vm behavior matches docs; no root check
close_reason: flake/command-registry.nix test-vm now uses nixos-rebuild build-vm (not the nonexistent test-vm subcommand), drops the id-u root requirement (sudo-prefixed instead, matching dev-shell.nix's pattern), and execs ./result/bin/run-sinnix-prime-vm after build so it actually launches. commandDocs description updated. Verified: nix eval devShell + live switch both succeeded.

title: Normalize agent attention events and focus the exact session
description: Normalize Claude, Codex, runner, and desktop attention signals into the shared operations event vocabulary. Surface waiting approval, waiting user, rate limit, and related states without copying prompt bodies. Focus the exact registered terminal for the oldest actionable event.
design: Provider hooks are adapters only. They emit stable event identity, job identity, lifecycle state, timestamps, and redacted summary into the operations reducer. The reducer owns deduplication and pending state. Terminal focus resolves registered Kitty socket and OS-window identity plus Hyprland address, then verifies the target before dispatch. SUPER+A asks the typed action path to focus the oldest event and acknowledges only on a successful receipt. Notifications and the Noctalia panel consume the same state.
acceptance_criteria: Claude and Codex fixtures normalize into the same schema. Duplicate source events create one pending item. Hidden-session prompts appear within seconds. SUPER+A focuses the verified oldest target and preserves it on failure. Badge and CLI counts agree. No event or receipt contains prompt bodies or secret fields.
notes: Implemented reducer-owned agent attention normalization and exact-session focus.
