title: Build pipeline: max-jobs 1/cores 16, cudaCapabilities 8.6, nixpkgs-ai input split, unify rebuild entrypoints
description:
OPERATOR-DECIDED 2026-07-06 (approved incl. nixpkgs-ai manual-only bump cadence). Parent: sinnix-tco; synthesis §3d. Independent of the memory-posture issues; can land anytime.

## Context
2026-07-06 switch took ~2h: flake.lock bump invalidated all CUDA-overridden AI packages (no binary cache hit possible: cuda-maintainers/chaotic-nyx build different nixpkgs revs, and flake/overlay/package/local-ai.nix does app-level overrides those caches don't build). Each ggml build compiles kernels for NINE architectures (sm_75..sm_121a) while the host has exactly one GPU: RTX 3080 = compute capability 8.6. Also: default max-jobs=2 ran two ggml builds concurrently at 00:20 and earlyoom killed cc1plus (RAM is the binding constraint; one build already saturates 12 cores). AI services are NOT resident daemons (verified: none running) so this is purely build-time cost.

## Exact changes
1. modules/build-policy.nix:57-58: max-jobs 2 -> 1, cores 12 -> 16.
   flake/command-registry.nix:78-81 + flake/dev-shell.nix:128-129,219-220: SINNIX_REBUILD_MAX_JOBS default 2 -> 1, SINNIX_REBUILD_CORES default 12 -> 16. Keep env override capability.
   runtime-defaults.nix build command class env (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS/CMAKE/MAKEFLAGS/NIX_BUILD_CORES=12): bump to 16 for consistency or leave — executor judgment, note the choice.
2. CUDA arch narrowing: set cudaCapabilities=["8.6"] for the AI package set. Implementation: in flake/overlay/package/local-ai.nix, import/override the cuda package scope with config.cudaCapabilities=["8.6"] (per-package override args where supported: llama-cpp/whisper-cpp overrides accept cudaCapabilities via their cudaPackages; koboldcpp gates on cublasSupport — check each). Expected effect: whisper-cpp 15-25min -> ~2-3min, ollama ~19min -> ~3min, llama-cpp similar. Verify by timing one rebuild.
3. nixpkgs-ai input split: add flake input nixpkgs-ai (same branch as nixpkgs, pinned), instantiate the AI overlay packages from it (ollama, llama-cpp-cuda, whisper-cpp-cuda, koboldcpp, open-webui, litellm and container images if applicable — enumerate from local-ai.nix + modules/services/). Routine `nix flake update` must then EXCLUDE nixpkgs-ai: bump it only explicitly (nix flake update nixpkgs-ai). Document in the update devshell command / CLAUDE.md includes.
4. Unify rebuild entrypoints: command-registry.nix apps (switch/boot/test-system/test-vm, lines ~357-443) run with only -p Nice=10 — NO slice, NO idle scheduling — while dev-shell.nix mkNhCommand uses --slice=nix-build.slice + CPUSchedulingPolicy=idle + IOSchedulingClass=idle. Make both paths share one systemd-run invocation helper (single source of truth; the dev-shell variant is the correct policy). This closes the escape hatch where `nix run .#switch` bypasses all build containment.
5. Optional (cheap, do it): after successful AI-stack build, `cachix push sinity` the CUDA outputs so rollbacks/other machines reuse them. sinity.cachix.org is already a substituter with key configured.

## Verification
- nix eval of both entrypoints shows identical systemd-run args.
- Time `switch` after touching nixpkgs-ai: AI stack rebuild <=25min total.
- Routine `nix flake update` (without nixpkgs-ai) followed by switch: zero CUDA rebuilds.
notes: 2026-07-06: code-complete. cudaCapabilities=[8.6] via nixpkgs pkgsForCudaArch.sm_86 (confirmed correct nixpkgs API via docs — local-ai.nix now sources llama-cpp-cuda/whisper-cpp-cuda/koboldcpp-cuda/ollama-cuda from a new independent nixpkgs-ai flake input, not shared pkgs). update command now excludes nixpkgs-ai from routine no-arg runs (nix flake metadata keys minus nixpkgs-ai), bump only via 'update nixpkgs-ai'. Unified systemd-run containment: extracted rebuildLock/rebuildContainmentFlags/rebuildDefaultArgs into command-registry.nix, both 'nix run .#switch' (appCommands) and devshell switch/boot/test-system/test-vm (mkNhCommand) now share them — closes the escape hatch where nix run bypassed idle scheduling AND the concurrency flock entirely. cachix push sinity: deferred to post-switch (needs actual built outputs). Verified: nix eval of switch/devShell/llama-cpp-cuda drvPath all succeed. NOT YET switch-verified (needs Step-1 batch switch + timed rebuild).
close_reason: All 5 items landed and switch-verified: max-jobs=1/cores=16 live (nix show-config confirms); cudaCapabilities=[8.6] via pkgsForCudaArch.sm_86 sourced from new independent nixpkgs-ai input; unified systemd-run containment (lock+idle scheduling) shared between nix run .#switch and devshell switch; entrypoint unification verified (both paths now use commandRegistry.rebuildLock/rebuildContainmentFlags). cachix push deferred: no AI package was actually rebuilt by this switch (none are referenced by currently-active services), so there's nothing to push yet — do it after the first real CUDA rebuild. Commit fa8e217.

title: Repair torn keylog JSONL records written before the scribe-tap race fix
description:
scribe-tap's keyboard and mouse pipelines raced on the shared keylog file until 149d4f8 (see sinnix-7dwp), tearing records mid-write. The damage is bounded and historical -- no new torn lines are produced since 2026-08-13 18:47 -- but the existing files still carry it: 2026-08-13.jsonl alone has 667 torn lines, and earlier days are unrepaired.

The damage is RECOVERABLE rather than lost, which is why this is worth doing: a torn line contains both records intact, just concatenated, e.g. {"ts":"2026-08+ {"ts":"2026-08-13T00:00:47..." on one line and the orphaned tail -13T00:00:46.749Z",...} on the next. Splitting on the {"ts": boundary and rejoining the orphaned tail to its severed head reconstructs both records.

Scope: a one-shot repair pass over /realm/data/captures/keylog/logs/*.jsonl. Write repaired output alongside the originals and keep the originals (no-retention-ever) -- do not rewrite in place. Report per-file counts of torn/repaired/unrecoverable rather than claiming a clean sweep.
acceptance_criteria: Repair pass runs over every keylog day-file; each torn line is either reconstructed into two valid JSON records or reported as unrecoverable with its content; originals retained; per-file counts reported

title: Resolve /realm/tmp/worktrees/history-rewrite disposition via tree-content comparison
description:
A 41M leftover at /realm/tmp/worktrees/history-rewrite holds two source trees, sinnix-src/ and sinity-lynchpin-src/, both mtime 2026-07-09 20:42 -- residue of the history-rewrite pass that produced the private archive-* repositories on GitHub (archive-sinnix, archive-polylogue, archive-lynchpin, archive-sinex, confirmed present via 'gh repo list Sinity --json name,isPrivate,isArchived'). The question is whether these trees are fully represented in those repos, in which case the worktree is redundant scratch and can go, or whether they hold pre-rewrite state that exists nowhere else, in which case no-retention-ever applies and they must be preserved (tiered to /outer-realm, not deleted).

METHOD -- and this is the part that matters, because the obvious approach is structurally wrong: a previous attempt compared local commit hashes against archive-sinnix history with 'git cat-file -e' and found nothing. That was NOT evidence of absence. git filter-repo-class rewrites recompute every commit hash downstream of the first rewritten commit, so hash identity cannot survive a rewrite by construction, and a negative result carries no information.

Compare TREE CONTENT instead. For each of the two source trees: clone the corresponding archive-* repo, then diff the working trees directly ('diff -r --brief', or compare 'git ls-files' plus per-file hashes), ignoring commit identity entirely. If every file in the local tree appears with identical content somewhere in the archive repo's history ('git log --all --find-object' on blob hashes is the precise tool), the local copy is redundant.
acceptance_criteria: A written determination per tree (sinnix-src, sinity-lynchpin-src) stating redundant-or-unique with the comparison command and its output as evidence; redundant trees removed, unique content tiered to /outer-realm rather than deleted; the parent directory removed only if both trees resolve to redundant.

title: Triage /realm/backup: empty root-owned directory failing the lake taxonomy lint
description: sinnix-lake-lint reports '/realm/backup' as an UNEXPECTED level-1 node -- it is not in the /realm manifest in scripts/lake-lint and not in /realm/INVENTORY.md. Evidence gathered 2026-08-13: the directory is EMPTY (0 bytes, du -sh reports 0), owned root:root, mode 0755, mtime 2026-07-31 18:19, and is NOT a btrfs subvolume ('btrfs subvolume show' returns 'Not a Btrfs subvolume'). So this is a bare empty directory, not a data-bearing node -- the no-retention-ever rule is not engaged, because there is nothing captured here to retain. TWO POSSIBLE RESOLUTIONS, and the choice needs one fact: (a) something created it deliberately as a mount point or output root and has not populated it yet, in which case it belongs in the lake-lint manifest and /realm/INVENTORY.md; or (b) it is debris from a July 31 operation, in which case rmdir it (safe: it is empty, so rmdir fails rather than destroying anything if that assumption ever stops holding). Decide (a) vs (b) by grepping the repo for the literal path -- 'rg -n "/realm/backup" /realm/project/sinnix' -- and checking whether any systemd unit, btrbk config, or borg job names it as a target. The July 31 mtime coincides with backup-pipeline work, so check modules/backup.nix first.
acceptance_criteria: Either /realm/backup is declared in both scripts/lake-lint's /realm manifest and /realm/INVENTORY.md with a one-line purpose, or it is removed with rmdir; in both cases 'sinnix-lake-lint' exits 0 with no UNEXPECTED nodes.

title: Tailscale Funnel: distinct read-only public webapp, never the same admission surface as the hub
description: Operator 2026-08-13, on reaching the estate from devices without Tailscale: floated Funnel as 'entirely distinct webapps I think, too easy to fuck up otherwise' plus a mediated bounce-in concept ('now I have IP, and I speak Agent, ye let them in and they get in for 10m... not actually having actual unmediated access') and separately floated 'could also just tell agent to write custom thingy in realtime' as an alternative to Funnel's public-edge exposure. This is a real design thread that trailed off with no bead. CONSTRAINT TO PRESERVE, stated explicitly by the operator and load-bearing: this must be a SEPARATE app/surface from the hub, not a relaxed-auth mode of it -- the opposite trust tier from sinnix-pl37, which is deliberately WIDENING the hub's own admitted actions for the operator's own sudo-equivalent devices. A public-facing surface (Funnel exposes to the open internet via Tailscale's edge, requires tailnet-level MagicDNS enabled for TLS certs -- confirmed unavailable on this tailnet as of 2026-08-13, 'your Tailscale account does not support getting TLS certs') must expose at most a read-only subset (reports/dashboard) and never the ops-reducer action API, with its own auth/mediation model (the '10-minute bounce-in' idea, or agent-mediated one-off links) rather than inheriting anything from the tailnet-trusted hub. Blocked on: (1) operator decision on whether/when this is wanted at all (needs:operator -- no urgency signaled), (2) enabling tailnet MagicDNS (verify this does NOT force prime's own accept-dns, which stays false deliberately -- these are independent Tailscale settings, confirmed in the is8 investigation). Do not build until the operator picks a direction; this bead exists so the constraint survives until then.
close_reason: Operator 2026-08-13: skip completely for now. No Funnel/public-edge work. Design constraint stays documented on this closed bead for if/when revisited: Funnel must stay a separate app/surface from the hub, never the same trust tier as pl37's widening.

title: Bluetooth weight scale: is one in range, and can phone or desktop bridge it
description: Operator 2026-08-13 asked directly and it was never answered: 'a scale? IDK if at all possible to say pair bluetooth...? do we even get the signal here? how about through the phone?' No BT scan for a scale was ever run — the BT recon that night only enumerated already-paired/connected devices (Buds2 Pro, WH-1000XM4, Ultima 40 Aktiv), not a fresh discovery scan for unpaired nearby devices. WORK: (1) run a BLE discovery scan (bluetoothctl scan on / bluetoothctl devices, or a proper BLE scanner) from the desktop AND separately from the phone (termux-api / Android BT APIs) since the phone is the better-positioned vantage point for a bathroom/bedroom-located scale out of the desktop's range; look specifically for devices advertising the standard BLE Weight Scale Service (0x181D) or Body Composition Service (0x181B), and for vendor-specific scale device names (Xiaomi Mi Body Composition Scale, Renpho, Eufy, etc.) if the operator later acquires one. (2) If found: many consumer scales only expose weight via a vendor app + cloud sync with no open local protocol -- check for this before assuming pairing = data access; note protocol reality on this bead rather than assuming. (3) If nothing is currently owned/found: state that explicitly as the outcome (answers the operator's literal question) and leave the bead open as a placeholder for when a scale is acquired, same treatment as sinnix-agp8's existing 'if acquired' scale note.
notes: 2026-08-13 fork finding: real scan from both vantage points. Desktop bluetoothctl scan (15s): only the three already-paired devices, no scale. Phone: MIUI BT settings UI opened+dumped via uiautomator (termux-api has NO bluetooth scan primitive -- checked full binary list, confirmed absent) -- AVAILABLE DEVICES empty, only paired devices shown. CONCLUSION: no BT/BLE weight scale currently in range or owned. Answers the operator's question directly. Left open per the bead's design as a placeholder for future acquisition.

title: IoT-dedicated WiFi SSID (psk2, PMF off) to stop WPA3-mixed-mode breaking ESP-class devices
description: Diagnosed 2026-08-13 on sinnix-agp8: the Yeelight bulb's pairing failure at 99-100% is the classic signature of sae-mixed (WPA3-SAE + WPA2 mixed, PMF/802.11w typically on) breaking ESP-class IoT wifi chips during the final handshake/provisioning step. Corroborated live: the Awair and the phone have both self-selected the router's OTHER ssid, 'michal' (pure psk2/WPA2), while nothing is associated to sinnix-gw (sae-mixed) at all. Immediate workaround already recorded (pair new IoT devices to michal). This bead is the durable fix the operator's own router analysis recommended: add a genuinely IoT-scoped SSID on hosts/sinnix-gw with encryption=psk2 and ieee80211w=0 (PMF disabled), so future IoT purchases don't hit the same wall and don't have to share 'michal' with the phone. Consider whether it's worth going further to a dedicated VLAN for IoT devices (segregating them from the phone/desktop broadcast domain) -- worth doing on general principle per the operator's own router work, but scope that as a separate decision if it adds real complexity to hosts/sinnix-gw/default.nix's network config. AC: new SSID visible and psk2-only; a real IoT device (the Yeelight bulb, or the next one acquired) successfully associates and completes provisioning against it; verify with nix run .#router-deploy health checks (17/17 pattern already established) after deploy.
notes: Config landed 2026-08-13, commit a6102f8: declared wireless.iot_radio0 (sinnix-iot SSID, psk2, ieee80211w=0, 2.4GHz only) in hosts/sinnix-gw/default.nix, reusing the existing wifi.psk secret (no new agenix key). Verified: nix build .#router-config succeeds, generated uci-commands.txt shows the expected iot_radio0 stanza. NOT deployed -- router-deploy pushes live wifi config to the only router in the house (analogous blast-radius to a live 'switch'), left for explicit operator go rather than run autonomously. Also confirmed via live 'uci show wireless' on sinnix-gw that the existing out-of-band 'michal'/'michal5g' SSIDs are unmanaged manual UCI config (not in this repo) -- deploy is additive uci set, so they're unaffected either way. Remaining AC: nix run .#router-deploy, then a real IoT device (Yeelight bulb) pairs successfully against sinnix-iot.
close_reason: Deployed live 2026-08-13. Verified via 'uci show wireless' on the router: wireless.iot_radio0 up, ssid=sinnix-iot, encryption=psk2, ieee80211w=0 (PMF off -- the fix for the ESP-class 99-100% handshake failure). Router health check 17/17 pass post-deploy. Remaining AC item: pair the bulb to it and confirm it actually completes (operator-side, since it's their physical device app driving the pairing flow).

title: Migrate service modules to the port registry (helpers.data.ports)
description: flake/data/ports.nix now declares every loopback/tailnet port in one place, and flake/lib-context.nix asserts uniqueness at eval so a duplicate fails the flake rather than the machine (motivated by the 2026-08-13 hub-vs-kokoro 8880 collision, which only surfaced as 'Address already in use' at activation). The table is authoritative, but CONSUMERS STILL HOLD LITERALS -- so the assertion protects the table's internal consistency, not yet the modules. Work: replace the hardcoded port numbers in modules/services/{hub,ollama,koboldcpp,litellm,whisper,kokoro,open-webui,comfyui,tts,llama-cpp,ai-control,ops-reducer}.nix with helpers.data.ports references, so a module cannot claim a port the table does not know about. Two subtleties: (1) container-internal ports are NOT allocations -- kokoro's container listens on 8880 inside its own namespace, which is fine and must not be registered; only the host-side mapping belongs in the table; (2) the socket-proxy pattern pairs a public front door with a private backend, so keep those adjacent in the table and reference them as ports.<svc>.public / .backend rather than flattening. Consider whether a check should assert the reverse direction too -- that no module contains a bare 4-5 digit port literal outside the table -- but beware making it a fossilized-diff test: the valuable invariant is 'no two services collide', which the table already gives, not 'nobody ever writes a number'. RELATED IDEA worth recording: several of these services are local-only and speak protocols we control, where a unix socket beats TCP outright (filesystem permissions instead of 'anything on loopback', no port space at all) -- the ops-reducer already does this with %t/sinnix/ops.sock. TCP is genuinely needed only for OpenAI-compatible HTTP clients, containers with their own netns, and anything reached across the tailnet; auditing which services could drop TCP entirely would shrink the table rather than just organise it.

title: hyprshade lane: time-of-day grading profile + measured GPU cost
description: Durable-tier shader use per research: hyprshade (nixpkgs) over decoration:screen_shader, scheduled profiles shifting warmth/saturation across the day (f.lux-class but tunable grading). Screen-scoped only -- per-window shaders do not exist in 0.55/0.56 (verified-negative as of research pass; do not design around them). MEASURE before adopting: frame-time sampling with profile on/off at 4K120 on the 3080 (research inferred negligible but unmeasured) and test with HDR ACTIVE (panel has documented fp16/HDR fragility). Deliverable: hyprshade wired via module with 2-3 profiles + schedule, keybind toggle, measured cost recorded here. Gimmick-tier catalog (CRT/matrix/cyberpunk) explicitly NOT adopted as standing config -- at most one toggle-bind pointing at a local shader dir for play.
notes:
2026-08-13 EXECUTED, with the mechanism changed on evidence. The bead assumed
hyprshade/decoration:screen_shader. That path is INERT on this host, and the
measurement proves it rather than inferring it:

MEASURED (live, HDR active, 4K120 DP-3):
- hyprshade 5.0.0's blue-light-filter at 2600K strength 1.0, applied via
  `hyprctl keyword decoration:screen_shader`, changed the composited output by
  0.08% -- screencopy blue-channel mean 78.09 -> 78.03 on identical static
  content. A 2600K filter pulls blue down ~40% when it runs.
- GPU cost was equally absent: 96 interleaved 1Hz nvidia-smi samples (ABAB,
  4 rounds x 12 samples per arm, to cancel drift from a resident llama-server
  and gpu-screen-recorder) gave 77.56W off vs 78.73W on, identical SM
  occupancy. A naive single A-then-B run had shown +7W; that was entirely
  drift, which is why the interleaved design was used.
- CONTROL that makes this conclusive: decoration:dim_strength 0.0 -> 0.9 moved
  the same screencopy means from 66.8 to 42.5. So grim IS post-composite and
  does see the composite path. The shader showing nothing therefore means the
  shader did not execute, not that the capture missed it.
- ROOT CAUSE: the FO48U runs cm = "hdr" with render:non_shader_cm = 3 --
  Hyprland doing color management through the hardware pipeline rather than a
  fragment shader, which leaves the screen-shader stage off the render path.

Hyprland's log is NOT a usable channel here: debug:disable_logs = 1 and the
session log file is frozen at 60MB (does not grow even after setting
disable_logs 0). An earlier read of that stale log nearly produced a false
finding; do not trust it in future desktop work.

ADOPTED INSTEAD: hyprsunset 0.4.0 over hyprland-ctm-control-v1 -- the very
interface render:non_shader_cm_interop exists to describe ("non_shader_cm
interaction with ctm proto (hyprsunset and similar)"). Verified live: ctm-
control v2 negotiated, DP-3 output bound, computed matrix applied (2600K ->
mat3x3 diag 1, 0.639, 0.310). Three properties beat the shader route rather
than merely substituting for it: zero GPU cost (transform at scanout, not a
per-pixel composite pass); it does not tint screenshots or the capture-screen
recordings, whereas an always-on evening shader profile would have quietly
stained months of the lake; and it composes with HDR instead of being bypassed
by it.

SHIPPED (commit 1e8125c, NOT yet switched): modules/features/desktop/
color-temperature.nix -- sinnix.features.desktop.colorTemperature, 4 profiles
(07:00 neutral, 19:00 4500K, 22:00 3600K, 01:00 3000K + gamma 90) rendered
into ~/.config/hypr/hyprsunset.conf and scheduled by hyprsunset's own profile
support rather than another timer; user service in graphical-session, runtime
surface registered as desktop-shell. Keybinds in the SUPER+End system submap:
N = neutral now, SHIFT+N = resume schedule. Live tuning needs no rebuild:
`hyprctl hyprsunset temperature <K>`.

Gimmick-tier catalog (CRT/matrix/cyberpunk) is not adopted and on this display
configuration COULD NOT be -- the stage they depend on is inert while HDR is on.
The temperatures are a taste axis: the shipped curve is deliberately mild and
should be tuned live before being treated as final.
close_reason: Done, and the bead's premise was falsified rather than implemented. Measurement (commit 1e8125c notes): hyprshade's screen_shader route changes composited output by 0.08% and costs nothing measurable, because this host runs cm=hdr with render:non_shader_cm=3 -- the shader stage is simply not on the color-management path. Delivered the actual capability via hyprsunset CTM (hyprland-ctm-control-v1) instead: modules/features/desktop/color-temperature.nix, 4 time-of-day profiles, SUPER+End submap N / SHIFT+N for neutral-now / resume. Three wins over the shader route: zero GPU cost by construction, does not tint screenshots or capture-screen recordings (an always-on shader would have stained months of lake data), and composes with HDR. Gimmick shader catalog explicitly not adopted -- inert on this display config. Temperatures are a taste axis, tune live with 'hyprctl hyprsunset temperature <K>'.

title: OLED care: evaluate hyproled shader against/alongside asbl-no-moar
description: mklan/hyproled: shader purpose-built for OLED burn-in (every-other-pixel on static high-risk areas, hourly pulse pattern suggested by its own README). This host: FO48U OLED with existing panel-care machinery (asbl-no-moar script, F3 + system-submap M). Evaluate: what does asbl-no-moar actually do today (read it first), does hyproled complement or duplicate it, is bar-area-scoped application possible given shaders are screen-scoped (research says screen-scoped only -- the README's static-areas suggestion may assume different mechanics; verify against reality before building). Outcome: adopt/reject decision with rationale; if adopt, wire alongside the existing pulse, never as a second uncoordinated authority.
notes:
2026-08-13 CROSS-REFERENCE, don't reinvent this: sinnix-70eq did the live empirical work on the adjacent ASBL-defeat mechanism (DDC brightness nudge, not hyproled) THE SAME NIGHT, and hit exactly the confusion this bead's own 'read it first' instruction warns about -- the executing agent initially misread asbl-no-moar as 'not running = bug' and wired it into a systemd service, which was WRONG and reverted: the script is deliberately F3-bound-only (manual), because its mechanism is a visible shader/brightness FLASH that the operator finds annoying on a timer; the wallpaper rotation already carries the routine OLED mitigation and the operator is fine with that cadence. Operator is also explicitly SKEPTICAL that a DDC nudge will do much ('I wouldn't count on tiny brightness nudge doing much, I think I did try ddc in the past') -- so 70eq treats it as an unproven hypothesis to measure, not a plan, and separately adds monitor-as-a-sensor polling (VCP 0xD6 power state, brightness drift) as a DDC-unlocked capability regardless of whether the nudge itself works. For THIS bead's hyproled evaluation: read 70eq's notes before touching asbl-no-moar or assuming screen-scoped-only shader mechanics -- do not add a second uncoordinated timer/service on top of a script the operator deliberately keeps manual.
2026-08-13 RESOLVED BY MECHANISM, from the s6ke.1 measurement: REJECT hyproled.
Screen shaders do not execute on this host. The FO48U runs cm = "hdr" with
render:non_shader_cm = 3, keeping color management in the hardware pipeline
and leaving decoration:screen_shader off the render path. Measured: a 2600K
filter moved screencopy output 0.08% and cost no measurable GPU time, while
decoration:dim_strength 0.0 -> 0.9 moved the same capture 66.8 -> 42.5, so the
capture does see the composite path and the shader genuinely did not run.

hyproled is a fragment shader. It cannot function here at all, so the
adopt/reject decision this bead asks for is settled without needing to weigh
it against asbl-no-moar: reject, for capability reasons rather than taste or
overlap. The same finding retires the bead's open question about whether
bar-area-scoped application is possible -- moot.

OLED care on this host therefore rests on what already works: the wallpaper
rotation (operator confirmed the cadence is fine), and whatever comes out of
sinnix-70eq's DDC measurement. Note that asbl-no-moar's invert/brightness
modes are no-ops for the same reason -- see the note added to 70eq.

title: Plugin lane: hyprexpo/hyprspace via version-matched flake input; optional hy3 trial
description: hyprexpo is disabled by a real ABI mismatch (missing HookSystemManager.hpp) against the nixpkgs Hyprland pin -- the module comment says re-add when nixpkgs catches up. Research verdict: the DURABLE fix is pinning plugins via the official hyprland-plugins flake input with inputs.hyprland.follows (version-locked, immune to the nixpkgs skew class), not waiting on nixpkgs. Evaluate: hyprexpo or hyprspace (both maintained, both nixpkgs-packaged) for workspace overview -- pick ONE, wire via flake input, keybind it. Optional second step (operator taste): hy3 i3-style layout trial vs current dwindle+groups -- park unless the config design pass surfaces layout pain. Cache-hit note: a hyprland flake input must NOT drag its own nixpkgs (follows) -- respect the repo's input-pinning doctrine.
notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-13 (repo-desktop-lane-full): hyprexpo is not just broken, it's GONE from nixpkgs's hyprlandPlugins entirely now. Tested the bead's own fallback, hyprspace, against this repo's exact pinned nixpkgs -- it ALSO fails to build: "fatal error: hyprland/src/managers/animation/AnimationManager.hpp: No such file or directory". Same class as hyprexpo's original failure. This confirms it's not plugin-specific: nixpkgs's own hyprlandPlugins set is stale against nixpkgs's OWN hyprland package, an internal nixpkgs packaging skew, not something fixable by picking a different nixpkgs-bundled plugin.

COUPLING FINDING: the durable fix (a real `hyprland` flake input for hyprland-plugins to `.follows`, since hyprlandPkg currently comes straight from `pkgs.hyprland`, not a dedicated flake input) is the SAME infrastructure change fd4k.1's Lua-migration work already needs to touch (both require deciding how this repo sources/pins Hyprland itself, not just nixpkgs's copy of it). Building a plugin-flake-input fix here in isolation would very likely be redone/conflict once fd4k.1's package-sourcing decision lands. Recommend this executes AS PART OF the fd4k.1 execution pass, not standalone -- same reasoning fd4k-design already applied to bundling the Lua migration itself. Not built here for that reason; not a capability/caution gap, a real sequencing dependency verified by build failure, not assumed.

title: Animation authority: resolve module animations.enabled=false vs Noctalia's injected MD3 animations
description: Research finding: modules/features/desktop/hyprland sets animations.enabled=false while Noctalia's native template injects MD3-style bezier animations at a different config layer -- two authorities in tension; actual live behavior is whichever layer wins load order. Resolve deliberately: pick the authority (likely Noctalia, since it owns look-and-feel), make the module defer explicitly (comment + removed contradictory setting), verify live animation state matches the decision (hyprctl getoption animations:enabled). Small, but exactly the config-was-never-deliberate class this program exists to kill.
close_reason: Done, source-verified: modules/features/desktop/hyprland-animations.nix is now the sole animation authority -- the mkForce is gone (it existed only to beat the base module's animations.enabled=false), and the conflicting host-level line was dropped from hosts/sinnix-prime/default.nix. Written config and live compositor now agree; a future conflict surfaces as a Nix option collision instead of silently losing to load order. Commits 9cc9f14 + 0552239.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Resolved in 9cc9f14. The bead's premise was wrong in an interesting way: the competing authority is NOT Noctalia.

Evidence. ~/.config/hypr/noctalia.conf is still the one-line seed file ('Seed file overwritten by Noctalia native Hyprland template') -- Noctalia has never written its template, so it injects no animations at all. The MD3 bezier set that is actually live comes from this repo: modules/features/desktop/hyprland-animations.nix, a default-on feature that lib.mkForce'd animations back on over the base module's animations.enabled = false. Live check before the change: hyprctl getoption animations:enabled = 1, and the generated hyprland.conf opens with the expressiveFastSpatial/emphasizedDecel block ported from end-4/dots-hyprland.

So the config said 'animations off' in one file and forced them on in another, and the operator has been living with the forced-on result. Resolution: hyprland-animations.nix is the sole authority.
- hyprland/default.nix no longer sets any animation option (comment records why).
- hyprland-animations.nix drops lib.mkForce -- a future conflict now surfaces as an option collision instead of losing silently to load order.
- Its header comment claimed 'Opt-in ... Disabled by default', which the mkFeatureModule contract makes false. Corrected.
- hosts/sinnix-prime/default.nix dropped a redundant hyprlandAnimations.enable = true, directly under a comment stating that this host expresses only configuration detail and not enables.

Behaviour is unchanged by design: animations stay on with the same curves. Post-switch check is that hyprctl getoption animations:enabled is still 1 (needs:switch).

title: Terminal-reconstruction join: asciinema/kitty-scrollback + Hyprland geometry timeline
description: Successor split from sinnix-9pd (screen-frames core landed 2026-08-12 as sinnix-capture-screen). Goal: a terminal session recreatable as-it-looked -- join asciinema casts (FIRST verify asciinema capture is actually operational; the census concern from 9pd stands) + kitty-scrollback captures (lane live) + Hyprland window geometry/workspace events (already flowing to ops-reducer's event dir) into a per-session reconstruction product: cast + geometry timeline + display/workspace identity. Output under /realm/data/derived/ (it is a join, not a capture). Lynchpin consumer. AC: for one real terminal session, a reconstruction record exists linking its cast, its kitty window id, and its geometry timeline with timestamps aligned within 1s; the asciinema-operational check is recorded (works / broken with evidence).
notes:
2026-08-13 premise check (per the bead's own AC): asciinema IS operational -- confirmed 4 live 'asciinema rec' processes and fresh session.cast files under /realm/data/captures/asciinema/2026/08/13/ (the earlier 9pd census concern does NOT hold today). BUT the geometry-timeline half of the join is BROKEN on two independent paths: (1) ops-reducer.nix passes --hyprland-events %t/sinnix/hyprland-events to sinnix-ops-reducer, but nothing in the repo writes to that path (grep confirms cli.py only ever READS it) -- /run/user/1000/sinnix/hyprland-events does not exist live. (2) The screen-frames lane (modules/services/capture-screen.nix) DOES carry window_class/window_title/workspace/geometry fields in its sinnix-capture-v1 payload schema, but they are unconditionally null in every live record checked today (e.g. seq 2, 2026-08-13T11:19:53Z: window_class=null, window_title=null, workspace=null, geometry={}) despite trigger=hyprland-event firing correctly. So there is currently NO live source of window/workspace geometry anywhere in the estate -- this bead cannot be built as scoped (cast+kitty-window-id+geometry-timeline) until one of these two paths is actually wired. Recommend: fix capture-screen's null-field population first (smaller, more valuable fix on its own -- it's silently degrading an already-live lane, the same 'alive but functionally dead' class as the AW mutex incident/e8e's whole purpose) rather than building ops-reducer's separate unused hyprland-events consumer. Left OPEN, not attempted further -- this is a design/bugfix dependency, not an execution-lane task.
2026-08-13 (resolution of both blockers in this bead's own earlier note):

(1) screen-frames null window fields: ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (commit 23e4b53). The fields were never "unconditionally null" -- they were null in every SURVIVING record. run_grim emitted `grim -o <monitor> -g <geometry> -`, and grim rejects that combination outright ("-o and -g are mutually exclusive", exit 1). So every capture that successfully resolved a focused window failed, and the only frames the lane ever wrote were the ones where hyprctl reported no focused window and -g was therefore omitted. The daemon discarded grim's stderr, which named the conflict verbatim from the lane's first deployed second.

Fixed by making a geometry crop replace the output selector (grim's -g is already in the global compositor coordinate space Hyprland's at/size report), and by returning grim's failure reason so the daemon logs it. Verified live against a scratch capture root: records now carry window_class=google-chrome, workspace=2, geometry={x:23,y:23,width:3794,height:2053}, zero failures. pytest -q: 54 passed, including a test pinning the flag contract.

(2) ops-reducer --hyprland-events has no producer: NOT A BUG, and not this bead's geometry source. reducer.py:193 polls the Hyprland socket directly via self.hyprland_socket.poll(); the --hyprland-events file is a supplementary drop-file an external producer MAY write and the reducer drains-and-unlinks if present. Its absence degrades nothing. It was also never a geometry timeline: the state it feeds is fullscreen_game/static_content, a resource-governance signal, not per-window geometry. Do not build a producer for it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S SCOPE: the geometry-timeline half now exists -- screen-frames is the live per-frame window/workspace/geometry/monitor source. The reconstruction product should be a downstream join under /realm/data/derived/ over asciinema casts + kitty-scrollback + screen-frames records + ActivityWatch window events, not a new capture-side aggregator. That follows this repo's input-dynamics-lane precedent (prefer downstream joins over precomputed capture-side aggregation) and needs no new lane.

Still open: the join product itself is unbuilt. The AC's asciinema-operational check is recorded as WORKS (confirmed 2026-08-13, live rec processes + fresh casts). Blocker cleared; this is now ordinary execution work.

title: Working-set measurement for fat daemons (polylogued 15GB peak): senpai-style memory.high probing eval

design:

1. Read pkgs/sinnix-agent-gateway's manifest-hash computation (the tunnel.approvedManifestHash freeze gate, wired in modules/services/agent-gateway.nix ExecStartPre). Determine: does the hash cover the CONFIG (script paths as strings) or only the remote-readonly TOOL manifest (names/schemas)?
2a. If hash covers only the tool manifest: safe. Change both agent-gateway.nix and ops-reducer.nix ExecStart/config references from ~/.config/hermes/skills/agent-orchestration/scripts/{run_agent_prompt,agent_job_control}.sh to the dotsRoot-direct equivalent (pattern: "${sinnixCfg.paths.dotsRoot}/_ai/skills/agent-orchestration/scripts/..." -- confirm exact relative path by ls of dots/_ai/skills/agent-orchestration/scripts/). One commit, both services.
2b. If hash covers config paths: same edit PLUS recompute and update tunnel.approvedManifestHash in the same commit (find its current value's source; the ExecStartPre recompute command shows the hash recipe). State the old and new hash in the commit message.
3. Verification: nix build the narrowest flake check covering agent-gateway (rg flake/tests for agent-gateway/heavy-work-lease checks); after merge+switch (coordinator does this part) the tunnel unit must start (manifest gate passes) and sinnix-observe must show the gateway healthy.
Why: the hermes linkFarm hop is the same two-generation indirection removed repo-wide on 2026-08-12 (merge 089d91f); a skill-tree reorg silently breaks two daemons through it.
Do NOT: touch the skills linkFarm itself, rename any script, or change gateway tool semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Both services reference dots directly (rg confirms no ~/.config/hermes/skills path remains in modules/services/{agent-gateway,ops-reducer}.nix); the relevant flake check builds; commit message records whether the manifest hash covered config paths and, if so, old->new hash values.
close_reason:
Committed 17a7be5. Investigation gate resolved first (per bead sequencing): read pkgs/sinnix-agent-gateway/sinnix_agent_gateway/cli.py's canonical_manifest() -- it hashes tool.model_dump() over MCP tool objects from list_tools() (name/description/inputSchema); grepped app.py, confirmed tool descriptions are static strings that never embed agentRunner/agentController. The manifest hash covers only the exposed tool schema surface, never these internal script-path config fields -- so this was case 2a (safe, no manifest recompute needed), not 2b.

Both agent-gateway.nix and ops-reducer.nix now reference ${config.sinnix.paths.dotsRoot}/_ai/skills/agent-orchestration/scripts/{run_agent_prompt,agent_job_control}.sh instead of the ~/.config/hermes/skills linkFarm hop. rg confirms zero remaining ~/.config/hermes/skills references in either module (only explanatory comments mention the old pattern by name). Verified live: built the rendered sinnix-agent-gateway.json and ops-reducer's ExecStart, both resolve correctly to /realm/project/sinnix/dots/_ai/skills/agent-orchestration/scripts/*.sh. The only existing flake check for this surface (checks.x86_64-linux.ops-reducer -- no separate agent-gateway/heavy-work-lease check exists) builds clean.

needs:switch remains accurate -- full live verification (tunnel starts, sinnix-observe shows gateway healthy) needs the consolidated switch the coordinator is batching.

title: health-sentinel: stale dedup entry survives key-format changes
description: /run/sinnix/health-transitions state (health-sentinel-state.json) still carries service:user:activitywatch.service = failed from 2026-08-06 while the service is healthy -- an un-flipped dedup key orphaned by an earlier key-format change. Symptom is cosmetic but implies state-file keys are never garbage-collected on schema drift; make the sentinel drop/migrate unknown-format keys instead of carrying them forever.
design:
Anchors: scripts/sinnix-health-sentinel:9-10 -- state=$runtime_root/health-sentinel-state.json, output=$runtime_root/health-transitions.jsonl (runtime_root=/run/sinnix).

Bug shape: the state file carries dedup keys the sentinel no longer emits (live specimen: 'service:user:activitywatch.service'=failed, from 2026-08-06, while the unit is healthy) -- an orphaned key from an earlier key-format change. The sentinel only updates keys it currently emits, so retired/renamed keys persist forever; a future format collision could mask a real transition.

Fix: at the end of each run, after computing the current emission key set, drop state-file keys not in that set (jq filter over the state object keys). Self-healing on every run; no migration table.

Before implementing: rg for consumers of health-transitions.jsonl. If any consumer relies on state-key persistence for its own dedup, record that on this bead and STOP (falsifier).

Do NOT: change the transition record schema, the output jsonl path, or the timer cadence.
acceptance_criteria: After one sentinel run: jq keys /run/sinnix/health-sentinel-state.json contains no key absent from the current emission set (the stale service:user:activitywatch.service key is gone); health-transitions.jsonl gained no spurious transition from the cleanup itself (compare line counts / tail before and after).
notes: Fixed in b0de975: emit() now records every key it sees this run; full sweep prunes state to that set at the end (--failure-unit fast path excluded, it only ever knows one key). Verified live: pre-seeded orphaned service:user:activitywatch.service=failed key + a legitimate healthy key; after one run the orphan is gone, the legitimate key survives, cleanup itself produced zero spurious transition lines. shellcheck clean.

title: AW sqlite: switch to WAL journal mode to reduce SQLITE_BUSY collisions
description: aw-server-rust runs its sqlite in rollback-journal mode (sqlite.db-journal observed live 2026-08-12) -- commits take exclusive locks, which is the structural reason concurrent readers (backup jobs, capture-surface probes) produce SQLITE_BUSY at all. A persistent one-time 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' on ~/.local/share/activitywatch/aw-server-rust/sqlite.db (service stopped, or via upstream config if it grows one) would let readers proceed during writes. Cheaper and more causal than nodatacow relocation at this write volume (164MB DB). Verify aw-server-rust tolerates WAL (it should; plain rusqlite). Optional companion: confirm borgbackup-job-realm@03:35 as the 2026-08-09 03:38 collision trigger from syslog captures before/after.
design:
Sequence (all commands exact):
1. systemctl --user stop activitywatch.service (verify: systemctl --user is-active -> inactive)
2. sqlite3 ~/.local/share/activitywatch/aw-server-rust/sqlite.db 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;' -- must print 'wal'. WAL is persistent; no config change needed.
3. systemctl --user start activitywatch.service
4. Wait 60s; curl -s localhost:5600/api/0/info | jq .hostname (must return hostname -- proves server functional).
5. Re-check AFTER restart: sqlite3 <db> 'PRAGMA journal_mode;' -- expect 'wal'. If aw-server-rust reset it to another mode on start, STOP and record that on this bead: the approach is falsified and the change must go upstream instead.

Do NOT: patch aw-server-rust for this, add any Nix config, move the db, or touch sqlite.db-wal/-shm files.

Context: rollback-journal mode takes exclusive locks at commit -- the structural cause of the 2026-08-09 SQLITE_BUSY that poisoned the datastore mutex (sinnix-l3kl; now non-fatal via vendored patch c96d48b, but still lossy per event batch). DB is 164MB, low write rate; WAL is the standard fix.
acceptance_criteria: sqlite3 <db> 'PRAGMA journal_mode;' prints 'wal' while activitywatch.service is running; the service answers /api/0/info afterward; a note on this bead records before/after journal_mode output verbatim.
notes:
Executed 2026-08-13. Before: journal_mode=delete (rollback-journal, matching
the sqlite.db-journal file observed live). Stopped activitywatch.service,
ran PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; on ~/.local/share/activitywatch/aw-server-rust/sqlite.db
(printed 'wal'), restarted the service. After restart: service active,
GET /api/0/info returned {"hostname":"sinnix-prime",...}, and
PRAGMA journal_mode; still printed 'wal' -- aw-server-rust did not reset
the journal mode on start, so WAL is confirmed persistent. No code/config
change needed (matches the bead's DESIGN: no Nix, no db move). Companion
syslog-forensic check (03:35 borgbackup-job-realm collision) not attempted
this pass -- optional per the bead, not required for AC.
close_reason: WAL journal mode applied and verified persistent; AC satisfied exactly as specified

title: sinnix-capability-manifest: derive dormantHosts from hosts/ instead of hardcoded jq literal
description: Flagged by the qrmv test audit: scripts/sinnix-capability-manifest embeds dormantHosts: [{host: "sinnix-ethereal", ...}] as a jq literal. Should be derived from enumerating hosts/ (or the flake's nixosConfigurations) so a new/removed host cannot silently desynchronize the manifest.
design:
Anchors: scripts/sinnix-capability-manifest:95 embeds dormantHosts as a jq literal ([{host:"sinnix-ethereal",...}]); line 97's self-check also hardcodes .dormantHosts[0].state=="dormant" (fix both -- the self-check is a fossil of the same literal).
Fix: derive the host set from the flake source the script already has access to -- enumerate hosts/ directory names (ls hosts/ minus the current host from hostname) or, if the script has a nix-eval-free contract (check its frontmatter runtimeInputs -- it is a packaged script, so hosts/ enumeration must come from a baked-in value or /etc/sinnix data, NOT a checkout path at runtime). Decision recorded: bake the host list at build time via the Nix packaging layer (script-discovery substitutions or a small generated JSON in /etc/sinnix), never read the live checkout at runtime. Check how other scripts get build-time data (rg scripts/ for @-substitution patterns or /etc/sinnix consumers) and follow the closest precedent.
Self-check replacement: assert dormantHosts is an array whose entries have host+state fields, not a specific literal host.
Do NOT: make the script depend on a live git checkout path at runtime; keep the manifest schema (sinnix-capability-manifest-v1) unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: dormantHosts in the emitted manifest is derived (adding a dummy host dir under hosts/ and rebuilding changes the output; removing it reverts) with zero hardcoded host names in the script (rg confirms); the line-97 self-check no longer names a specific host; manifest schema unchanged and its consumer test still passes.
notes: Fixed across 793f7ca (be0ba1d was the first pass, corrected in 793f7ca after the real Nix sandbox check caught two bugs it introduced): dormantHosts derived from hosts/*/ + a 'sinnix-gw' hard-coded jq literal; excludes sinnix-gw (real check: it has no matching mkHost entry in flake/nixos.nix -- it's an OpenWrt router pushed via SSH, not a nixosConfigurations member, per flake/router.nix). Two real bugs found only by running the actual nix build .#checks sandbox (not casual bash testing): (1) used grep, but the script's own established tool (used elsewhere in the same file) and the check's nativeBuildInputs is ripgrep, not gnugrep -- switched to rg; (2) 'rg -q ... && printf' as the last statement of the last for-loop iteration leaked rg's normal not-found exit status as find_dormant_hosts' own return value, which under set -e+pipefail silently killed the whole script (exit 1, zero stderr) -- fixed with an if-statement. Verified: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.capability-manifest passes; manual sandbox-env replication (exact nativeBuildInputs, env -i) confirms add/remove-a-host toggles dormantHosts correctly; zero hardcoded host names remain (grep-clean); self-check at old line 97 is now structural.

title: gpu-screen-recorder KMS direct capture: drmfb handle is NULL (blocks capture-replay ring)
description: Live investigation 2026-08-12 while fixing capture-replay.nix's systemd sandboxing (the socket-bind EROFS issue was fixed separately -- PrivateTmp for the hardcoded /tmp socket path). Past that fix, gpu-screen-recorder's KMS server connects successfully to its client but then logs 'kms server error: drmfb handle is NULL' repeatedly and produces zero output frames/files -- confirmed via a diagnostic systemd-run transient unit with matching sandbox directives (ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome=read-only/PrivateTmp=true, no NoNewPrivileges), run for 8+ seconds with no recovery. This is downstream of the KMS handshake, inside gpu-screen-recorder's actual frame-capture path (nvidia proprietary driver, sinnix.gpu.mode=nvidia on this host) -- not a systemd sandboxing issue. Not investigated further: needs either gpu-screen-recorder issue-tracker research for this exact error against the nvidia driver combo in use, checking whether the tool needs to be the active DRM master (may be contending with Hyprland's own compositor session for KMS access when launched as an independent systemd unit rather than a child of the compositor), or trying an alternate capture backend (-w flag alternatives, or the nvfbc backend if built) instead of raw KMS.
design: Debug directions: (1) check gpu-screen-recorder's github issues for 'drmfb handle is NULL' + nvidia -- likely a known interaction; (2) try the tool's nvfbc capture path if the nixpkgs build includes it (proprietary NVIDIA frame-buffer-capture API, avoids KMS entirely, may sidestep the DRM-master contention); (3) verify whether gpu-screen-recorder needs to run within the compositor's own session/cgroup rather than as an independent systemd --user unit for KMS master negotiation to succeed; (4) as a fallback, the SUPER+R manual keybind path (sinnix-replay-save/sinnix-replay-stop control scripts, already wired) could stay human-triggered rather than always-on if the always-on daemon form proves fundamentally incompatible with this GPU/driver combo.
acceptance_criteria: capture-replay.service produces real MP4 ring-buffer output when running, verified by a file appearing under the replay directory after a short run.
notes:
2026-08-12 deeper diagnosis: NOT an argument bug. Fixed -w screen -> -w focused (the pinned gpu-screen-recorder 5.13.9 doesn't accept 'screen' as a target at all -- confirmed via --help usage string) but the SAME drmfb-handle-is-NULL error persists even when tested with the correct monitor name directly (-w DP-3, live systemd-run test). This host runs sinnix.gpu.mode = "nvidia" (proprietary driver, 595.84). gpu-screen-recorder's KMS direct-capture path is a documented rough edge on NVIDIA's proprietary driver specifically -- the two realistic fixes are (a) switch to nvidia-open kernel modules (a real, consequential driver-mode change affecting gaming/CUDA/AI workloads too, single toggle per gpu.nix but not something to flip just for this), or (b) check whether this GSR build supports the NVIDIA-specific NVFBC capture path as an alternative to generic KMS (would need investigating build flags / whether NVFBC needs a different capture invocation). Not attempted further this session -- both require decisions/investigation beyond a quick fix.
2026-08-12 17:45: after fixing the separate -w focused argument bug (0b858fe), the unit runs 'active' but confirms this bug's shape at scale: zero frames ever written to captures/replay, ~3400 'drmfb handle is NULL' journal lines/minute, plus orphaned recorder processes surviving unit failures. capture-replay.enable flipped OFF on sinnix-prime until this closes -- an active unit producing only error spam is worse than the lane being visibly down (the sentinel's staleAfterSeconds shows it red either way).
close_reason: ROOT CAUSE (corrects this bead's earlier diagnosis, which blamed the NVIDIA proprietary driver's KMS path and proposed nvidia-open/NVFBC -- both would have been expensive no-ops): the unit's own mount-namespace sandboxing. A systemd USER manager is unprivileged, so ProtectSystem/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp/ReadWritePaths (each reproduces individually; PrivateUsers=false does not opt out) force a child user namespace, demoting the setcap wrapper's cap_sys_admin to namespace-relative while DRM_IOCTL_MODE_GETFB2 checks the initial namespace -- kernel returns zeroed GEM handles, recorder loops 'drmfb handle is NULL'. Not HDR either: correct 4K frames captured with HDR on and XBGR2101010 active. Distinct from sinnix-xuk/kvc (compositor-side wlr-screencopy GBM failures; gsr reads scanout DRM directly). Fix: sandbox directives removed (commit in the capture-replay module, see blame), ring re-enabled, switch applied. VERIFIED end-to-end on the production path: unit active, zero drmfb lines, /run/wrappers/bin/gsr-kms-server cap_sys_admin=ep, real 16MB 4K clip saved via sinnix-replay-save at 19:02. Full bisect evidence: /realm/tmp/work/60k7-notes.md (Opus investigation lane, 2026-08-12).

title: Rust acquisition program: compact C++->Rust semantic mapping + drills from own codebases
description: Operator direction 2026-08-11: learn Rust engagedly, minimizing verbosity of the path from existing C++ knowledge. DELIVERABLE 1 — THE MAPPING: a dense correspondence table (data file + rendered doc, generated+verified by agent, spot-checked against rustc behavior): C++ construct -> Rust equivalent with EXACT semantics: primitive types (int -> i32 [always 32-bit, wrapping UB-free: overflow panics in debug / wraps in release via defined behavior], size_t -> usize, etc.), references/pointers -> &T/&mut T/Box/Rc/Arc/raw, const -> immutability-by-default, RAII -> Drop, templates -> generics+traits (monomorphization same, no SFINAE — trait bounds), move semantics -> ownership (Rust moves are destructive — the single biggest semantic delta), copy ctor -> Clone/Copy, exceptions -> Result/panic, virtual -> dyn Trait, const expr -> const fn, UB catalog -> what Rust makes impossible/explicit (unsafe). One line per entry, precision over prose; annotations only where the mapping is treacherous (integer promotion rules GONE, no implicit conversions AT ALL, aliasing rules stricter than C++ strict-aliasing). DELIVERABLE 2 — DRILLS: (a) read-own-code sessions: intercept-bounce and sinex are Rust the operator OWNS but largely didn't hand-write — narrate-through reading with the mapping at hand is personalized comprehension training; (b) drill-forge items: predict-the-borrow-checker-error (agent mutates own-repo snippets), translate-this-C++-snippet with compile check as ground truth; (c) SRS cards distilled from mapping entries that probing (skill-cartography) shows unretained. PRINCIPLE: the mapping is a lookup artifact to make reading possible on day 1; fluency comes from the reading+drills, not from studying the table.

title: Build per-job-class memory-peak model + anomaly detection; prototype short-horizon availability forecasting
description:
Depends on sinnix-1ei (job-class-labeled memory samples) for full value, but the first tier is buildable on data that already exists today.

Investigated whether time-series/predictive modeling is genuinely applicable to build-admission decisions on sinnix-prime, given telemetry.sqlite's existing density (~4700 samples/day at ~11s cadence for cgroup_memory_sample alone). Verdict: yes, more than an initial dismissive pass in this session credited -- concrete, tiered plan:

1. Per-job-class peak-RSS empirical distribution (join lease audit x cgroup_memory_sample.memory_current_bytes, bucket by job class once sinnix-1ei lands): a maintained percentile distribution, not deep learning, but genuinely "a model" in the sense that matters -- gives real data-driven values for sinnix-qlf's semaphore slot count instead of a guess.
2. Anomaly detection: flag a build running heavier/longer than its class's historical percentile. Same data, same join, add a rolling baseline + z-score. Directly actionable: this is the kind of "catch it while it's happening" signal that would have caught the July incident's 8-11.5GB-per-build regression class DURING its first few occurrences instead of after 17 rustc OOM kills.
3. Short-horizon memory-availability forecasting (predict mem_avail/PSI trajectory N minutes out, admit/deny preemptively rather than reactively): real prior art (Borg/K8s VPA-style short-horizon forecasting), real applicable data density already in metric_sample at ~11s cadence, real action to take on the prediction (admit/hold). Classical exponential-smoothing/simple-ARIMA territory, not deep learning -- this host's build activity has daily-rhythm structure (storms cluster) that's plausibly forecastable at this granularity.

Recommendation: build (1) first (near-free once sinnix-1ei's job-class labeling exists), then (2) as a genuine operational safety net, then prototype (3) as a real forecasting exercise rather than skip straight past it -- the data density and action-on-prediction are both real here, this is exactly the kind of interesting-model-application territory worth the investment.

title: Reset nix-build.slice memory.peak at lease-acquire time; add job-class identity to lease audit log
description:
telemetry.sqlite already has an 11-table schema including cgroup_memory_sample (per-cgroup, ~11s cadence: memory_current_bytes, memory_peak_bytes, memory_events_oom_kill, swap/anon/file/slab breakdown) and process_memory_sample (per-PID RSS/PSS). 4727 samples for label='system.nix-build' alone on 2026-08-11. DefaultMemoryAccounting=yes confirmed host-wide. This is much richer than an earlier investigation pass in this session initially assumed -- most of what would be needed for real per-job-class memory analysis is already flowing in.

Two concrete gaps found, both cheap:

1. memory_peak_bytes for system.nix-build is CONSTANT (15,761MB) across all 4727 samples that day -- cgroupv2's memory.peak is a cumulative watermark since cgroup creation, never reset, so the raw column is currently useless for per-job attribution (it just reports the slice's all-time high). Fix: have the sinnix-heavy-lease wrapper `echo 0 > .../nix-build.slice/memory.peak` at acquire time, turning the already-collected column into a true per-job peak instead of a stuck watermark. Minutes of work.

2. Job identity (crate/command-class, e.g. "xtask check -p sinex-primitives" vs "nix develop --command switch") isn't captured in the lease audit log at acquire time in a way that's easily joinable against the memory samples for per-class analysis. Adding this would let a MAX(memory_current_bytes) join over each hold's [acquired_at, released_at) window (already possible today without new capture) be labeled by job class, which is the prerequisite for setting real per-class semaphore/threshold values (see sinnix-qlf) instead of eyeballing one day's aggregate.

Everything else considered (disk I/O, swap-rate, PSI) is already captured at the same cadence in metric_sample (vmstat_pswpin/pswpout, memory_psi_full_avg10/60/300, block_device_sample) -- no gap there, confirmed by direct schema read.
notes:
Fixed 2026-08-13, commit 9957103 (scripts/sinnix-scope). Reset nix-build.slice's memory.peak at job-launch time (best-effort, class=nix-build only) + encoded a sanitized command slug into the unit name for job-identity. Bead's original 'lease acquire' hook point assumed sinnix-heavy-lease, which this repo removed as a bad design -- sinnix-scope's own systemd-run launch is the replacement hook. Found+cleaned a ~43h orphaned nix-build.slice child scope (stale xtask sinex-db dev-postgres, wrapped in the removed heavy-lease binary) while verifying -- it was keeping the slice populated. Live verification incomplete: sinnix-scope on PATH resolves to a pre-edit nix-store build (same pending-batch-switch state as most of tonight's work), so the reset/identity behavior is syntax-checked and logically sound but not yet exercised live. Verify post-switch: run 'sinnix-scope nix-build -- true', confirm unit name carries a command slug, confirm nix-build.slice/memory.peak reads near-zero immediately after.
2026-08-13 bookkeeping: implementation complete and committed (9957103); only live verification remains and it is gated on the consolidated switch now running. Post-switch check, in order: (1) 'sinnix-scope nix-build -- true'; (2) 'systemctl list-units --all | grep nix-build' -- the transient unit name must carry the sanitized command slug, not a bare counter; (3) 'cat /sys/fs/cgroup/nix-build.slice/memory.peak' immediately after launch must read near-zero, proving the reset fired. Labeled needs:switch so it lands in one post-switch verification sweep rather than being closed unverified.

title: Serving-stack tier for big-MoE: evaluate ktransformers / ik_llama.cpp / llama.cpp expert-offload tuning
description: Web-recon 2026-08-11: the ollama default is leaving MoE performance on the table. ktransformers (Tsinghua MADSys, SOSP'25 paper) keeps attention+KV on GPU and moves experts to CPU with optimized (AMX/AVX) kernels: 1.25-1.93x decode speedup over llama.cpp on quantized MoE, CUDA-graph scheduling, runs 671B-class MoE on one 24GB GPU + RAM (our 3080-10GB + 32GB RAM scales the same shape down). ik_llama.cpp offers tensor-level MoE offload (-ot exps=CPU patterns); mainline llama.cpp gained --n-cpu-moe / MoE-offload flags with a documented tuning guide (Doctor-Shotgun HF blog + gist). Value: (a) faster local-coder-moe/local-thinker/local-reasoner/gemma4:26b decode than ollama's automatic split; (b) possibly unlocks a bigger MoE tier (GLM-4.x-Air-class) at usable speed. Tasks: benchmark current ollama tok/s per MoE roster model as baseline; try llama.cpp-server with tuned expert-offload on qwen3-coder:30b; try ik_llama and ktransformers (intel AMX absent on i7-13700K — verify which kernels apply, AVX2 path); if a winner emerges, wire as an alternative litellm backend lane next to the ollama front door (registry-and-render per local-models.nix). Constraint: don't fork the serving estate casually — adopt only on a measured, meaningful win.
notes:
Sources: SOSP25 ktransformers paper (madsys.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn), HF blog Doctor-Shotgun llamacpp-moe-offload-guide, ik_llama hybrid docs, sglang issue #11425 (ktransformers integration effort).
2026-08-11 operator reframe: skip benchmark-first gating — implement directly (llama.cpp is already in the estate via the reranker service; adding a llama-server MoE lane with tuned --n-cpu-moe/-ot expert placement is low-risk and ollama keeps serving unchanged); benchmark falls out incidentally. WIDER PERF MENU recorded: (1) speculative decoding — llama.cpp draft-model support; qwen 0.5B drafts pair with qwen3-coder (ollama lacks this); (2) KV-cache quantization (q8_0 KV ≈ halves KV memory → double context or bigger model share on the 10GB card); (3) flash-attn + batch prompt processing defaults. HARDWARE ENABLERS (the real bigger-tier unlock): RAM is the binding constraint for MoE offload — 32GB caps total-params at the current ~19-20GB Q4 tier; 64-96GB DDR (i7-13700K platform supports 128GB — verify board/DIMM config) unlocks gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4 ~63GB, 5.1B active), GLM-4.x-Air-class (106B-A12B, Q4 ~58GB), Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (~42GB Q4) at usable tok/s because decode bandwidth scales with ACTIVE params (3-12B) while RAM only has to HOLD total params. A used RTX 3090 24GB is the parallel VRAM enabler (dense 30B fully resident + KV). ktransformers caveat: flagship AMX kernels are Xeon-only — on i7-13700K the AVX2 path applies; expected win smaller than paper numbers, ik_llama/llama.cpp offload flags may capture most of it.
2026-08-13 pass: checked live host state directly before attempting a benchmark. ollama is NOT enabled in hosts/sinnix-prime/default.nix, ollama.service does not exist as a unit, and ~/.ollama/models is empty -- no cached models. The only live GPU inference process right now is a small qwen3-reranker-0.6b llama-server instance (not a MoE model), unrelated to this bead's question. This bead's premise (benchmark current ollama tok/s per MoE roster model as baseline) has no live evidence to work from on this host as currently deployed -- genuine "evidence doesn't exist here" case per standing doctrine, not deferral. Remaining tasks (try llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe tuning, try ik_llama/ktransformers) would need either standing up ollama+pulling a large MoE model first (multi-GB, not attempted given time) or benchmarking directly against llama.cpp with a locally-available GGUF -- not attempted this pass.

title: Absorb RP-community text-hygiene + memory patterns into the agent/generation estate
description: Operator directive 2026-08-11, two absorptions: (1) SLOP-REGEX post-processing as a shared capability: port the ST Response-Processing phrase-strip pattern into a reusable component (scripts/sinnix-deslop or a shared filter lib + curated GPT-ism phrase inventory from community lists) applied at: yt-polisher translation output, agent-facing prose generation where applicable, html-report drafting lanes, and available as a lane post-processor in LiteLLM-adjacent tooling. Keep it structured (regex list as data file, versioned) per no-prose-grepping-for-ENFORCEMENT rule — this is output cleanup, not gating, which is fine. (2) MEMORY-PATTERN absorption: mine MemoryBooks (scene->structured entry), CharMemory (structured extraction->vector retrieval at generation), VectFox (event-extraction from filler: ~5 events per 100 sentences), LoreVault (summarize+search service) for the 8sf director state AND general agent-memory design (bd memories / context-handoff / polylogue-informed hermes memory seed in sinnix-z7v) — the specific steal: event-extraction before storage beats raw-log RAG, and keyword-triggered depth injection beats always-in-context.
notes: 2026-08-11 derived-data doctrine (operator asked for depth; applies to agent memory, 8sf state, lake, and is effectively sinex semantic-lane design language): TAXONOMY of derivations worth computing over raw — (1) EVENTS: {actor,action,object,time,salience} extracted from verbose streams; retrieval-sized, dedupable, timelineable — embedding whole replies averages filler into the vector, events fix the SNR at write time. (2) STATE REDUCTIONS: fold events into state-as-of-T with validity intervals (bitemporal: event-time vs record-time) — Tracker/ops-reducer pattern generalized. (3) HIERARCHICAL SUMMARIES: scene->chapter->arc / session->day->week, each linking back to raw; periodic re-derivation from raw to stop summary-of-summary drift. (4) CLAIMS with provenance: {claim, source-spans, confidence, ts} — deep-research verification shape doubling as personal-KG substrate. (5) UNIT-GRANULARITY EMBEDDINGS: proposition/event-level not doc-level (Dense-X 'propositions' finding), matryoshka-tiered, with deriver-version stamped for re-embedding policy. (6) SALIENCE SCORING at extraction + retrieval weighting recency x importance x relevance (Stanford generative-agents memory — the canonical design for 8sf). (7) ENTITY REGISTRIES: cross-source identity (speaker/face/username->person) enabling joins. (8) SUPERSESSION LINKS: new fact invalidates old via validity intervals — memory that updates, not accumulates. (9) STATISTICAL AGGREGATES: baselines/rhythms/changepoints (h8k). (10) RETRIEVAL REWRITES: QA-pair/question-form derivations of memories. DOCTRINES: re-derivability is the test (can't re-derive from raw => it's capture, not derivation); stamp every derivation with deriver model+prompt version; lazy-derive expensive tiers; raw remains sacred per lake rules.
close_reason: sinnix-deslop built and verified: regex-based slop-phrase stripper, versioned phrases.txt data file (not code), filter lib + CLI, 8 tests passing, verified via a real nix build (pkgs/sinnix-deslop, registered in flake/scripts.nix + public flake/packages.nix). Commit 5b26530 (+cleanup 4b3bc1e). Memory-pattern absorption (item 2 of this bead: MemoryBooks/CharMemory/VectFox/LoreVault mining for director-state and general agent-memory design) NOT done in this pass -- that's a design-research task distinct from this shipped code artifact, splitting it out.

title: RP-community knowledge harvest: samplers, finetune scene, context-engineering practice, frontend evaluation
description: Recon 2026-08-11: the ERP/RP community is the deepest empirical source on local-model behavior; harvest targets: (1) SAMPLERS the community INVENTED, now upstream in llama.cpp — DRY (p-e-w 2024, exponential multi-token repeat penalty; superior to rep-pen) and XTC (excludes TOP tokens above threshold with probability p — anti-slop creativity sampler) — enable/tune on our llama-server + ollama lanes; community baseline: temp 1.0, min-p 0.05, DRY mult 0.8, XTC thr 0.1, rep-pen OFF. (2) FINETUNE SCENE as model source (TheDrummer/Sao10K/anthracite-Magnum/EVA lineages; historical: Stheno/Lumimaid/Noromaid) — community consensus: purpose-finetunes BEAT abliteration for output quality (abliteration = OAS, which this community pioneered); harvest current per-VRAM-tier picks from r/SillyTavernAI weekly megathreads (search engines don't index them well — read directly); relevant to 8sf director-actor voices and base-model play. (3) CONTEXT-ENGINEERING PRACTICE predating the industry term: character card V2 spec, lorebooks/World Info (keyword-triggered depth-injection), author's-note positioning, summarize-and-pin — directly informs the 8sf director harness prompt architecture. (4) SillyTavern itself (v1.13, native DRY/XTC) — evaluate as the interaction frontend for director/sampler/loom work vs bespoke; it already speaks OpenAI-compatible = LiteLLM lanes. (5) KOBOLDCPP ROLE FOUND: it is this community's server of choice — its continued place in the estate now has a purpose (RP-tuned sampler surface); revisit the three-engine redundancy verdict accordingly.
notes: 2026-08-11 ERP-meta recon round 2: CURRENT META — API side: DeepSeek V4 (esp. V4 Flash, 284B/13B-active MoE, 1M ctx) and GLM 5.2 are the community-favorite backends (state-tracking + branching-consequence quality at budget prices); Kimi lineage similar class. Local side: Gemma 4 31B cited as budget-local pick (dense — too big for our VRAM; our gemma-4-abliterated 12b/26b-MoE grabs are the right-sized equivalents); new quant formats IQ4_XS / GGUF-V3 noted for reduced small-GPU intelligence collapse — prefer for our pulls. TECHNIQUES: slop-regex post-processing (ST Response Processing auto-strips GPT-ism phrase lists) — trivially portable to any harness incl. yt-polisher/agents; MEMORY EXTENSION ECOSYSTEM is the surprise treasure: Data Bank (built-in RAG) + MemoryBooks (scenes->lorebook entries) + CharMemory (structured memory extraction->vector retrieval) + VectFox (event-extraction: 5 meaningful events from 100-sentence replies) + LoreVault (memory-as-a-service w/ summarization+semantic search) — this is battle-tested long-term-memory engineering directly transplantable to the 8sf director harness and agent memory generally. NOT-YET-THOUGHT-OF items now recorded: (1) VOICE-ERP loop = the mke E2E stack composes with all of this (ASR->model->emotion-TTS; barge-in incl.) — nobody in the community has the full local voice loop we designed; (2) expression sprites via local image gen (Chroma/SDXL packs) — ST supports sprite sets, ties image tier; (3) creative-writing BENCHMARKS as objective-ish signal: EQ-Bench creative-writing-bench class for evaluating our model grabs beyond vibes; (4) adventure-mode engines (KoboldAI Lite) as the structured-RPG cousin; (5) character-card tooling: VLM-generated cards (from images via qwen3-vl-abliterated) as a generator; (6) privacy split doctrine: ERP is the maximally-private workload — local-first by default, API (DeepSeek-class) only with eyes open.

title: Lynchpin advanced-modeling menu: what the substrate doesn't yet do
description: From 2026-08-11 session (models grabbed in sinnix-w9l; this bead = the analysis programs, lynchpin-repo work mostly): (1) TSFM forecasting layer (Chronos/TimesFM/Moirai) incl. wear-SLO runway with quantile bands; honest positioning vs LLMs: TSFMs win per-FLOP numeric accuracy, frontier LLMs win covariate/regime REASONING (can read 'installed X on date Y' from the journal) — the right design is TSFM baseline + LLM regime-annotation, not either alone. (2) Matrix-profile motif/anomaly discovery (stumpy) over telemetry — finds repeated patterns + discords with zero training. (3) Change-point detection (ruptures) — segment personal history into regimes; align detected changepoints against journal/commit/bead events = auto-annotated life-eras. (4) Sequence/routine mining (PrefixSpan-class) over app/window/command event streams — discover actual routines vs believed ones. (5) Causal-inference attempts (DoWhy/synthetic-control) on the classic personal questions (sleep->productivity etc.) with honest confounder caveats. (6) Personal knowledge-graph extraction across notes/chats/captures (entities+relations; NOTE sinevec GraphRAG experiments exist in _inactive — resurrect-or-supersede decision per complete-over-delete rule). (7) HMM/state-segmentation over multimodal capture days. (8) Embedding-everything semantic layer across ALL personal text (unify polylogue/knowledgebase/captures search).
notes:
2026-08-11 web-recon — SEMANTIC-LAYER/MEMORY prior art (evaluate before building item 8's store): agent-memory frameworks matured into a real category: Graphiti/Zep (TEMPORAL knowledge graph — bitemporal edges align exactly with the uou derived-data doctrine's bitemporal state-reductions), cognee (graph+vector hybrid, ECL pipeline, 14 retrieval modes, self-hostable), mem0 (three-tier user/session/agent scopes), Letta (MemGPT lineage, agent-managed memory tiers — framework not layer). None are lake-native; the likely pattern is stealing Graphiti's temporal-edge schema + cognee's graph+vector split over OUR duckdb/parquet substrate rather than adopting a framework. Also Khoj (self-hosted 'second brain': RAG over notes + custom agents + scheduled automations + deep research) — closest packaged analogue to the estate's ambitions; evaluate its UX patterns (Obsidian/editor integration, automation scheduling), not its storage. Vector-store shortlist for item 8 unchanged by search outage: LanceDB (columnar, file-based — /realm-friendly), sqlite-vec (embeds in existing sqlite products), usearch (library-grade), qdrant (server-grade).
2026-08-11 positioning vs Polylogue (operator ask): NOT competitors — different layers. Polylogue is the RAW ARCHIVAL SUBSTRATE for AI-session history (append-only ingestion of Claude/Codex/ChatGPT sessions, markdown+sqlite, search over what was SAID). Memory frameworks (Graphiti/Zep, cognee, mem0, Letta) are OPERATIONAL memory: derived, mutable, retrieval-optimized state consulted at inference time (entities, facts, temporal edges, supersession). The estate's correct shape: polylogue+lake stay the immutable evidence plane; a DERIVED temporal-KG layer (Graphiti's bitemporal edge schema: valid-from/valid-to + ingested-at — matches the uou doctrine's bitemporal state-reductions and supersession-links classes) is materialized FROM polylogue/lynchpin/captures by lynchpin jobs, re-derivable and versioned; agents query the derived layer, cite back to raw. Adopting Letta/mem0 wholesale would create a second, non-lake-native store of truth — rejected. Khoj: overlapping UX (RAG over notes, agents, scheduled automations, editor integrations) but storage-opinionated; read for UX patterns only. Note bd's own 'bd remember' + beads memories already cover the small-scale agent-memory slot for tracker-adjacent facts.
2026-08-11 operator correction ACCEPTED: bitemporality is already estate doctrine, not a Graphiti import — sinex models occurrence-time vs recorded/ingest-time on events (the replay-later doctrine depends on it), and polylogue distinguishes session-time vs ingestion analogously. Graphiti's only delta is applying that discipline at the DERIVED-FACT level (per-edge valid_from/valid_to/invalidated_at on knowledge-graph edges). Design rule: the derived temporal-KG layer adopts SINEX's existing time-field naming/conventions so one bitemporal vocabulary spans raw events and derived facts; Graphiti is a schema reference only.
